MANILA, Philippines – How is power built? Who enables it? What happens when you follow the money? And more importantly, how can citizens turn leads and tips into concrete actions that hold public officials accountable?
On September 11, Rappler+ members are invited to an exclusive briefing, “From Information to Action: The Romualdez Trail,” at the Rappler Civic Hub in Pasig City.
This briefing takes attendees beyond the headlines to examine the bigger picture surrounding former House speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez.
Romualdez has faced allegations linked to the flood control corruption scandal, the national budget, and more. But the story extends beyond any single case.

Rappler’s investigations have examined the broader network around Romualdez, from high-value properties and newly incorporated companies to people with business, professional, and personal ties to the former speaker. Rappler has previously reported on the expansion of Romualdez’s political and business influence (Read the investigative series: Romualdez associate, frat brother linked to another US property worth P425M)
At this briefing, we put the pieces together, for you.

Rappler lead editorial researcher Jodesz Gavilan and justice reporter Jairo Bolledo will walk members through the latest developments and Rappler’s body of reporting to understand: the cases, the properties, the people, and the connections.
Corruption watchdog groups will show how journalism and civil society can work together to hold public officials accountable.

More than a recap of the news, the briefing gives members a chance to ask questions directly, and examine how political and economic power is built and sustained, before opening a larger conversation, about what accountability can look like from here.

articles.title: Kenyan runners stamp class in Pru Life UK run
articles.summary: Kenyans Gilbert Muge and Pamela Bundotich flashed a potent combination of speed and endurance, weathering dark skies and intermittent drizzle to stamp their class in the centerpiece 30-km race of the…

blocks.text: Kenyans Gilbert Muge and Pamela Bundotich flashed a potent combination of speed and endurance, weathering dark skies and intermittent drizzle to stamp their class in the centerpiece 30-km race of the Pru Life UK POP (Promise of Protection) Run at the Ayala Triangle Gardens in Makati last Sunday, Aug. 30.

Muge and Bundotich wasted little time flexing the racing form honed through numerous international competitions, pulling away from a field of Filipino challengers and adding another pair of victories to their growing list of triumphs on local roads.
Muge, whose most recent victory on Philippine soil came in the Trilogy Run Asia 2026 in March, seized control early and never looked back, clocking 1:44:03 in the novel 30K distance.
James Cruz finished six minutes behind Muge in 1:50:44, while Aldrin Serrano clocked 2:01:31 for third.

The 30K race was one of five categories offered in the event, which sought to cater to runners across the spectrum – from beginners taking their first steps into the sport to seasoned athletes looking for a demanding new milestone.

The distance also carried special significance for Pru Life UK, which created the 30km race to mark its 30 years in the Philippines. Rather than simply adding another race category, the company positioned the 30 kilometers as a physical representation of its three decades of serving Filipino policyholders and communities.
Bundotich, a familiar presence in various regional marathon events in the country, likewise proved too strong for the local field, topping the women's 30km in 2:02:38.
Tricia Rufano came in second in 2:17:32, while Edna Magtubo was third in 2:26:02.
The other titles disputed were in the 3K, 5K, 10K and 21K categories, producing several close finishes in the race organized by Sunrise Events, Inc.
National athlete Jessa Mae Roda captured the women's 21K crown in 1:29:49, beating Nicole Diloy, who clocked 1:33:26. Fayelle Castro finished third in 2:01:43.
Roy Laudit, meanwhile, ruled the men's 21K in 1:16:03, turning back Ricky Organiza, who finished in 1:19:19. Kenyan Evans Bomer was a close third in 1:19:21.

Alfred Braza emerged on top in a tightly contested men's 10K, clocking 32:43 to beat Junel Gobotia (33:13) and Noli Torre (33:43), while Meljoy Gonzales took the women's 10K crown in 40:29, holding off Kenyan Purity Serem, who finished in 41:31. Angel Lumacang was third in 42:53.

The men's 5K produced one of the day's closest finishes, with Jevie Rebutazo edging Rahby Seno by just one second. Rebutazo clocked 16:21, while Seno settled for second in 16:22. Matthew Donnery was third in 17:08.
The women's 5K was likewise decided by a matter of seconds, with Kaye Villanueva timing 19:17 to beat Princess Amarante, who clocked 19:36. Nila Acampado finished third in 21:17.
Jerico Cadag and Marilou Caduyac completed the 3K sweep, winning the men's and women's divisions in 9:22 and 11:24, respectively.

Joe Ross Simangan was second in the men's 3K in 9:47, while Gian Clava placed third in 10:23. In the women's race, Yessamin Carbonilla clocked 12:17 for second, followed by Maria Lyn Balguma in 15:17.

articles.title: Monday briefing: Nepal and Tibet’s floods are a warning for the future
articles.summary:
In today’s newsletter: As rescuers search for survivors after catastrophic floods, the disaster offers a stark warning about the climate risks facing the region, and the world

Good morning.…

blocks.text: Good morning. Over the weekend, rescue workers in Nepal and Tibet raced to find people who are still trapped in villages affected by catastrophic flash floods. As of this morning, the death toll stands at 903, and more than 4,000 people are missing.

For those of you reading this in a place where life continues as usual, the scale of devastation is hard to fathom. In a matter of minutes, a torrent of mud and debris engulfed entire villages, snapped bridges and swept away people’s homes and families. Some survivors are marooned on top of buildings that rescue workers can’t reach. Others are trapped in tunnels beneath the ground. Many have no idea if their loved ones are still alive.

The floods exemplify a wider threat. The delicate processes that have shaped our climate for centuries are unwinding at a terrifying pace. Scientists are still investigating the precise sequence of events that caused these floods, but as the planet heats up and glaciers melt, events like this will keep happening.

The Guardian has been covering the floods extensively – you can read our visual guide to the disaster, and our latest report on it here. For this morning’s newsletter, I spoke to our south Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen, who is on the ground in Kathmandu. She’s been speaking to survivors and reporting on the rescue operation since Thursday. That’s after the headlines.
Weekend roundup

items: UK politics | PC Andrew Harper’s killers will remain in prison after Andy Burnham announced changes to the early release scheme that will see anyone convicted of unlawful killing, including all forms of manslaughter, excluded from the scheme.

Milo Yiannopoulos | Far-right British media provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the US back to the UK by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in connection with what the agency said was expired authorisation to be in the country.

US-Iran | Iran has launched retaliatory strikes on airbases in Jordan after the United States attacked Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the strait of Hormuz, the first such strikes in a month.
Iceland | In a blow to Brussels, Iceland has held a referendum that has narrowly ⁠rejected ⁠the government’s proposal ​to hold ⁠accession talks with ⁠the ​EU.

Nepal-Tibet disaster | A headteacher in Nepal evacuated 900 children from a school moments before a deadly wall of water struck their town amid the devastating flash floods that have killed almost 800 people and left thousands missing.

blocks.text: In depth: An ‘absolute catastrophe’

blocks.caption: ‘Everything was either submerged in mud, or mangled’  Photograph: cnsphoto/Reuters

blocks.text: At 8:37am on Wednesday morning, an enormous chunk of ice from a glacier in the Himalayas broke off and crashed on to a mountain near the border between Nepal and Tibet. It caused a fearsome avalanche of ice and rock, which surged downstream into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, submerging villages and sweeping roads away.

At first, the scale of damage was unclear. Nepal is prone to natural disasters, and many of the villages affected by these floods are extremely remote. Early satellite images of the region were obscured by thick clouds of dust, and scientists initially assumed that an earthquake must have caused the flood, rather than a glacier collapse. By Wednesday night, as more images and reports emerged, it became clear that the floods were an “absolute catastrophe,” Hannah says. On Thursday, she boarded a flight to Kathmandu, the capital city near the destruction.

When Hannah arrived in Bidur, a small city two hours from Kathmandu, on Friday morning, most of its buildings had been destroyed, their carcasses exposed like matchsticks. A team of rescue workers in yellow hard hats were working to clear the roads. “There was a bank, an ATM machine, and a truck that was lying on its side,” she says. “Everything else was either submerged in mud, or mangled.”
The race to save lives

The Nepali army has been organising the rescue operation from a military base in Bidur. Large sections of the road that links Bidur to villages higher in the valley have been washed away, so rescues are happening by air, and the sound of helicopters is nearly constant. Every two to three minutes, a chopper lands, deposits survivors, and sets off again. The mud is so thick in some places that helicopters have struggled to land. Rasuwa, an area where entire villages were destroyed, was still inaccessible when I spoke to Hannah on Sunday afternoon. “The ground zero of the floods has still not been reached by journalists, and is only just being reached by the army,” she says.

Hundreds, if not thousands, of people have been rescued, and hundreds of people are now waiting outside the army base in Bidur scanning lists of survivors posted on the walls. At hospitals in Kathmandu, health workers have put up photos of bodies that are so disfigured their families have struggled to identify them. Authorities have begun burying human remains because there isn’t enough mortuary space to prevent them from decomposing. “I’ve spoken to people who have up to 12 relatives who have gone missing,” says Hannah, who visited hospitals in Kathmandu on Saturday. “And there’s no phone signal in the more remote villages. So another big cause of suffering is this huge uncertainty.”
Thousands still missing

So far there are 4,247 people who are missing, according to Nepal’s disaster agency (592 of whom are foreigners, including 43 Australians, and 48 from the UK, including 15 reported missing in China). Among them are 933 workers from Nepal and neighbouring countries who were working on hydroelectric power projects along the river. These rely on vast tunnel systems that are built deep into the ground, and rescue teams have to dig through mud and bore through tunnel walls to extricate trapped workers. On Saturday, the Nepali army had a small breakthrough when it successfully inserted a pipe into a tunnel at a hydroelectric site in Trishuli, allowing air to be pumped into the tunnel. In the early hours this morning, rescue efforts were “intensified” at the site, with a team of 90 people deployed.

The army is racing against time to rescue the living. “People are stuck in areas that have no drinking water, or access to food. They’re completely cut off,” Hannah says. The picture of devastation has emerged more quickly in Nepal than in Tibet, where the Chinese government retains a tight grip on information. On Friday, as the official death toll in Nepal rose to 538 people, China estimated that just five people had died in Tibet. The Chinese authorities have since revised their numbers, and estimate that at least 16 people are dead and 546 missing.
The long road to recovery

It will take months to clear away the mud, and some people will never find their relatives’ bodies. Some were pushed so far down the river that they have washed up in India. “People have lost everything,” says Hannah. “I saw one woman clutching a bottle of cooking oil, because it’s the only thing she had left.” Climate stories in the global south often struggle to break through, so it’s encouraging that these floods have been covered so widely. But when the news cycle has moved on, Nepal will be left with the enormous task of rebuilding. It estimates that cost could be between $4bn to $5bn, almost a tenth of its economy.

“It’s getting increasingly difficult for Nepal to pick itself up,” Hannah tells me. In Kathmandu, buildings destroyed by the 2015 earthquake, which killed nearly 9,000 people, are still in ruins. The EU has committed €2m to Nepal to help with the floods, and Britain has committed £5m. There’s also been a lot of focus on the need for better early monitoring systems. All of this matters. But as Sunil Acharya, a climate policy specialist based in Kathmandu, wrote in this interesting Opinion column, it also obscures a more fundamental problem: systems to monitor these events were designed for yesterday’s risks, not today’s extremes. Nepal’s warning systems were destroyed before they could alert people near the source of the flood.

Looming over all this is the fact that nations like Nepal, which has contributed a minuscule amount to historic greenhouse gas emissions, will suffer the worst effects of the climate crisis. It needs far more assistance to cope with the consequences of richer nations’ actions. And it needs those nations to rapidly cut their emissions, before the crisis gets worse.
The week to come

items: Tuesday | Justice secretary Alex Norris is due to present the government’s revised plans for the prisoner early release scheme, which includes a headroom review aimed at freeing up more space in the system.
Thursday | In the first UK visit by an EU leader of Andy Burnham’s tenure, the prime minister is will host talks with French president Emmanuel Macron.

Saturday | Officials from Jamaica will visit the UK to lodge a petition with King Charles to seek legal guidance from the privy council on the country’s request for reparations over Britain’s involvement in the slave trade, on the anniversary of the 1781 Zong slave ship departure from West Africa.

The i Paper splashes “Harry should pay for security costs in UK, say two-thirds of public in poll”, the Express leads with “‘I fear Andrew’s staff won’t co-operate with police’”, and the FT has “Big Tech profits enjoy $160bn paper boost from stakes in other AI groups”. blocks.text: The Upside
A bit of good news to remind you that the world’s not all bad

blocks.caption: The number of people living with dementia around the world is forecast to nearly triple to 153 million by 2050. Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

blocks.text: Results from a 15-year study suggest that statins, the cholesterol-busting drugs, can lower the risk of dementia by 15%. In the largest study of its kind, researchers tracked more than 132,000 people in Denmark between 2006 and 2021. Those who started on statins during the study period were 10% less likely to develop dementia. Those taking them early reduced their risk by 15%. The results were similar in women and men. The number of people living with dementia globally is forecast to nearly triple to 153 million by 2050. But, experts believe almost half of dementia cases could be prevented or delayed.

articles.title: 5 datos na may kinalaman sa pag-ahon mo sa kahirapan
articles.summary: Magkakakabit na problema ang edukasyon, kahirapan, at hanapbuhay — at sa kaso ng Pilipinas, perpetuating cycle ito ng underdevelopment

blocks.text: Magkakakabit na problema ang edukasyon, kahirapan, at hanapbuhay — at sa kaso ng Pilipinas, perpetuating cycle ito ng underdevelopment

items: The Philippines has achieved a single-digit poverty rate of 9.7% in 2025, the lowest in history, but the Multidimensional Poverty Index indicates that 12.8% of the population remains multidimensionally poor.

Despite being classified as an upper-middle-income country with a GNI per capita of $4,850, significant income disparities exist across regions, with average incomes varying greatly between areas like Makati and Zamboanga.

The country faces a severe literacy crisis, with 88% of students unable to read at a Grade 7 level, which poses challenges for future employment and perpetuates a cycle of poverty and underdevelopment.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Nag-single-digit poverty rate na pala ang Pilipinas? Ayon sa datos ng Philippine Statistics Authority, 9.7% na lang and mahihirap na Pilipino noong 2025, ang pinakamababa sa kasaysayan. Katumbas nito ang 11.08 milyong Pilipino, mula sa 17.54 milyon noong 2023. ‘Yan ang statistic No. 1 natin.

blocks.caption: AnimatEd,Editorial, Poverty, Flooding, Money

blocks.text: Pero mismong bagong datos ng gobyerno ang nagsasabing baka hindi ito totoo kapag tiningnan sa lente ng edukasyon, pabahay at batayang serbisyo, kalusugan, at hanapbuhay. Ayon sa Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) — nasa double digit pa rin o 12.8% ang multidimensionally poor. ‘Yan ang statistic No. 2.
May tatlo pang datos na dapat ibangga riyan kapag tiningnan natin ang kahirapan sa Pilipinas.

Statistic No. 3, sa wakas classified na tayo na upper-middle income country, na may GNI [gross national income] per capita of $4,850 (mahigit-kumulang P291,000 sa palitang $1 = P60). At disclaimer ng mga economist, hindi ito ang be-all and end-all. Yugto lang daw ito sa development journey.
Ang GNI per capita kas ay isang average statistic. Hindi nito ipinapakita ang disparity o agwat sa kinikita ng mayaman at mahirap.

At karugtong niyan ang statistic No. 4, na nagsasabing malala pa rin ang income disparities across regions, ayon sa latest Family Income and Expenditure Survey (FIES) ng Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). Ibig sabihin, may Luzon-Mindanao divide pagdating sa income ng mga pamilyang Pilipino.
Halimbawa, habang nasa P796,990 ang average income sa Makati, sa Zamboanga’y kakarampot na P309,610.

Lumago raw ang income ng mga pamilyang Pilipino nang 16.5% mula 2023 hanggang 2025, pero lumobo rin ang spending na umabot sa 24.7%. Kaya hindi natin naramdamang may extra income tayo, dahil ubos lakas sa gastusin.

Ang average annual family income ng Pilipino ay P411,350 ayon sa FIES. Malaki sana, pero kapag tiningnan mo in dollars, $6,610 lamang ‘yan. For comparison sa pinakamayamang bansa sa Southeast Asia na Singapore, ang average annual household income nito ay approximately US$149,000 (P8,940,000) habang US$9,970 (P698,200) naman ang sa Vietnam, ang sinusundan ng Pilipinas sa listahan.
Sabi ng mga yumamang galing sa hirap, “hindi balakid sa tagumpay ang kahirapan.” We salute you, kayong lahat na nagsikap at nakaahon sa hirap.
Pero para sa karaniwang Pilipino, paano ka makaaahon sa hirap kung palyado ang educational system na kinalakhan mo?

At diyan pumapasok ang statistic No. 5: Ayon sa Final Report ng EDCOM 2, “severe” ang literacy crisis sa bansa, kung saan 88% ng mag-aaral ay hindi nakababasa sa Grade 7 level at 0.4% lamang ang proficient pag tapak ng Grade 12. (BASAHIN: 88% of students entering Grade 7 struggling to read at that level)

Ito ang krisis na nakaamba sa Pilipinas — sa kabila ng pag-angat ngayong 2026, masu-sustain ba ito? Kapag sumali na sa labor force ang mga kabataang mababa ang kalidad ng edukasyon, paano sila matatanggap kung wala sa kanila ang skills na hinahanap ng employers? At siyempre, mauuwi ‘yan sa paglala ng unemployment at underemployment. Saan tayo pupulutin bilang bansa?
Magkakakabit na problema ang edukasyon, kahirapan, at hanapbuhay — at sa kaso ng Pilipinas, perpetuating cycle ito ng underdevelopment.

Kung ipinanganak kang mahirap, dehado kang makaangat dahil wala kang access sa kalidad na edukasyon. Maaaring lugmok ka sa kultura ng kahirapang nagdudulot ng helplessness at inferiority complex. Malamang din, tingin mo sa politiko ay padrinong pagkukunan ng ayuda, hindi tagapagsulong ng opportunity equality.

At ‘yan ang cycle na kailangang maigpawan, upang magkaroon ng tunay na pagkakataon ang mahihirap na makaangat sa buhay. ‘Yan ang delubyong tila umaanod sa ating papalayo sa panaginip nating maginhawang buhay. – Rappler.com

articles.title: DepEd chief urges parents to help prevent school violence
articles.summary: Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Juan Edgardo “Sonny” Angara has urged parents and guardians to take an active role in preventing school violence by closely monitoring their children and…

blocks.text: (MB FILE PHOTO)

Department of Education (DepEd) Secretary Juan Edgardo “Sonny” Angara has urged parents and guardians to take an active role in preventing school violence by closely monitoring their children and maintaining regular communication with school authorities, saying learner protection must begin at home and extend beyond the classroom.

“Hindi natin kayang solusyunan ang karahasan sa mga paaralan kung sa loob lang ng classroom tayo kumikilos. Ang tahanan ang ating unang depensa (We cannot address violence in schools if we act only inside the classroom. The home is our first line of defense),” he said in a statement released on Monday, Aug. 31.
The DepEd chief encouraged families to talk to their children daily, listen to their concerns, and coordinate with teachers and school officials.

“Kausapin natin ang ating mga anak araw-araw, pakinggan natin ang kanilang mga pinagdaraanan, at makipag-ugnayan tayo sa kanilang mga guro at paaralan. Kailangan nating matutunang mapansin ang mga red flags at pagbabago sa kilos ng bata bago pa man umabot sa pananakit o bullying. Ipadama natin sa kanila na hindi sila nag-iisa (Let us talk to our children every day, listen to what they are going through, and coordinate with their teachers and schools. We must learn to recognize red flags and changes in a child’s behavior before these lead to violence or bullying. Let us make them feel that they are not alone),” he said.

blocks.caption: (MB FILE PHOTO)

blocks.text: To strengthen parents’ participation in learner protection, DepEd said it is expanding its Kaagapay Program under DepEd Memorandum No. 002, series of 2026, and integrating it with the Parent Effectiveness Service (PES) Program under Republic Act No. 11908.

The agency said the Kaagapay Program provides parent communities with practical tools through capacity-building sessions intended to help them identify warning signs, manage behavioral concerns, and coordinate directly with school Child Protection Committees and guidance personnel.
Also, DepEd said it is working with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to harmonize the PES modules with the Kaagapay Program.
The partnership seeks to facilitate the full-scale implementation of the programs and address factors linked to violence, including mental health struggles and online safety risks.

From July to November, the education department said it is also rolling out its program on Strengthening Collaboration of Parents and Teachers on Learner Protection in the Cordillera Administrative Region, National Capital Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, and Bicol Region.

The initiative uses session guides developed by the DepEd Bureau of Learner Support Services-Learner Rights and Protection Division in partnership with ChildFund Philippines, Stairway Foundation Inc., and Meta Philippines.

The training sessions cover online sexual abuse and exploitation of children, child sexual abuse and exploitation material, bullying and cyberbullying prevention, nihilistic violent extremism, parenting approaches, technology-based protective tools, and reporting and referral procedures.

Trained regional and division Learner Rights and Protection personnel and education program specialists in values education are expected to lead the training of facilitators at the division and school levels.

At the school level, DepEd said it is coordinating with Parent-Teacher Associations and School Governing Councils to incorporate parent education into existing learner protection measures and strengthen partnerships between homes and schools.

“Shared accountability ang pagprotekta sa ating mga mag-aaral. Sa pagtutulungan ng paaralan, magulang, at komunidad, masisiguro natin na ligtas, nababantayan, at may nagmamahal sa bawat batang Pilipino (Protecting our learners is a shared responsibility. Through the cooperation of schools, parents, and communities, we can ensure that every Filipino child is safe, protected, and loved),” Angara said.

articles.title: DigiPlus hires Teneo as strategic adviser amid global expansion plans
articles.summary: DigiPlus Interactive Corp., the country’s leading online gaming provider, has tapped global CEO advisory firm Teneo to help navigate domestic headwinds and drive its international expansion strategy.…

blocks.text: DigiPlus Interactive Corp., the country’s leading online gaming provider, has tapped global CEO advisory firm Teneo to help navigate domestic headwinds and drive its international expansion strategy.

In a statement on its website, DigiPlus said bringing Teneo on board as strategic advisor reinforces its commitment to accelerating growth, strengthening its domestic foothold, and expanding its global presence.
“The partnership comes at a pivotal stage in DigiPlus’ growth as the Company pursues opportunities beyond the Philippines,” DigiPlus said.

The gaming operator noted that “Teneo will provide global perspective and senior counsel to help DigiPlus navigate complex business environments, assess emerging opportunities and risks, and make well-informed strategic decisions.”

The collaboration underpins DigiPlus’ transition from a local market leader into a broader digital entertainment player. It also complements ongoing investments in innovation, responsible gaming, corporate governance, and operational capabilities—laying a stronger foundation for sustainable growth both locally and abroad.

Leveraging its global team and network of senior advisors, Teneo delivers specialized services across five core business segments—offered independently or as an integrated service—to help clients address complex corporate challenges. Its global clientele includes a substantial roster of Fortune 100 and FTSE 100 companies, alongside major financial institutions and global enterprises.
Abacus Securities Corporation noted that the advisory deal follows recent updates on DigiPlus’ ventures in Brazil and South Africa, as well as a license application in New Zealand.
“The slow reception from its Brazil launch did not appear to stop PLUS from maintaining its strategy for its international expansion,” the brokerage said.
However, Abacus pointed out that during a recent briefing, “management refrained from providing more clarity on the timing and strategies for its re-launch in Brazil and South Africa.”

While noting it will take time to determine if hiring Teneo will yield tangible results, the brokerage emphasized that the move “shows the certainty of its plans to boost its international expansion.”

articles.title: Calabarzon measles-rubella vax drive crosses halfway mark
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The measles-rubella vaccination campaign in Calabarzon has surpassed the 50-percent mark of its target population, the Department of Health regional office reported. Agency data showed…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The measles-rubella vaccination campaign in Calabarzon has surpassed the 50-percent mark of its target population, the Department of Health regional office reported.
Agency data showed that 690,417 children, or 51.7 percent of the target population, had received measles-rubella (MR) vaccines as of 10 p.m. Friday, Aug. 28.
The DOH is targeting 1,335,685 children aged 6 to 59 months across Calabarzon under the Ligtas Tigdas 2026 immunization drive.
Meanwhile, 609,176 children had received Vitamin A supplementation, equivalent to 42.4 percent of the region’s target population of 1,436,443.

“We have made significant progress, but we still have a long way to go because our target is to vaccinate 1.3 million children,” said Dr. Rosa Maria Balisnomo-Rempillo, assistant regional director of the DOH in Calabarzon.
The campaign has been extended until Sept. 4 to make up for the heavy rains in recent weeks brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon.
The campaign was originally scheduled to end on Aug. 28.
The DOH reiterated that the MR vaccine is free of charge and that parents do not have to pay any fees.
Balisnomo-Rempillo said vaccination services have also been brought closer to communities, with health workers administering vaccines in barangays where the target children live.
She added that partner private clinics are also providing the MR vaccine free of charge to children aged 6 to 59 months under the campaign.
Balisnomo-Rempillo acknowledged that parents may have concerns about having their children vaccinated.
“There are normal reactions to vaccines, but the Measles-Rubella Vaccine we are administering now has been used in the Philippines for the last 50 years,” she said. /mcm

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 903, missing 4,247 – disaster authority
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Devastating floods near the border with China have killed at least 903 people in Nepal, while the number of missing in the country has soared to 4,247, its disaster authority said…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Devastating floods near the border with China have killed at least 903 people in Nepal, while the number of missing in the country has soared to 4,247, its disaster authority said Monday, as rescue efforts entered a sixth day.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 dead and 546 people missing in Tibet following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the overall toll to 919 dead and 4,793 missing.
Nepal’s list of the missing includes 592 foreigners.
It also includes 933 workers on hydropower projects along the river which the torrent crashed through, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
Nepal’s disaster agency listed 3,655 missing citizens in its update on Monday morning.
That includes Nuwakot district, where the missing rose sharply to 1,158, up from 115 reported on Sunday, as well as a further 562 unaccounted for in Rasuwa district.
The missing includes 45 Nepali army soldiers, 38 police and armed police officers, and 19 customs and immigration officers.
In India, authorities in Uttar Pradesh state said they had recovered 17 bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Indian authorities are seeking to identify the bodies, and they are not included in the toll. /dl

articles.title: US: Deadly flash flood hits Grand Canyon
articles.summary: Arizona's Grand Canyon received rainfall of up to 1 inch triggering a flash flood which forced more than 60 people to evacuate. At least one person has died, with over a dozen missing.

image.caption: The flooding destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek, and swept boulders and debris into the Colorado RiverImage: Parth Desai/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: At least one person died and 15 others are assumed to be missing after a flash flood hit Arizona's Grand Canyon National Park, authorities said on Sunday.

According to the National Park Service, the body of a 46-year-old man was recovered Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River. The flash flood also forced the evacuation of more than 60 people.
Rainfall on the Kaibab Plateau caused the flash flood at about 2:30 pm on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area, according to park services.
People rescued by helicopter
Parth Desai was hiking in Bright Angel Canyon with a group when the rain started.
"We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere, boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere," he told the Associated Press.
Making their way toward Phantom Ranch, the group saw a 4-foot (1-meter) debris wall headed toward them, forcing them to run up into a patch of cacti, he said.
They were finally rescued by helicopter.

blocks.caption: The Grand Canyon National Park Service is working with Arizona authorities to evacuate people and account for the missingImage: J. Thompson/National Park Service/AFP

blocks.text: What caused the flash flood?
The National Weather Service said up to 1 inch (2.5 cm) of rain fell in about 20 minutes in the area, with much of it running down the steep terrain.
The natural phenomenon destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek, and swept boulders and debris into the Colorado River.
Water restrictions were prompted after the flooding damaged the park's sole water pipeline.
More thunderstorms and heavy rain are expected into Monday.

blocks.caption: Rainfall on the Kaibab Plateau caused the flash flood at about 2:30 pm on SaturdayImage: Craig Sanderson/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The park will remain open for day use. The Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab Trail were closed on Sunday.
Overnight stays at lodges and hotels inside the park will be suspended from Monday. Colorado River rafting trips have also been halted.

articles.title: AUB approves ₱72-billion capital expansion to fuel digital payments push
articles.summary: Asia United Bank Corp. secured shareholder approval to nearly quintuple its authorized capital stock to ₱72.5 billion, laying the groundwork for broader push into digital payments and expanded…

blocks.text: Asia United Bank Corp. secured shareholder approval to nearly quintuple its authorized capital stock to ₱72.5 billion, laying the groundwork for broader push into digital payments and expanded lending operations
During a Special Stockholders’ Meeting held Aug. 28, 2026, AUB reported that investors voted to amend the lender’s articles of incorporation, raising the capital threshold from ₱14.7 billion.
The expansion, however, remains subject to regulatory clearance.

Shareholders also cleared a 100 percent stock dividend. The distribution will satisfy the 25 percent subscription and paid-up capital requirement required to execute the capital stock increase, the bank said. Official record and payment dates will be fixed after regulators sign off on the plan.
The capital injection is designed to give the mid-sized lender the financial leeway to scale up its commercial and consumer lending portfolios while deepening its footprint in financial technology.
AUB has been building out its digital ecosystem, concentrating on its core e-wallet infrastructure and cross-border payment platforms.

“The approval of our capital expansion marks a pivotal moment for AUB,” Abraham T. Co, AUB chairman, said. “Supported by our strong financial results, low cost of funds, and robust asset quality, we are laying the groundwork for sustained, long-term profitability.”
Manuel A. Gomez, AUB chief executive officer, meanwhile, pointed to changing market conditions as the primary driver behind the aggressive digital push.

“As financial landscapes rapidly evolve, we are doubling down on expanding our digital ecosystem by embedding cutting-edge technology into every facet of our operations,” Gomez said, adding that the goal is to secure new growth corridors and sustain technology-led profit momentum.

The capital expansion follows strong earnings performance through the first half of 2026. AUB recorded a net income of ₱6.19 billion for the six-month period, underpinned by double-digit growth across its core banking activities.

Total operating income climbed 10 percent year-on-year to ₱12.32 billion, fueled by a 14.9 percent gain in net interest income to ₱10.11 billion. Total loans and receivables expanded 10 percent to ₱281 billion over the same period. (James A. Loyola)

articles.title: Level 5 heavy rain warnings briefly issued for 3 Fukui cities
articles.summary: TOKYO, Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- The Japan Meteorological Agency issued Level 5 emergency rain warnings for the cities of Fukui, Ono and Katsuyama in the central Japan prefecture of Fukui on Sunday,…

blocks.text: A car submerged in water in a residential area due to heavy rain in the city of Sakai, Fukui Prefecture, on Sunday, Aug. 30.

TOKYO, Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- The Japan Meteorological Agency issued Level 5 emergency rain warnings for the cities of Fukui, Ono and Katsuyama in the central Japan prefecture of Fukui on Sunday, but later downgraded them.
Level 5 is the highest on the agency's disaster alert scale. After the warnings were issued at 4:30 a.m., the three cities urged residents to take immediate action to protect their lives.
The rain weakened later in the morning, and at 11:40 a.m. the agency downgraded the warnings to Level 4, before later lowering them further.

The 24-hour rainfall reached 350.5 millimeters in Katsuyama through 9:10 a.m., 318 millimeters in the Miyama area of the city of Fukui through 11 a.m. and 281 millimeters in Ono through 11:20 a.m., all setting new record highs since observations began.
A road flooded due to heavy rain in the city of Fukui on Sunday, Aug. 30.
Areas that received particularly heavy rainfall may face an increased risk of landslides due to loosened ground conditions.

According to the Fukui prefectural government, many rivers overflowed, and flooding damage was confirmed at 16 homes in three cities and one town, including Ono and Katsuyama. A landslide occurred in the city of Fukui, while a sinkhole opened up on a road in the city of Sakai in the same prefecture. A woman in her 30s suffered a broken leg on a flooded road in the city.
As of 10:30 a.m., prefectural police had received 106 reports involving stranded vehicles, flooding and other incidents.

blocks.caption: A river swollen due to heavy rain in the city of Fukui on Sunday, Aug. 30.

blocks.text: A river swollen due to heavy rain in the city of Fukui on Sunday, Aug. 30.

At a predawn press conference, Takuya Hosomi, director of the meteorological agency's Forecast Division, explained that a weather front extending from the Sea of Japan toward Fukui Prefecture had been fed by warm, moist air flowing northward around the edge of a high-pressure system over the Pacific Ocean, causing thunderclouds to develop.

Hosomi noted that the situation was similar to the one that prompted Level 5 emergency rain warnings in five municipalities in Toyama and Ishikawa prefectures in central Japan on Thursday. However, he emphasized that, rather than extremely intense downpours occurring within a short period, very heavy rain of 50 to 60 millimeters per hour continued intermittently for a long time from Saturday night.

articles.title: Old Australian courthouse finds new life as Nihon University facility
articles.summary: NEWCASTLE, Australia (Jiji Press) -- A 134-year-old former courthouse in Newcastle, Australia, is now a facility of Japan's Nihon University, with its preserved courtrooms offering students a…

blocks.text: A former courthouse repurposed as a Nihon University facility is seen in Newcastle, eastern Australia, on Thursday.

NEWCASTLE, Australia (Jiji Press) -- A 134-year-old former courthouse in Newcastle, Australia, is now a facility of Japan's Nihon University, with its preserved courtrooms offering students a hands-on lesson in the justice system.

Completed in 1892, the former Newcastle Courthouse, distinguished by an arched entrance, is listed as a New South Wales cultural heritage site. After the court moved to a new building in 2016, Nihon University purchased the property and had it restored.
The university has used the former courthouse since 2024, along with classrooms and lodging facilities built on either side.

Courtrooms of different sizes, holding cells as well as rooms where defendants met their lawyers, remain in their original configurations. The defendant's dock in the former Grand Courtroom is enclosed by a wooden railing, with a dedicated staircase connecting it to the cell directly below.
Students taking part in a study program in Australia in late August held a mock trial in the former Grand Courtroom.

blocks.caption: Nihon University students pose at the judges' bench inside a former courthouse in Newcastle, eastern Australia, Thursday.

blocks.text: Nihon University students pose at the judges' bench inside a former courthouse in Newcastle, eastern Australia, Thursday.
The smaller courtroom was named the Yamada Room after Akiyoshi Yamada, a former Japanese justice minister and founder of Nihon University's predecessor, Nihon Law School, which was founded in 1889.
The university and the former courthouse date back to roughly the same period.
"Preserving the site's historical value is meaningful," Takenari Shiba of Nihon University's office for internationalization promotion said. "We hope it will help students learn from the past."
Haruhisa Ikenaga, a second-year student of the university's College of Law, said, "The courtroom felt authentic, and I gained a vivid sense of how it differed from Japan."

Hana Harada, a second-year student of the university's College of Humanities and Sciences, said: "I saw cells for the first time. Scars on the walls prompted me to imagine the emotions of people who had been incarcerated there."

articles.title: MGB warns of possible landslides, flooding in over 3,000 Luzon barangays
articles.summary: More than 3,000 barangays nationwide are susceptible to rain-induced landslides and flooding due to Tropical Depression Pilandok and the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), the Department of Environment and…

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 1:09pm

More than 3,000 barangays nationwide are susceptible to rain-induced landslides and flooding due to Tropical Depression Pilandok and the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), the Department of Environment and Natural Resources' Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB) said.
According to the MGB, 3,786 barangays are susceptible to geohazards from August 30 to September 2 based on rainfall forecasts from the state weather bureau PAGASA.
As of 8 p.m. Sunday, August 30, most of the 3,786 landslide- and flood-prone barangays were in Luzon:

items: Ilocos Region — 2,235
Central Luzon — 718
Cordillera Administrative Region — 617
Cagayan Valley — 107
MIMAROPA — 87
CALABARZON — 22

blocks.text: "Based on the latest DOST-PAGASA 72-hour rainfall forecast, residents in listed areas and those nearby or downstream are urged to remain vigilant and take necessary precautions," the MGB said.
The MGB said geohazard susceptibility maps are produced based on local geology, landforms and terrain, as well as human activities that could increase disaster risks.

"The DENR-MGB barangay lists are generated using rainfall forecast data from PAGASA, rain-induced landslide and flooding susceptibility maps from DENR-MGB, and barangay boundaries from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA)," the bureau said.

"The rainfall forecast is applied to the hazard maps and barangay boundaries. Based on the established rainfall threshold, the barangays that may be affected by flooding or rain-induced landslides are identified and included in the DENR-MGB barangay lists," it added.
Tropical Depression Pilandok maintained its strength as it continued to meander over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, according to PAGASA.
Pilandok maintains strength over PH Sea, to intensify to tropical storm — PAGASA
Meanwhile, Habagat will continue to bring cloudy skies and monsoon rains over Luzon and the western section of the Visayas. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: BSP seen holding off on rate hike until 2027 as growth falters
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank AG expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to hold off on its next quarter-point interest rate increase until the first quarter of next year, as monetary authorities balance…

blocks.text: Deutsche Bank AG expects the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to hold off on its next quarter-point interest rate increase until the first quarter of next year, as monetary authorities balance sticky inflation expectations against sputtering economic recovery.

The Frankfurt-based bank’s forecast follows signals from monetary authorities that they are hesitant to tighten policy further immediately, choosing instead to prioritize economic growth following a series of domestic and external headwinds.

On Aug. 27, the policy-setting Monetary Board (MB) decided to raise the benchmark borrowing rate by 25 basis points (bps) to five percent a move BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr. described as a decision that “wasn’t so hard” even as all other options were considered.

According to the BSP, inflation could still flare up over coming periods given pressures expected from the looming El Niño and the potential implementation of a record-high ₱85 wage hike in Metro Manila. Such risks warranted “preemptive” policy action.

While a boon to price stability, further raising key borrowing costs could add stress to the country’s productivity. Domestic economic growth slumped to a post-pandemic low of 2.3 percent in the second quarter, bringing the first-half average to 2.6 percent.
Deutsche Bank believes further tightening remains on the table, citing the BSP’s elevated inflation assumptions for both 2026 and 2027.

However, the German lender expects the BSP to defer further tightening from October this year to February 2027: “We think the BSP would prefer to watch for potential changes in inflation expectations or second-round effects from earlier shocks before making its next move.”

Following its latest monetary policy meeting, the BSP now expects inflation to average 6.1 percent in 2026, down from its previous forecast of 6.4 percent. However, its inflation forecast for 2027 was raised to 5.4 percent from 4.5 percent.
Both updated assumptions remain well above the BSP’s two percent to four percent target range.

Headline inflation is expected to return near the three percent target by 2028. The revised outlook comes as inflation eased to 6.2 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June and a more-than-three-year high of 7.2 percent in April.
For August, Deutsche Bank believes inflation may have fallen further to 5.8 percent “on the back of favorable base effects in food prices.” If realized, August inflation would reach a four-month low.

Though forecasting higher figures than Deutsche Bank, Dutch financial giant ING and Singapore-based United Overseas Bank, Ltd. (UOB) also expect inflation to have softened to six percent on lower retail fuel prices.
“Core inflation pressures, though, should remain elevated, with food inflation continuing to pick up,” said Deepali Bhargava, ING regional head of research for Asia-Pacific.

articles.title: Embattled Sydney property developer Bathla warns it could fold by the end of the week
articles.summary:
Administrators said it would be forced to close the business if it failed to secure additional funding, revealing hundreds of staff have not been paid for weeks

The administrators of…

blocks.text: The administrators of embattled property developer Bathla Group have said the company will fold by the end of the week unless they can secure additional funding to keep it afloat.
The insolvency advisory Teneo assumed control of Bathla’s operations on 25 August after the Sydney-based construction company went into voluntary administration.
Thousands of customers have been left in the lurch, many of whom have partially built homes.
Teneo’s senior managing director, Stephen Longley, on Monday said some of Bathla’s 350 head office staff had not been paid for eight weeks.
“There’s no cash here. We don’t have any cash to pay wages. We don’t have any cash to pay suppliers,” he said.
“So, unless that situation can be resolved, we won’t have any option other than to close the business.”
Some staff had taken a “leap of faith” to keep working unpaid until the end of the week, in the hopes that an emergency financial backer could be found, Longley said.
He flagged potential redundancies should Bathla survive the week, with Teneo doing a review of its 350 staff “to work out which ones are mission critical”.

In a notice announcing its decision to go into administration, Bathla said Teneo’s immediate priority was to “stabilise” its operations and work with lenders to support employees and the continued delivery of projects.
Teneo said it was not in a position to refund deposits that hopeful homebuyers had paid to Bathla, which according to its website has 20,000 apartments and 7,000 dwellings in the pipeline.
Longley said the administrators would prioritise Bathla’s 45 projects that were already under construction, which were expected to result in between 2,000 and 2,500 new homes.
after newsletter promotion
Teneo was working to secure the backing of other lenders after the New South Wales government rejected its request for a financial lifeline.
Longley said Teneo would be able to provide an update on Bathla’s future after a meeting with the potential creditors on Friday.
“The lenders’ response has been good,” he said.
“It’s just something that’s come quickly and we need a lot of people to come together to put a solution together. I’m hopeful that in the next couple of days we’ll get there.”

articles.title: Color photos of occupied Japan face fading future
articles.summary: SENDAI, Miyagi Pref., Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- Color photographs of Japan under Allied occupation are vanishing more than 70 years after U.S. service members captured vivid scenes that may reveal…

blocks.text: The Tanabata festival in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, photographed on Aug. 6, 1949, by then-U.S. serviceman Norbert S. Lang (Courtesy of Fujio Chiba)

SENDAI, Miyagi Pref., Aug. 30 (Jiji Press) -- Color photographs of Japan under Allied occupation are vanishing more than 70 years after U.S. service members captured vivid scenes that may reveal forgotten fragments of history.
From 1945 to 1952, when Allied forces governed Japan after World War II, U.S. service members stationed in the country photographed postwar Japan on color film, which was still rare in the country.
Many of the photos are gradually being dispersed or lost over time, while some may contain historically significant scenes.
An exhibition featuring color photos taken by U.S. service members was held in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, northeastern Japan, in August.

The photos capture everyday scenes, including the area around a railway station, shopping streets and department stores decorated for the Tanabata festival, one of the three largest festivals in the Tohoku region of northeastern Japan, and Christmas. Their vivid colors are so striking that they look as though they were taken only recently with a digital camera.
The photos are believed to have been taken by a U.S. Army officer stationed in Sendai with a camera made by Germany's Leica Camera AG and Eastman Kodak Co.'s Kodachrome reversal film.

Fujio Chiba, 67, a senior official of a local history research association in Sendai, collected the photos on display. He searches for and acquires Japan-related photos and film through websites run by former U.S. military personnel and their relatives, photo-sharing sites and auctions.

blocks.caption: Fujio Chiba stands in front of panels of collected color photographs in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, on Aug. 5.

blocks.text: Fujio Chiba stands in front of panels of collected color photographs in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, on Aug. 5.
Chiba owns about 1,000 such photos, which show mainly cities where U.S. forces were stationed. Some vividly preserve places and objects that no longer exist.

One photo whose photographer and date are unknown shows a monument marking the hypocenter of the Aug. 9, 1945, atomic bombing of the southwestern city of Nagasaki, capturing a white wooden pillar bearing the black inscription "marker of the atomic bomb hypocenter" atop a rounded mound. It precedes the current triangular black-granite pillar.

Urakami Cathedral in the same city, which was heavily damaged by the atomic bombing, was rebuilt in 1959. A photo believed to have been taken in 1955 preserves a view of the cathedral's ruined state before reconstruction.

blocks.caption: Ruins of Urakami Cathedral, heavily damaged in the 1945 atomic bombing of Nagasaki, are seen in a photograph believed to have been taken in 1955. (Exact date and photographer unknown. Courtesy of Fujio Chiba)

blocks.text: Ruins of Urakami Cathedral, heavily damaged in the 1945 atomic bombing of Nagasaki, are seen in a photograph believed to have been taken in 1955. (Exact date and photographer unknown. Courtesy of Fujio Chiba)
Color film did not become widely available in Japan until after the 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games.
Long before then, however, U.S. service members had been recording through color film the unfamiliar landscapes they saw through their viewfinders.

Many of those service members have since died. Their children and grandchildren, who may have no particular attachment to the photos' subjects, sometimes leave the photos in cardboard boxes with other belongings or take them to antique shops as unwanted clutter.
Some of those photos may preserve historical records that Japanese people themselves never documented, prompting Chiba to continue collecting them.

blocks.caption: A marker identifying the hypocenter of the Nagasaki atomic bombing is seen in a photograph taken shortly after World War II. (Exact date and photographer unknown. Courtesy of Fujio Chiba)

blocks.text: A marker identifying the hypocenter of the Nagasaki atomic bombing is seen in a photograph taken shortly after World War II. (Exact date and photographer unknown. Courtesy of Fujio Chiba)
"Photos tucked away among someone's belongings may have no value to their current owners but could be immensely valuable to Japanese people," he said. "I don't want them to end up as mere garbage."

articles.title: Marcos has right to confidential funds as AFP commander in chief – Abante
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. could have confidential funds as the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Manila 6th District Rep. Bienvenido Abange…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. could have confidential funds as the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Manila 6th District Rep. Bienvenido Abange asserted on Monday.

Abante made the remark in response to Senate finance panel head Sen. JV Ejercito’s vow that confidential funds should be allocated only to security, intelligence and law enforcement government offices.
“We got to remember that the president is also the commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces. Therefore, he has all the right to have confidential fund,” Abante said in a press conference.
The House committee on appropriations is set to deliberate on the Office of the President’s P8.2 billion proposed budget for fiscal year 2027.
Abante maintained the need for transparency in the use of confidential funds.
“All we need to know is how it will be used, where it will be used,” he said.
“As commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces, as he is also the subject of threats, especially from the vice president. It is only necessary that the president has a confidential fund,” he explained.

House Deputy Speaker and La Union Rep. Paolo Ortega V echoed the sentiment, saying “It is important that if you have any funds donated. They must be used correctly, go to the right place, and follow the correct process.”

Confidential funds have been the subject of scrutiny, particularly as the budget deliberations coincide with Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, wherein she is accused of misappropriating such funds.
Duterte is also accused of betrayal of public trust for grave threats after making public pronouncements of reportedly threatening to kill Marcos. /apl

articles.title: Annual Pacific Islands summit: At least 5 leaders won’t attend
articles.summary: KOROR, Palau — At least five leaders will skip the Pacific Island region’s annual summit, officials said Monday, hours before the opening of talks overshadowed by Taiwan-China tensions.…

blocks.text: KOROR, Palau — At least five leaders will skip the Pacific Island region’s annual summit, officials said Monday, hours before the opening of talks overshadowed by Taiwan-China tensions.
The gathering aims to grapple with thorny regional issues including climate change, drug crime, and the Chinese test-firing of a ballistic missile that landed in the Pacific Ocean in July.
China’s security and economic influence has added resonance this year, because the 18-member Pacific Islands Forum is being hosted by Palau, a diplomatic ally of Taiwan.
Beijing has protested against Taiwan’s inclusion among aid partners invited to attend, along with China, Singapore, Japan, Britain and the United States.
China, which claims self-ruled Taiwan as part of its territory, also declared Palau an “unsafe” place for tourists.
The Pacific forum has been touted for decades as a symbol of regional unity.
“The Pacific is our home, not a theatre for geopolitical competition,” Palau President Surangel Whipps said in an interview on Sunday.
Tensions between the Pacific’s partners should not detract from island priorities on renewable energy, drug crime, food security and climate change, he urged.
But a growing number of leaders are skipping this year’s forum and sending lower-ranked ministers in their place.
Samoa’s government said in a statement its delegation would be led by the deputy prime minister.
The prime minister of Vanuatu and the head of government of the French territory of New Caledonia will also skip the summit, a forum official told journalists.
No confidence motion
Kiribati’s president has already said he will not be attending the talks.
Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale unexpectedly flew out of Palau on Sunday to deal with a political crisis at home after a no-confidence motion was lodged against his leadership.
Solomon Islands had been China’s closest partner in the Pacific until Wale was recently elected, vowing to review a secret security pact and repairing ties with the United States and Australia.
Fiji, a founding member of the forum, said its delegation to Palau would be led by the foreign minister but it was not known whether the prime minister might join at a later stage.
The leaders’ absence may weaken any joint Pacific statement on the Chinese missile test, said Oliver Nobetau, Pacific analyst at the Lowy Institute, a Sydney-based think tank.
“Not having these leaders there really lowers the expectation of whether or not we will see a strong statement come out of the Pacific Islands Forum,” he told AFP.
Some Pacific leaders were staying at home to tackle domestic political priorities, said Nobetau, director of the institute’s Pacific Islands programme.
But the leaders may also have decided that one-on-one discussions with external powers are more useful than forum negotiations in some areas.
“Some matters may be better dealt with in the realm of individual sovereignties, like when it comes to security, economic support, development support,” Nobetau said.
Around 110 police drawn from various Pacific islands will provide security at the forum, the first large-scale demonstration of Pacific-wide cooperation on policing.
Australia, the biggest forum member and aid donor, has led efforts for the Pacific to provide its own security, arguing there is no need for China to have police in Kiribati and the Solomons. /dl

articles.title: American wanted in US nabbed in Dumaguete City
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY, Philippines — A 45-year-old American wanted by United States authorities for a parole violation involving an underlying dangerous drugs charge has been arrested by the Bureau of…

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY, Philippines — A 45-year-old American wanted by United States authorities for a parole violation involving an underlying dangerous drugs charge has been arrested by the Bureau of Immigration (BI) in Dumaguete City, Negros Oriental.

The BI said on Saturday, Aug. 29, that its Fugitive Search Unit (FSU), working with US law enforcement agents, the Philippine National Police and local police and maritime authorities, apprehended Jason Michael Hill at Purok St. John in Barangay Calindagan on Aug. 11.

Hill was reportedly wanted in the United States for violating his parole, with an underlying dangerous drugs charge, based on an outstanding warrant issued by the Sacramento County Superior Court in California.
BI records showed that Hill entered the Philippines in March 2023 as a temporary visitor but had overstayed his authorized period of stay.
He was also the subject of existing BI derogatory records for being an undesirable alien and a fugitive from justice, the bureau said.
BI Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado said the arrest should serve as a warning to fugitives seeking refuge in the Philippines.
“Let this be a clear message to fugitives: The Philippines is not a safe haven for those escaping justice,” Viado said.

“If you come here to hide from the law, the BI will find you. We will work with our foreign law enforcement partners to locate you, arrest you, and ensure that you face the appropriate legal and immigration consequences,” he added.
Hill will remain in BI custody while undergoing immigration proceedings. /dl

articles.title: Pangasinan under state of calamity
articles.summary: CALASIAO, Pangasinan — Pangasinan has been placed under a state of calamity due to the combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, which caused…

blocks.text: CALASIAO, Pangasinan — Pangasinan has been placed under a state of calamity due to the combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, which caused substantial damage to infrastructure, agricultural crops, livestock, and communities across the province.

Pangasinan Vice Governor Mark Lambino said the Sangguniang Panlalawigan approved Provincial Resolution No. 985-2026 during an online session on Monday morning (August 31), declaring a state of calamity “to enable urgent response, mobilization of resources, and intensified humanitarian operations.”
Lambino said Governor Ramon Guico III endorsed the Sangguniang Panlalawigan’s action.

The weather disturbances brought torrential rains and widespread flooding, particularly in low-lying areas of Pangasinan, severely affecting communities, infrastructure, agriculture, private properties, and livelihoods

Reports from the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) showed that more than 370,000 families, or approximately 1.2 million individuals, have been affected by the successive weather disturbances.
The disasters also caused significant damage, with initial estimates placing losses to infrastructure at P232.5 million, agriculture at P649.23 million, and livestock at P2.11 million.
The state of calamity will put an automatic price freeze on basic necessities and prime commodities under Republic Act No. 7581, or the Price Act, and its implementing rules and regulations.

It will also allow the provincial government, municipalities, component cities, barangays, and concerned national government agencies to expedite relief, recovery, rehabilitation, and other humanitarian operations aimed at protecting the welfare of affected Pangasinan residents.

Eight local governments in Pangasinan had earlier declared their respective areas under a state of calamity. Authorities expect the number of affected families and the extent of damage to rise further as assessment and response operations continue. /dp

articles.title: NHS to offer free high-street cholesterol tests in England
articles.summary:
Checks at pharmacies for people aged 40 to 84 are aimed at identifying those at risk of heart attack or stroke

The NHS in England is to offer free finger-prick blood tests for cholesterol on…
articles.byline: Andrew Gregory Health editor in Munich

blocks.text: The NHS in England is to offer free finger-prick blood tests for cholesterol on the high street for the first time under plans to reduce heart disease and stroke deaths by a quarter within the next decade.
The seven-minute tests will be available at participating pharmacies as part of a national rollout to spot “ticking timebombs” earlier.
People aged 40 to 84 who are not pregnant and have not had a blood test in the past year will be eligible to walk in and get tested.

Blood will be taken from a person’s fingertip using a lancet – a small, sharp medical tool used to prick the skin – and analysed immediately. A pharmacist prescriber can then provide lifestyle advice and determine whether any treatment, such as statins, may be needed.
Patients will receive a copy of their results by email. They will also be offered a blood pressure check as part of a clinical consultation with a pharmacist prescriber.
Details of the scheme – the first of its kind globally – were announced during the European Society of Cardiology’s annual congress in Munich, the world’s largest heart conference.
David Webb, the chief pharmaceutical officer for England, said pharmacies could be a vital first line of defence against serious illness.

He said: “By making it easier for people to get a quick and convenient cholesterol health check on their local high street, we can spot ticking timebombs earlier, helping people take action, and prevent heart attacks and strokes before they happen.

“This is the latest in a series of initiatives involving pharmacies in delivering care previously only offered in GP surgeries as part of the 10-year health plan to bring care closer to where people live.”
The rollout follows a successful pilot in north London by Barts Health NHS trust in collaboration with UCLPartners and the cholesterol charity Heart UK, in which 2,493 patients had checks.

Nearly one in five patients (19%) were found to be at high risk of a heart attack or stroke within the next decade. These people were offered advice and referred for treatment. At least 88 people started taking statins as result.
In the first phase of the national rollout, about 100 NHS pharmacies across England will begin offering the checks from this autumn.

Dr Sotiris Antoniou, the clinical lead for the scheme at Barts Health, said: “By scaling this approach across England, we can support pharmacists to identify cardiovascular risk earlier and, importantly, act on the results through timely advice and treatment.
after newsletter promotion
“This has the potential to improve outcomes and reduce health inequalities, particularly in communities where the burden of cardiovascular disease is greatest.”

Dr Rani Khatib, NHS England’s national specialty adviser for cardiovascular disease prevention, said everyone should strive to be aware of the most common risk factors for heart disease, including high cholesterol and blood pressure, and “know their numbers”.
“This initiative will help people manage their risk factors earlier and reduce their risk of having heart attacks or strokes,” he said.

Alison McGovern, a health minister, said it was “exactly the type of innovation” she wanted to see across the NHS. “We’re making it easier for people to spot potential problems earlier and take action to protect their health,” she said.
“Early detection can help prevent serious conditions such as heart attacks and strokes, helping people stay healthier for longer while reducing pressure on NHS services.”

articles.title: PHILCONSTRUCT Mindanao 2026: Where Mindanao’s Construction Industry Meets
articles.summary: Mindanao is entering a period of continued development, with infrastructure, commercial, residential, and industrial projects reshaping communities across the region. With it comes a simple question…

blocks.text: Business
Brought to you by the Philippine Constructors Association (PCA)

Mindanao is entering a period of continued development, with infrastructure, commercial, residential, and industrial projects reshaping communities across the region. With it comes a simple question for the construction sector: how can the industry build better for what lies ahead?

From September 3–5, 2026, at the SMX Convention Davao at SM Lanang Premier, PHILCONSTRUCT Mindanao 2026 will bring the industry together for its 15th edition, guided by the theme "Smarter." Stronger. Sustainable.”

Brought to you by the Philippine Constructors Association (PCA), the exhibition will feature construction machinery, equipment, building materials, tools, technologies, and other solutions relevant to today’s projects.
The significance of an industry exhibition goes beyond the products showcased.

It is where builders learn not just where to find products, but how to evaluate and acquire them—empowering businesses with trusted suppliers and giving emerging technologies a place in the market. These encounters can influence how projects are planned, delivered, and maintained long after the exhibition ends.
For Mindanao, that matters.

The region’s development requires an industry capable of responding to diverse project demands, evolving technologies, resource constraints, and rising expectations. Having access to new products and ideas gives businesses more room to grow and make informed decisions.

PCA has long supported the development of the Philippine construction sector by creating platforms that bring its stakeholders together. PHILCONSTRUCT Mindanao continues that role by giving the regional market an avenue to see what is available, assess what is relevant, and engage with the people behind it.
The bigger picture goes beyond construction itself.

Every project eventually becomes part of everyday life—a road that connects people, a facility that supports an enterprise, a home for a family, or infrastructure that enables a community to function.
What the industry builds in Mindanao today becomes the foundation on which Filipinos thrive tomorrow. Better construction is more than a business goal—it is nation-building in action.
This September 3–5 at SMX Convention Center Davao, PHILCONSTRUCT Mindanao 2026 opens its doors to the people and businesses who answer that call.
Three days. One industry. A wider view of what Mindanao can build next.

articles.title: Welcome to the ‘United States of Makati,’ where family income is PH’s highest – and most unequal
articles.summary: Makati had the country’s highest average family income at P796,990 in 2025, but families in its top 10% earned nearly eight times as much as those in the bottom 10%

items: Makati, Philippines, is dubbed the 'United States of Makati' by office workers, reflecting its high average family income of P796,990, the highest among urban areas in the country.
Despite its wealth, Makati faces significant income inequality, with a Gini coefficient of 0.4569, indicating a stark contrast between the highest and lowest income families.

The city's economic activity is driven by a large number of businesses and offices, contributing to a GDP of P1.2 trillion in 2024, but many workers reside outside Makati, complicating the narrative of its affluence.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Have you been to the United States of Makati lately?

It’s where office workers have taken to calling themselves OFWs – whether that means “Onsite Filipino Workers” or, depending on the day, “Overworked Filipino Workers” – earning their keep in “Makati dollars.”

Even the Department of Tourism (DOT) joined in, pitching Makati as a “visa-free” destination for museums, malls, weekend markets, food trips, and runs around the Commercial Business District (CBD). One Ayala, a modern commercial-transport hub at the corner of EDSA and Ayala Avenue, even issued a weather update from the new republic.

But all jokes aside, Makati really does stand apart by the numbers. In the Philippine Statistics Authority’s (PSA) preliminary 2025 Family Income and Expenditure Survey, Makati posted an average annual family income of P796,990, or around P66,400 a month – that’s the highest among highly urbanized cities and higher than any province or region too.

Rappler mapped out just how high Makati’s average family income is compared to other cities in the Metro. The next map, meanwhile, reveals that while it’s the country’s richest city, it’s also the most unequal.
The nationwide average was P411,350, just over half Makati’s figure.
Makatizens also spent more. Average annual family expenditure reached P606,700, likewise the highest among Highly Urbanized Cities (HUCs).
Check out Rappler’s in-depth data visualization of which cities and provinces had the highest average family income in this article below.

blocks.caption: MAP: Where Filipino families earn the most and least

blocks.text: Even beyond household income, Makati is an economic anomaly.

The city generated P1.2 trillion in gross domestic product (GDP) in 2024. Its GDP per capita stood at a staggering P3.89 million, the highest among all provinces and HUCs and nearly 20 times the national P197,325. It’s also far ahead of second place Pasay.

However, note that Makati’s GDP per capita is partly inflated by the sheer amount of economic activity generated by offices and businesses whose workers may actually live elsewhere. Their output is counted in the city’s GDP, but they aren’t counted in Makati’s resident population. No wonder the CBD can sometimes feel less like a neighborhood and more like the headquarters of Philippine capitalism.

You see that in the office market statistics too. Even as Philippine office leasing slowed in the first half of 2026, Makati posted at least 106,000 square meters (sqm) worth of transactions – the most of any location tracked by Leechiu Property Consultants and ahead of Bonifacio Global City’s (BGC) 61,000 sqm.

blocks.caption: SUNNY. A quiet afternoon at the Legazpi Active Park’s Food Festival 2025. Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.

blocks.text: I can attest to that pull personally. When I worked as an analyst for a consultancy serving foreign-based funds, we were based in Makati even though, in theory, we could have worked almost anywhere. Makati simply felt like the obvious place to be.
It helps that Makati is one of the few places where getting lunch a couple blocks away is a welcome walk rather than an obstacle course of broken pavements and missing sidewalks.

Take, for example, the 1.1-kilometer elevated Dela Rosa Walkway, stretching from Makati Medical Center to Greenbelt. From there, pedestrians can continue through a series of malls toward MRT3 Ayala Station – a godsend for commuters, though they might still begrudge a certain development for breaking up that usual path.

blocks.caption: The Philippines is now upper-middle income. Really?

blocks.text: That walkability carries over into the rest of the CBD. Greenbelt and Glorietta sit within easy reach of offices, hotels, restaurants, and residential towers, while Salcedo and Legazpi Villages mix condos and cafés with small pockets of greenery.

blocks.caption: DRIZZLY. People stroll beneath the rain-dampened trees of Washington Sycip Park. Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.

blocks.text: If you’re an office worker stuck inside a cubicle for eight hours a day, those small pockets are enough to keep you sane. If you live in Makati, the parks become fixtures for community events too on weekends. Jaime Velasquez Park becomes the Salcedo Saturday Market; Legazpi has its Sunday market and two nearby parks. Ayala Triangle Gardens provides another patch of green in the middle of the office towers.

Ayala Avenue itself turns into exercise space on Sunday mornings, when a 2.3-kilometer stretch goes car-free for runners, cyclists, dog walkers, and families. The program started in 2023 and has since become a crowd favorite, drawing in visitors from all across the metro. Similar car-free initiatives have since spread around other cities, including Tomas Morato in Quezon City.

blocks.caption: KAPE! Coffee lovers hunt for their next caffeine fix at Kapecon 2025 along Paseo de Roxas. Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.

blocks.text: And if you’re looking for a night of lively drinking, then Poblacion’s only a few minutes’ walk away too.

It’s no wonder then that residential real estate prices are also sky-high. Two of Metro Manila’s most exclusive enclaves, Dasmariñas Village and Forbes Park, are technically Makatizen territory. In Leechiu’s Q4 2025 prime village data, Dasmariñas Village reached about P711,000 per sqm, up 7% year on year, while Forbes Park was at P648,000 per sqm, up 1%.
For comparison, other prime villages like Green Meadows was at P287,000 and Ayala Alabang at P233,000.
But don’t let the jokes about Makati obscure the painful reality that while there is fabulous wealth to be found in the city, there’s also intense inequality in how it’s distributed.
The average family income in Makati, P796,990, is just that – an average. It doesn’t describe every Makati family, far from it.

In fact, the same survey by the PSA shows Makati had the highest inequality among all major cities in the Philippines. It had a Gini coefficient of 0.4569 in 2025, considerably higher than the national Gini of 0.391 and National Capital Region’s (NCR) 0.3489. The closer that inequality measure gets to 1, the more unequal the distribution of income.
The detailed PSA tables show just how wide that gap can be.

Families in Makati’s bottom 10% had an average annual family income of P338,230, or roughly P28,200 a month. That’s below the P411,350 national family average and almost the same as the P337,970 average for families in Surigao del Norte.

At the other end, Makati families in the highest income decile averaged P2.66 million a year, or about P221,000 a month. That’s nearly eight times the family income of those in Makati’s lowest decile.

Even the amount left between income and spending looks radically different. The lowest income decile earned an average P338,230 and spent P314,930, a difference of only about P23,300 for the entire year.

For the highest decile, average income of P2.66 million compared with expenditure of P1.77 million, leaving a gap of nearly P889,000. Those differences shouldn’t automatically be treated as savings, but they do illustrate how much more financial room higher-income households have.

blocks.caption: HIGH ABOVE. Seen from the Zuellig Building, Makati’s skyline stretches across the CBD, where immense wealth sits alongside one of the country’s starkest income inequality. Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.

blocks.text: And Makati, that glittering little city of ambition, is expensive. A family earning P338,000 there and another earning roughly the same amount elsewhere may be living very different lives once housing, food, transport, and other costs enter the picture. – Rappler.com

blocks.caption: Filipino family income grew 16.5% since 2023. So why doesn’t it feel like it?
