articles.title: Mayor Wes clarifies use of Valenzuela vehicle seen at airport
articles.summary: Valenzuela City Mayor Weslie “Wes” Gatchalian clarified on Sunday, Aug. 30, that a city government vehicle seen at the airport was used to transport Baby Ayla and her mother ahead of the child’s…

blocks.text: Valenzuela City Mayor Weslie “Wes” Gatchalian clarified on Sunday, Aug. 30, that a city government vehicle seen at the airport was used to transport Baby Ayla and her mother ahead of the child’s liver transplant in India.
A photo posted on a Facebook group page showing the Valenzuela City government vehicle at the airport. (Photo courtesy of Mayor Wes Gatchalian)
The clarification came after a Facebook post questioned why a Valenzuela City vehicle marked “Strictly for Official Use Only” was seen at the airport.
Gatchalian said the passengers were Baby Ayla and her mother, who were being assisted by the city government for their trip abroad.
“Isang paglilinaw lang po, ang sakay ay si Baby Ayla at nanay niya (Just to clarify, the passengers were Baby Ayla and her mother),” he said.
Baby Ayla, a Valenzuela resident diagnosed with biliary atresia, left for India on Sunday for an urgent liver transplant.

blocks.caption: Baby Ayla with her parents and a CSWDO official at the airport departure area before their flight to India. (Photo from Valenzuela LGU)

blocks.text: Baby Ayla with her parents and a CSWDO official at the airport departure area before their flight to India. (Photo from Valenzuela LGU)

blocks.caption: Baby Ayla and her parents at the airport departure area before their flight to India. (Photo from Valenzuela LGU)

blocks.text: Baby Ayla and her parents at the airport departure area before their flight to India. (Photo from Valenzuela LGU)
The city government earlier provided financial assistance for the family’s airfare and hotel accommodation during the child’s operation and recovery in India.
The assistance was coordinated through the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO).
The city had also previously extended medical assistance to Baby Ayla’s family in October 2025, while the CSWDO continued monitoring the case in March 2026.

Doctors had recommended an urgent liver transplant. Although assistance through a foundation partner at the Chinese General Hospital was initially considered, the family later decided to have the procedure in India.
Gatchalian also reminded the public to verify information before sharing posts online.

“Huwag pong maging bahagi ng pagkalat ng fake news o maling impormasyon. Mag-verify muna bago mag-share (Please do not be part of spreading fake news or misinformation. Verify information first before sharing),” he said.
The city government also asked the public to pray for Baby Ayla’s safe journey, successful transplant, and recovery.

articles.title: Marcos Jr. on National Heroes Day: 'Do more than remember'
articles.summary: He says heroism also lives on in Filipinos who serve their communities.

blocks.text: President Bongbong Marcos leads Heroes' Day ceremonies at Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City on Monday, Aug. 31, 2026.
RTVM; Philstar.com screenshot, composite
MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called on Filipinos to honor the country's heroes not only by remembering their sacrifices but also by carrying their ideals forward.
In his National Heroes Day message Monday, August 31, Marcos urged the public to "do more than remember."
"Let us also renew our solemn duty to carry forward the nation for which they fought and sacrificed," Marcos said.

"Our forebears won our freedom, defended our dignity, and laid the foundations of the Republic we cherish. We honor them best by embodying their courage, keeping the flame of patriotism alive, and becoming the citizens our country needs," he added.
Marcos said the spirit of heroism also lives on in ordinary Filipinos who contribute to causes greater than themselves.

"We see it in our soldiers and first responders who risk their lives to keep us safe. We recognize it in our teachers, health workers, farmers, fisherfolk, and overseas Filipinos who sustain our families and communities. We find it in every citizen who helps a neighbor, protects the vulnerable, and works honestly for the common good," he said.
National Heroes Day is a regular holiday observed on the last Monday of August, which falls on August 31 this year.

articles.title: Families scour Nepal morgue for loved ones swept away by flood
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Raj Kumar Tamang of Bidur, Nuwakot, had fed his five-year-old son Prince and sent him to school in his uniform when he learned that the Trishuli river had flooded. Raj Kumar was…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Raj Kumar Tamang of Bidur, Nuwakot, had fed his five-year-old son Prince and sent him to school in his uniform when he learned that the Trishuli river had flooded.
Raj Kumar was safe, but Prince never returned home.
He searched desperately for his son. Then, while scrolling through photographs of recovered bodies published on the Nepal Police website, he spotted a child wearing a school tie.

The body had been taken to Pokhara Academy of Health Sciences. Raj Kumar travelled to Pokhara on Saturday and identified his son by his school tie, a necklace and an earring. The tie bore the name of Uttargaya Secondary School in Bidur, where Prince was an LKG student.

His body had been recovered on the banks of the Narayani river in Nawalparasi on Thursday, far downstream from the flood zone. Rajkumar collected his son’s body and returned to Bidur later on Saturday.

For Satya Krishna Prajapati of Bhaktapur, it was a tattoo that helped identify his elder brother, Satya Sundar Prajapati. He recognised the body from a tattoo on his brother’s shoulder and took the remains back to Kathmandu on Friday.
Satya Sundar had been working as a site engineer at the under-construction Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project in Rasuwa for the past year and a half.

Relatives of 45-year-old Narayan Thapa, a schoolteacher from Arghakhanchi who had been teaching at a community school in Betrawati, arrived in Pokhara on Friday after suspecting that a body recovered in Nawalparasi East was his.

A photograph released by Devchuli Police and a silver pendant worn around the man’s neck helped relatives identify the body. Thapa’s wife and other family members formally identified the body on Saturday and took it away.
Following the Bhotekoshi flood, 102 bodies recovered from Gorkha, Tanahun, Dhading and Nawalparasi East were brought to Pokhara. By Saturday, relatives had identified and claimed 10 of them.

More than 1,000 relatives of people missing in the Rasuwa flood arrived at Pokhara Academy of Health Sciences on Saturday alone to search for their loved ones, according to Deepak Rijal, acting spokesperson for Kaski Police.
Police have set up a help desk at the hospital.
Photographs and identifying details of the bodies are displayed in a hall at the academy, allowing relatives to search for missing family members.

“Where faces are no longer recognisable, relatives are identifying bodies through school ties, tattoos, necklaces and earrings,” Police Inspector Rijal said. “More relatives are continuing to arrive.”
The help desk provides assistance including free help with filing reports, free ambulances for transporting bodies and free food and accommodation for relatives searching for missing family members.
With support from the Hotel Association, police accommodated 47 people in Lakeside hotels on Friday and another 19 on Saturday, Rijal said.
Of the 102 bodies brought to Pokhara, 46 had undergone post-mortem examinations by Saturday.

Five forensic specialists, including three from Pokhara Academy of Health Sciences and one each from Manipal College of Medical Sciences and Gandaki Medical College, have been deployed for the examinations. They have been working from 9am to 6pm.
Two specialists from Nepal Police’s Central Forensic Science Laboratory arrived in Pokhara on Friday to collect DNA samples and analyse fingerprints.
Bodies to remain in Pokhara for several more days
The mortuary at Pokhara Academy of Health Sciences has 72 refrigerated compartments, but it is currently holding more bodies than its official capacity.
Authorities have managed the shortage by arranging the bodies carefully, including smaller bodies and dismembered remains.
A container was placed inside a cold room at the academy on Saturday, and authorities are preparing to transfer up to 25 bodies into it under controlled temperatures.

According to the academy’s information officer Sushil Aryal, the facility has one of Nepal’s largest and most modern mortuaries outside Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj. Bodies can be preserved at temperatures between 2 and 6 degrees Celsius for around 10 days to two weeks.
The process of handing over identified bodies to relatives is continuing.

For bodies that remain unidentified, authorities must follow the government’s 2021 directive on the management of unidentified and unclaimed bodies. Under the rules, a body management committee led by the district police chief is responsible for the process.
Photographs, fingerprints and DNA samples are collected and preserved before burial.

If a body remains unidentified for a prolonged period, it must be buried at a site designated by the local government. The burial site must be chosen so that no structure is built there for at least 12 years.
“We bury the bodies with tag numbers and geo-location records,” Rijal said. “If relatives come forward within 12 years, the remains can be exhumed and identified through DNA analysis.”
Kaski Chief District Officer Kuman Singh Gurung said Pokhara could continue storing the bodies for several more days.

“Relatives are arriving in Pokhara after checking bodies recovered in Chitwan and Nawalparasi,” he said. “The situation here is not like Chitwan, where an improvised mortuary led to a foul smell. We have refrigerated facilities here, so there will be no immediate problem.”

Authorities will wait for several more days before deciding whether to bury unidentified bodies, he said. The decision will be taken jointly by the District Security Committee and the body management committee. /dl

articles.title: Trump calls for ‘punishment’ of NBC reporter Kristen Welker
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Sunday threatened a prominent NBC broadcast journalist with possible punishment by US media regulators as the Republican expressed disappointment with…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Sunday threatened a prominent NBC broadcast journalist with possible punishment by US media regulators as the Republican expressed disappointment with coverage of his candidate endorsements ahead of November’s midterm elections.
Trump took to his Truth Social platform to attack Kristen Welker as the “unpopular ‘hostess’ of the once great Meet the Press” talk show.

He objected to her having said the president had had “mixed results” on his endorsement of political candidates in party primaries, insisting the races had gone his way 98 percent to 100 percent of the time.
Welker, speaking early Sunday to a local NBC affiliate, said Trump would “loom large over these midterms.”
When it came to endorsements, she added, he “had some mixed results, but most recently, his pick of Senator Darline Graham… was successful in her primary battle.”

Trump, in his comments, said “because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment”. The Federal Communications Commission assigns and oversees licenses for radio and television broadcast frequencies.
“Unfortunately, she is not the only one,” he added. “The Radical Left News is going out of their way to harass, demean, and libel anything ‘TRUMP.'”
Welker is an award-winning journalist who earned bipartisan praise after moderating a 2020 presidential debate featuring Trump and Joe Biden, the Democrat who won that year’s election.
An NBC News spokesperson, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, defended Welker on Sunday, telling AFP that “Kristen is one of the best in the business and we stand by her.”
Lawsuits and restrictions
Trump’s endorsements overall have proved helpful for Republican candidates running for statewide office.

But his approval ratings have slid, and at least 10 of Trump’s picks have been defeated this cycle, according to a tally compiled by Ballotpedia. They include four US House hopefuls and six candidates for governor, among them conspiracy theorist Mike Lindell in Minnesota.

Billionaire Trump has used American media to his advantage over the years as a provocative real estate developer in New York. But as president he dramatically turned against the press and what he called “fake news.”
He has sued several newspapers including the Wall Street Journal and New York Times, and ordered federal funding slashed for public media.
His administration has ramped up restrictions and attempts to intimidate journalists, and the FCC — headed by a close Trump associate — has pressured broadcasters to toe the line.
“I hope that Chairman Brendan Carr, and the fine people of his Commission, will take this Threat to our Country very seriously,” Trump said.
The latest attack is part of the Trump administration’s months-long offensive against media outlets it deems overly critical.

Such efforts are facing growing resistance from news organizations and major broadcast networks. Several of them have filed lawsuits against the FCC, arguing such pressure constitutes political retaliation that violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which protects freedom of speech.

Relations between Trump and Welker have been under pressure for months. In June the president abruptly cut short an interview with her following a tense exchange, during which he grew irritated by Welker’s questioning, particularly on the war against Iran.
Experts argue the FCC lacks the legal authority to punish broadcasters or reporters for their viewpoints.
According to a 2025 paper by the Yale Journal on Regulation, the US Supreme Court has confirmed that US law “does not grant the FCC the power to ban controversial speech.” /dl

articles.title: ICYMI: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Week 8 highlights
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – The week’s most consequential testimony came on Day 18, August 25, when Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio, designated as the second…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The week’s most consequential testimony came on Day 18, August 25, when Office of the Vice President Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio, designated as the second hostile witness in the trial, told the Senate impeachment court that Vice President Sara Duterte knew about and had authorized all activities related to the use of confidential funds under her office’s disposal.
Also, the week’s proceedings highlighted the sub judice ruling issued by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero.

The testimony came amid heated exchanges over unusual names appearing in acknowledgment receipts, questions over whether Col. Raymund Dante Lachica would take the witness stand, and a ruling reminding all participants—including Duterte—that the sub judice rule bars public comments on the merits of the case. The prosecution also moved to streamline its presentation as it sought to wrap up its case, while new witnesses and subpoenas were lined up for the coming hearings.
Key developments August 24, 2026 (Day 17)

items: Former OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta continued her testimony as the prosecution questioned acknowledgment receipts bearing unusual names, including Antonio Pagong, who was listed as receiving P100,000 for the purchase of information, and Timon Andrew Pusa, who was listed as receiving P100,000 for vehicle rental.

Acosta testified that it was standard operating procedure in Duterte’s Davao City office and later in the OVP to turn over confidential funds to the security officer, despite the officer not being a bonded official.

She also said she could not recall confidential fund allocations reportedly given to Duterte while she was mayor of Davao City from 2019 to 2022. The prosecution said these allocations totaled about P1.8 billion.

The question of whether Col. Raymund Dante Lachica would testify remained unresolved. Two previous witnesses had testified that Lachica received P500 million in confidential funds, prompting calls for him to appear before the impeachment court.

blocks.text: August 25, 2026 (Day 18)

items: Lemuel Ortonio, OVP assistant chief of staff and the trial’s second hostile witness, was presented and testified that Duterte knew about and authorized all activities involving the use of confidential funds under her office.
The testimony came amid heated exchanges over unusual names appearing in acknowledgment receipts, questions over whether Col. Raymund Dante Lachica would take the witness stand.
Ortonio also testified that he personally paid P150,000 to cover excess confidential fund expenses after a request was relayed through Acosta and traced to Lachica.
The prosecution argued that the testimony indicated the OVP had treated confidential funds like petty cash, pointing to alleged gaps in liquidation and fund management.
The testimony strengthened the prosecution’s effort to establish Duterte’s role as the approving authority over the confidential funds.

blocks.text: August 26, 2026 (Day 19)

items: Escudero ruled that the sub judice rule under Rule 18 of the Rules of Impeachment applies to everyone participating in the trial, including Duterte.
Escudero directed Duterte’s defense lawyers to inform her of the restriction after she issued public remarks criticizing the prosecution and the impeachment complaints.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said Duterte should be mindful of her public statements concerning the merits of the case.
Both the prosecution and defense said they would consider whether to replace their respective spokespersons following the ruling.

A separate courtroom dispute erupted over the unusual names appearing in acknowledgment receipts. Sen. Robin Padilla cited the use of aliases by national heroes as a possible explanation, while Sen. Bam Aquino pointed out that Ninoy Aquino had not received confidential funds.
Prosecution counsel Mae Divinagracia clarified that the prosecution had never alleged that the names on the acknowledgment receipts were aliases.

Ortonio also said there was nothing wrong with giving confidential funds to informants and allowing them to buy medicines themselves, but Sen. Francis Pangilinan questioned whether such purchases should instead have undergone bidding.

blocks.text: The prosecution announced that defense counsel Michael Poa would be called to testify on September 2 on how the Department of Education disbursed confidential funds during Duterte’s tenure as Education Secretary, while previously planned witness Maj. Gen. Adonis Bajao would not be called.

It also sought subpoenas for three AFP officers, Col. Manaros Boransing II, Col. Magtanggol Panopio, and Col. Adonis Bajao, after DepEd disbursing officer Edward Fajarda suffered a stroke and could not appear.

Separately, the AFP said it had terminated its own inquiry into Lachica to avoid duplicating the Ombudsman’s investigation, and the DOJ confirmed that Duterte’s criminal grave threats case can proceed independently of the impeachment. /dp

articles.title: De Lima seeks all-out protection of mangroves amid heavy rains, floods; warns vs earth-balling
articles.summary: House Senior Deputy Minority Leader and Mamamayang Liberal (ML) Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima is prodding the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to suspend its earth-balling and…

blocks.text: House Senior Deputy Minority Leader and Mamamayang Liberal (ML) Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima is prodding the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) to suspend its earth-balling and relocation of mangroves.
This, as De Lima expressed concern over the destructive impact of the recent strong typhoons and "Habagat" as well as climate change on the livelihoods and lives of Filipinos.
Earth-balling is defined as the practice of digging up a tree with its surrounding soil to form a compact, circular mass, which is then protected during transport to a new location.

During the House budget briefing on the proposed 2027 budget of the DENR on Aug. 26, De Lima asked about the status of the DENR Memorandum dated Oct. 8, 2025, which provides interim operational guidance and conditions on the earth-balling and relocation of mangroves in exceptional circumstances.

“We understand that there is a technical working group (TWG) that was recently created regarding the earth-balling of mangroves. I am wondering why that memorandum was issued at all, even before consultations, or even before the creation of TWG, or a scientific study. What exactly is the survival rate?” De Lima asked during the briefing.

"All of these things should have been confirmed or verified first before allowing the issuance of this memorandum. Yes, it is considered interim operational guidance, but is it really interim, or is it now a de facto policy na mag-allow ng earth-balling of mangroves for flagship infrastructure?” she added.

Responding to De Lima, DENR Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said that, amid numerous requests for permits for earth-balling for government projects, the agency deemed it appropriate at the time, under sustainable development that they are following, to issue interim guidelines through a memorandum specifying certain methods or guidelines to be followed.

Cuna also shared that the DENR was in consultation with the Ecosystem Research and Development Bureau (ERDB), the Biodiversity Management Bureau (BMB) and the Forest Management Bureau. According to Cuna, they requested these agencies to come up with a study particularly on the survival rate.

“We're encouraged by the initial results that have been sent to us already, but for us to be able to to really extensively complete the study, we are targeting December of this year,” the DENR chief said.

De Lima stressed that the DENR must be more forthright about study’s findings, given the extremely low, if not zero, survival rate of mangrove earth-balling. She then urged the DENR to first suspend the implementation, if not do away with the memorandum altogether.
Cuna committed to evaluate the matter in light of ongoing developments.

Last July 2026, De Lima filed House Resolution (HR) No. 1206 seeking to conduct an inquiry into the DENR memorandum as this directly conflicts with the Philippines’ internationally-endorsed commitments and undermines the country’s credibility and standing as a steward of global mangrove conservation.

According to HR No. 1206, the memorandum contravenes Section 99 of Republic Act (RA) No. 8550 or the “Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998” as amended, which prohibits the conversion of mangroves for any other purpose, as well as RA No. 8371 or the “Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act of 1997”, if mangrove areas are located within ancestral domains.

The resolution also cited Presidential Proclamation 2152, which declares the entire Province of Palawan and certain parcels of the public domain and/or parts of the country as mangrove swamp forest reserves.

The Global Mangrove Alliance Philippines (GMAP) welcomed De Lima’s measure “as an important opportunity to ensure that decisions affecting our mangroves are guided by science, existing environmental laws, the constitutional right of Filipinos to a balanced and healthful ecology, and the long-term welfare of our communities".

“Available evidence also indicates that successful earth-balling has been demonstrated primarily for young, small-diameter mangroves. Most trees affected by development projects are mature mangroves, making successful transplantation highly uncertain and ecologically risky,” GMAP said in a statement.
Coastal greenbelt zones sought

Relatedly, De Lima also filed House Bill (HB) No. 8353 seeking to require the establishment of coastal greenbelt zones, which are mangroves and beach forests stretching to at least 100 meters in width, designed to prevent coastal erosion.
The measure also specifically defines the country’s policy goals and objectives for the management of mangrove resources in the country.

“The lack of a national policy on mangroves poses a great challenge and has caused existing mangrove protection and rehabilitation efforts to remain ineffective and unsuccessful," she noted in her bill.
De Lima says a "comprehensive mechanism" must be urgently implemented to address this.

articles.title: Super Manila Comic Con celebrates Philippine Komiks legends with two exclusive classics
articles.summary: Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks. This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage…

blocks.text: Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks.

This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage with two highly collectible exclusive releases: Classic Darna #1, featuring the earliest adventures of Mars Ravelo's legendary heroine, and Kaluluwa ni Dante, a landmark masterpiece by the "King of Komiks," Francisco V. Coching.

Available exclusively at SuperManila Comic Con, these special editions give longtime fans an opportunity to revisit two Philippine komiks classics while introducing their timeless stories and artwork to a new generation of collectors.
CLASSIC DARNA #1
THE LEGEND RETURNS!
Created by legendary Filipino komiks writer Mars Ravelo, Darna first appeared in Pilipino Komiks in 1950 and went on to become one of the Philippines' most enduring cultural icons.

Classic Darna #1 SuperManila Comic Con Exclusive reprints stories from Darna's earliest komiks appearances, including her first appearance and legendary origin story. The original stories feature the breathtaking artwork of acclaimed Filipino artist Nestor Redondo, whose illustrations helped define Darna's iconic look for generations of readers.
Adding a stunning contemporary touch to this historic release, both editions feature exclusive cover artwork by internationally renowned artist Stanley "ARTGERM" Lau.
The release comes in two strictly limited editions:
Full-Color Virgin Cover Edition — ₱1,000 per copy
1,000 copies featuring the original stories presented in vibrant color.
Sepia Cover / Black-and-White Interior Edition — ₱800 per copy
1,000 copies featuring a sepia-toned cover and the stories reproduced in black and white, paying tribute to the way generations of Filipino readers experienced Darna in the pages of komiks.
Every copy of both editions also includes an exclusive Darna trading card.
This is not a new story or retelling, but a reprint of the classic material that helped establish Darna's enduring legacy.
Classic Darna #1
Created by Mars Ravelo
Illustrated by Nestor Redondo
Exclusive Cover Artwork by Stanley "ARTGERM" Lau
KALULUWA NI DANTE
A MASTERPIECE FROM THE "KING OF KOMIKS"

Francisco V. Coching (1919–1998) is widely regarded as one of the greatest storytellers and illustrators in Philippine comics history. Hailed as the "King of Komiks," Coching created more than 50 serialized komiks novels over a career spanning four decades, including such celebrated works as Pedro Penduko, Hagibis, Sabas, ang Barbaro, El Indio, Lapu-Lapu, and Kaluluwa ni Dante.

First serialized in 1949, Kaluluwa ni Dante follows Dante Magtanggol on an extraordinary out-of-body journey guided by the mysterious Dr. Futiphar. Blending mystery, fantasy, adventure, and moral drama, the story explores justice, redemption, love, and the timeless struggle between good and evil.
With Coching's richly detailed artwork and cinematic storytelling, Kaluluwa ni Dante remains one of his most celebrated masterpieces.

Coching's influence extended far beyond komiks. 51 of his 63 komiks novels were adapted into films, making him one of the most adapted creators in Philippine cinema. In 2014, he was posthumously conferred the title of National Artist for Visual Arts.
SuperManila Comic Con presents a special 116-page softcover edition of Kaluluwa ni Dante, faithfully reproduced in its original black-and-white format, preserving Coching's timeless artwork.
Only 300 copies will be produced, making this a particularly rare opportunity for collectors and fans of Philippine komiks history.
Kaluluwa ni Dante
By Francisco V. Coching, the "King of Komiks"
116-page softcover edition
Original black-and-white format
Only 300 copies
₱1,000 per copy
TWO LEGENDS. TWO CLASSICS. ONE CELEBRATION OF PHILIPPINE KOMIKS.

From Darna, the legendary heroine created by Mars Ravelo, to Kaluluwa ni Dante, the masterpiece of National Artist Francisco V. Coching, these exclusive SuperManila Comic Con releases celebrate the creators and stories that helped shape Filipino pop culture.

Classic Darna #1 and Kaluluwa ni Dante will be available exclusively at the SMCC Merch Booth at The Concourse during SuperManila Comic Con 2026, September 4–6, 2026, at The Concourse and SPACE at One Ayala, Makati City.
Limited quantities. Exclusively at SuperManila Comic Con.
For tickets and event updates, visit supermanila.ph and follow SuperManila Comic Con on its official social media channels.

articles.title: Patient access programs at Asian Hospital and Medical Center: Making cancer treatment more affordable
articles.summary: Cancer treatment can be a long and challenging journey. Aside from coping with the physical and emotional effects of cancer, many patients and their families also worry about the cost of treatment.…

blocks.text: Cancer treatment can be a long and challenging journey. Aside from coping with the physical and emotional effects of cancer, many patients and their families also worry about the cost of treatment. The good news is that Patient Access Programs can help eligible patients continue their treatment by making cancer medicines more affordable.

Patient Access Programs are designed to help eligible patients reduce the cost of their prescribed cancer medicines through discounts or free medicines funded by pharmaceutical companies. Depending on the specific program, patients may receive discounts on their treatment or qualify for free doses after meeting certain eligibility requirements. These programs help lessen the financial burden of cancer care and allow patients to stay on track with the treatment plan recommended by their physician.

"Cancer treatment should never be interrupted because of financial concerns. Patient Access Programs play an important role in helping eligible patients continue their prescribed treatment by connecting them with available support that can make life-saving medicines more affordable," said Dr. Mary Ondinee Manalo-Igot, Oncologist at the Asian Cancer Institute, Asian Hospital and Medical Center.

Many people are unaware that financial assistance may be available to help cover the cost of cancer treatment. By asking their healthcare team about Patient Access Programs, eligible patients can learn about the available options and determine whether they qualify. Each program has its own eligibility requirements, which typically include a valid prescription and other medical and program-specific criteria.

"Early conversations about financial support are just as important as discussing treatment options. Patients should feel comfortable asking their healthcare team about Patient Access Programs, as these may help them stay on track with the treatment recommended by their physician," Dr. Manalo-Igot added.

At Asian Hospital and Medical Center, patients may inquire about available Patient Access Programs through their attending physician or by visiting Chrys Specialty Pharmacy. As a patient access hub, Chrys Specialty Pharmacy provides information on available programs, explains eligibility requirements, assists with enrollment, and works closely with the patient's healthcare team to make the process as smooth and convenient as possible.

In addition to Patient Access Programs, eligible patients may also explore government financial assistance. With the guidance of the Medical Social Worker at the Outpatient Health Services, patients can apply for available government assistance programs. Chrys Specialty Pharmacy can also prepare the treatment quotation required for the application.

To further help patients manage the cost of treatment, Asian Hospital and Medical Center also partners with BDO, BPI, UnionBank, and HSBC to offer qualified cardholders flexible installment payment options, including up to three months at 0% interest. Together with Patient Access Programs and government financial assistance, these initiatives help ensure that financial concerns do not prevent eligible patients from receiving the treatment they need.

"Our goal is to ensure that eligible patients have access to the treatment they need without unnecessary delays due to financial challenges. Through Patient Access Programs and the support of our multidisciplinary team, we help patients navigate available assistance so they can focus on their treatment and recovery with confidence," Dr. Manalo-Igot emphasized.

For inquiries about Patient Access Programs, you may call the Asian Hospital and Medical Center hotline at (02) 8771-9000 local 5913 or email [email protected]. You may also follow the hospital's official social media pages at @AsianHospitalPH for updates, health information, and patient services.

articles.title: Tarlac declares state of calamity as floods wreck 2 bridges
articles.summary: Aquino and Agana bridges were damaged as the province declares calamity.

blocks.text: The Aquino Bridge in Tarlac City, Tarlac, is seen partially collapsed on Aug. 28, 2026.
Radyo Pilipinas / Grace Acuar
MANILA, Philippines — Tarlac has been placed under a state of calamity after severe flooding damaged two bridges and disrupted major roads.
The Sangguniang Panlalawigan approved Resolution No. 416-2026 during a special session Sunday, August 30, citing the widespread and continuing effects of heavy southwest monsoon rains.

The resolution said continuous rainfall had caused widespread flooding and other rain-induced hazards, "rendering major thoroughfares impassable," including after portions of the Ninoy Aquino Bridge and Agana Bridge collapsed.
The provincial board also cited damage to agricultural crops and properties and severe disruption to the livelihood and day-to-day activities of communities.
The provincial board said the bad weather had "significantly disrupted transportation, access to essential services, agricultural operations, and other economic undertakings."
It also warned that vulnerable communities and critical infrastructure remained exposed to possible further damage and disruption.

The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council recommended the declaration, citing the extent and severity of the damage and the need for "immediate, coordinated, and sustained relief, response, recovery and rehabilitation measures" across Tarlac.

A portion of the Ninoy Aquino Bridge in Tarlac City first collapsed late Friday, August 28, amid strong currents in the Tarlac River. Another portion of the bridge gave way Sunday as high water and strong currents persisted.
The Agana Bridge, which had been used as an alternative route after the Aquino Bridge was closed, also collapsed Saturday night, August 29.
A vehicle carrying five people fell into the river when part of the Agana Bridge gave way. One passenger was rescued, while four others remained missing as search operations continued.
The back-to-back bridge failures have disrupted routes linking Tarlac City with communities west of the Tarlac River.
Temporary access eyed
Authorities have begun working on temporary measures to restore access.

Heavy equipment was deployed near the Agana Bridge as preparations were made for a temporary Bailey bridge, while the Department of Public Works and Highways has been assessing possible repairs and temporary access at the damaged Ninoy Aquino Bridge.
Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon inspected the Aquino Bridge over the weekend as authorities assessed damage from the swollen Tarlac River.
The state of calamity declaration allows the provincial government to mobilize resources for relief, recovery and rehabilitation efforts following the severe flooding.
More rain possible
The disruption comes as the southwest monsoon continues to affect Tarlac and other parts of Luzon.
PAGASA's weekly outlook said occasional rain may persist over Tarlac through Tuesday, September 1, as the enhanced southwest monsoon continues to affect Luzon.
The weather bureau has warned that repeated rainfall may heighten the risk of flooding in areas where the ground and waterways have already absorbed significant rain.
Authorities continue to assess damage to roads, bridges, agricultural areas and private property across Tarlac.

articles.title: Retired Marine colonel wins P9.5-M pension claim after mutiny case
articles.summary: Retired colonel Achilles Segumalian was previously accused of involvement in a 2006 mutiny against the Arroyo administration but was cleared of all charges

blocks.text: The Commission on Audit in Commonwealth Ave., Quezon City.
Wikimedia Commons
Retired colonel Achilles Segumalian was previously accused of involvement in a 2006 mutiny against the Arroyo administration but was cleared of all charges

items: The Commission on Audit ruled in favor of retired Colonel Achilles Segumalian, allowing him to claim over P9.521 million in unpaid pension dating back to May 17, 2010.
The COA found that the delay in processing Segumalian's pension claim was justified, as his compulsory retirement was not formally established until December 28, 2022.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Audit (COA) has ruled in favor of a retired military colonel, who faced allegations over a mutiny, in a claim for unpaid pension dating back to May 17, 2010. He stands to collect more than P9.521 million.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) dismissed the case against Achilles Segumalian in 2018, eight years after he retired from the military with the rank of Marine colonel.

Segumalian served in the Armed Forces for more than three decades before his retirement. He was accused of links to a 2006 rebellion by Marines against the Arroyo administration, spent four years in detention and faced a rebellion charge. He was eventually cleared of the allegations.

Segumalian pursued his retirement benefits while working civilian jobs in the absence of a pension. He filed his application for official retirement with the Naval Adjutant on July 20, 2022, and received a Compulsory Retirement Order on December 28, 2022.

The Armed Forces of the Philippines Pension and Gratuity Management Center issued a certification on February 15, 2024, showing that Segumalian was owed monthly pension payments from July 20, 2012, to December 31, 2022, amounting to over P8.480 million.
Segumalian, however, challenged the computation before the COA, pointing to a July 9, 2023, disbursement voucher for P9.52 million covering his pension from May 17, 2010, to December 31, 2022.

The COA en banc ruled in his favor on July 20, finding that he was entitled to pension payments from his retirement date and that the 10-year prescription period did not apply because of the circumstances surrounding his case.

The commission said Segumalian had shown that the delay in processing his claim was justified. It noted that his compulsory retirement was not formally established until the issuance of General Orders No. 1894 on December 28, 2022, making his late filing legally acceptable.
The COA also cited favorable recommendations from the AFP pension center and the auditors who reviewed the claim. – Rappler.com

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Heavy traffic has been observed on sections of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx), while the Libtong Exit in Meycauayan, Bulacan was temporarily closed on Monday. This is due to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Heavy traffic has been observed on sections of the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx), while the Libtong Exit in Meycauayan, Bulacan was temporarily closed on Monday.
This is due to flooding caused by the southwest monsoon or “habagat.”

In its 9 a.m. traffic advisory, the NLEx Corporation said traffic remains heavy along the NLEx-Candaba Viaduct, Tulaoc (San Simon, Pampanga), and the southbound lane of the San Simon Interchange due to continuous heavy rainfall or flooding on local roads.

“Motorists approaching San Simon Northbound and San Simon Southbound may take the San Simon Exit and re-enter NLEx via the San Simon Entry as an alternative route to avoid the flooded section,” the corporation said in the advisory.
“The San Fernando Southbound Entry is temporarily closed due to heavy traffic in San Simon caused by water buildup,” it added.
NLEx Corp. also noted that southbound motorists who want to return to the northbound lane may use U-turn slots before the Tulaoc Overpass and before the San Simon Interchange.
Patrol officers are on-site to assist motorists and manage the traffic situation in the areas, said the NLEx Corp.
Meanwhile, light traffic was continuously seen on the following NLEx roads:

articles.title: Nepal floods: Brother searches tunnel for fifth day for missing sibling
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Ram Budha traveled once again on Sunday morning to the mouth of a tunnel in Rasuwa where he believes his younger brother has been trapped for five days. Standing a short distance…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Ram Budha traveled once again on Sunday morning to the mouth of a tunnel in Rasuwa where he believes his younger brother has been trapped for five days.

Standing a short distance inside the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project at Hakubesi, Ram shouted repeatedly, hoping to hear the voice of his 20-year-old brother Prabin Budha from somewhere in the darkness.
There was no response.
Ram waited for a while before walking back out, disappointed but still unwilling to abandon hope.

A resident of Patarasi Rural Municipality-5 in Jumla, Ram has been returning to the tunnel every day since floods swept through the area, cutting off contact with his brother and other workers inside.

“I went to the mouth of the tunnel again this morning and called out to my brother. There was no response,” Ram told the Post on Sunday morning. “My hope is fading. We know nothing about the conditions inside the tunnel.”
Ram and relatives of other missing workers arrived in the Trishuli area on Sunday morning. On Saturday, he entered the tunnel himself in search of his brother and the others.
He managed to go around 100 metres inside, despite thick mud deposited by the floodwaters.
“The mud came up to my chest. I went about 100 meters inside and shouted as loudly as I could, but there was no response,” he said. “Then I had to come back out.”
Since the first day of the disaster, Ram has repeatedly appealed to the Nepali Army to rescue his brother and other workers trapped inside. The army has told him that rescue efforts are underway.
“The rescue could not happen quickly,” he said. “I have now heard that a Chinese team has also arrived. I just hope we can soon find out what the situation is inside the tunnel.”
Ram and Prabin had both been working at the Upper Trishuli-1 project in Hakubesi, Rasuwa. Ram had been employed there for about a year.

Prabin, who had recently completed Grade 12, had been preparing to go abroad for work. His paperwork was being processed in Kathmandu, and he had joined his elder brother at the hydropower project to earn money for his planned journey overseas.
“Rather than sitting idle while his documents were being processed, I brought him to work with me so he could earn some money,” Ram said.
Back home in Jumla, their parents have been anxiously waiting for news. Ram said he has been trying to reassure them that search efforts are continuing.

He said he had received information that around 25 people from Patarasi, including his brother, were trapped inside the tunnel. Relatives of the missing workers have been calling him constantly, asking for updates.
The day before the flood hit the Bhotekoshi river system, Ram had left Hakubesi for Kathmandu, leaving his younger brother at the project site.
On the day of the disaster, Prabin and around 25 other workers from Jumla were working inside Tunnel No 216 of the Upper Trishuli-1 project.

The project is being built by Sinohydro Corporation. Ram had joined the project about a year ago and brought his younger brother to Rasuwa around a month ago because the work offered relatively good earnings. /dl

articles.title: Filipinos who braved floods, disasters hailed as modern-day heroes
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Senators on National Heroes’ Day paid tribute not only to country’s historical heroes but also ordinary citizens who risked their safety to help others amid recent rains,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senators on National Heroes’ Day paid tribute not only to country’s historical heroes but also ordinary citizens who risked their safety to help others amid recent rains, flooding, and other disasters.

Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said that while National Heroes’ Day is rooted in the country’s collective struggle for freedom—beginning with the 1896 Revolution—it honors not only historical figures, but also ordinary Filipinos who courageously love and serve the country.
He cited parents, overseas Filipino workers, environment defenders, fisherfolks, farmers, truth-tellers, and those holding people accountable as modern-day heroes.
Pangilinan also paid tribute to those who responded to the recent rains caused by the southwest monsoon or habagat.

Nitong mga nagdaang linggo ng walang tigil na ulan, sumuong sa baha ang mga kapitbahay, rider, social worker at health professional, at volunteer sa disaster at emergency response,” Pangilinan said in a press release on Monday.
(In recent weeks of incessant rains, neighbors, riders, social workers, health professionals, and disaster and emergency response volunteers waded through floodwaters)
“‘Yan ang bayaning Pilipino: Hindi nagpapasiil sa hamon ng buhay,” he added.
(That is the Filipino hero: One who does not let life’s challenges defeat them.)

Sen. Bong Go echoed Pangilinan’s sentiments, highlighting the contributions of frontliners, health workers, rescuers, uniformed personnel and volunteers who continue to respond to emergencies and disasters.

“Sa mga nararanasan nating kalamidad at masamang panahon, marami sa kanila ang hindi nag-atubiling tumulong at rumesponde para masiguro ang kaligtasan ng ating mga kababayan,” Go said in a Facebook post.
(Amid the calamities and severe weather we have experienced, many of them did not hesitate to help and respond to ensure the safety of their fellow Filipinos.)
Go said their courage, compassion, and love for the country should inspire other Filipinos.
Meanwhile, Senate President Win Gatchalian called on Filipinos to carry the spirit of heroism into the challenges they face.
“Pugay sa ating mga bayani at sa tapang nilang manindigan para sa bayan,” Gatchalian said in a post on Facebook.
(Salute to our heroes and to their courage to stand up for the country.)
“Dalhin natin ang diwang ito sa bawat hamong kinakaharap natin — manindigan sa tama, ipaglaban ang kapakanan ng bawat isa, at higit sa lahat, unahin ang Pilipinas,” the Senate president added.
(Let us carry this spirit into every challenge we face — stand up for what is right, fight for the welfare of everyone, and above all, put the Philippines first.)
Moreover, Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III also praised Filipinos who had dedicated their lives and service to the country.
For Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel “Migz” Zubiri and Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, the occasion is a chance to honor heroes across generations.
National Heroes’ Day is observed every last Monday of August as a national holiday to commemorate the sacrifices and contributions of the country’s heroes./dp

articles.title: Torrential rain to lash South Korea on Monday
articles.summary: SEOUL — Heavy rain accompanied by gusty winds, thunder and lightning is forecast across most of South Korea through Monday. The central west coast is expected to bear the brunt of the…

blocks.text: SEOUL — Heavy rain accompanied by gusty winds, thunder and lightning is forecast across most of South Korea through Monday. The central west coast is expected to bear the brunt of the downpours.

Rain was already falling in southern parts of the country Sunday, where heavy rain warnings were in effect as of 5 p.m., according to the Korea Meteorological Administration. The rain will spread across most of the country by Monday, hitting hardest in southern Gyeonggi Province, southwestern Gangwon Province, the central Chungcheong region and North Jeolla Province.

South Chungcheong Province and the cities of Daejeon and Sejong are expected to receive 80-150 millimeters of rain through Tuesday — totals could climb past 250 millimeters along the coast and 200 millimeters inland. North Chungcheong Province could also see up to 200 millimeters.

Southern Gyeonggi is expected to get 50-100 millimeters, with certain areas topping 150. Seoul, Incheon, northern Gyeonggi and Gangwon Province are in line for 30-80 millimeters, though mountainous parts of southern Gangwon could get more than 120.
In the greater Seoul area, the heaviest rain is expected between the predawn hours and Monday morning.
The rain should end in southern regions and on Jeju Island by Monday night but will linger over central parts of the country into Tuesday morning.
The weather agency warned of possible damage from the downpours, saying rainfall will vary sharply from one area to the next with strong bursts alternating with lulls.

The rain will do little to cool the southern half of the country, where heat advisories remain in place. The heat index there and on Jeju is expected to reach around 33 degrees Celsius in the coming days. /dl

articles.title: OCD: Damage to infra at P6.16B, agriculture at P2.32B due to Habagat
articles.summary: Infrastructure damage from the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat has reached P6.16 billion, while agricultural losses stood at P2.32 billion, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Monday.

blocks.text: Published August 31, 2026 9:55am
Infrastructure damage from the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat has reached P6.16 billion, while agricultural losses stood at P2.32 billion, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Monday.

“Total po ang nawala o nasira in terms of figures ay P6.16 billion in infrastructure. Sa damage to agriculture naman po ay P2.32 billion,” OCD Disaster Preparedness Service director Vicente Gregorio Tomas said in an interview on GMA News’ Unang Balita.
(Total damage to infrastructure is P6.16 billion while to agriculture, P2.32 billion.)
Tomas added that 724 areas were flooded in Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, Metro Manila, and Calabarzon.
Central Luzon accounted for the largest number of flooded areas, with 561 affected areas reported in Bataan, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac, and Zambales.
From other regions, 122 areas remained flooded in Pangasinan, 24 in Laguna, and 11 in Muntinlupa and Valenzuela.
Tomas said a total of 110 road sections and 14 bridges remained impassable due to landslides and damaged infrastructure.
Search and rescue operations were ongoing, including in Tarlac where a bridge collapsed. One person was rescued while four others remained missing from the incident.
A total of 677 personnel organized into 32 teams were deployed for search-and-rescue operations, while more than 20,000 personnel from various security sectors and local governments were on standby.

Tomas said relief resources remained sufficient, particularly food, non-food items, and other assistance being provided through the Department of Social Welfare and Development-led response cluster. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: 'Pilandok' slightly intensifies over Philippine Sea, may become storm
articles.summary: It may briefly become a tropical storm Tuesday before weakening again.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok slightly intensified early Monday while remaining almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of extreme Northern Luzon, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
As of 4 a.m. Aug. 31, Pilandok was 1,130 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon, packing maximum sustained winds of 55 kph near the center and gusts of up to 70 kph.
Strong winds extended up to 450 kilometers from its center. No Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal was in effect.
PAGASA said Pilandok may briefly intensify into a tropical storm by Tuesday afternoon before weakening back into a tropical depression by Wednesday morning.
The cyclone is forecast to move generally north-northwestward and exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility by Wednesday evening or early Thursday morning.
It is unlikely to make landfall and is expected to remain far from the Philippine landmass.
PAGASA is also monitoring two tropical depressions outside PAR northwest of the Philippines.
Weather specialist Aldczar Aurelio said the tropical cyclones are enhancing the southwest monsoon, or habagat, which continues to bring rain to Luzon and the western section of the Visayas.
"Kaya makakaasa pa rin tayo ngayong araw ng maulan na panahon lalo na sa malaking bahagi ng Luzon, kasama ang Metro Manila," Aurelio said.
("So we can still expect rainy weather today, especially across a large part of Luzon, including Metro Manila.")

Forecast. Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga may experience monsoon rains, with possible flash floods or landslides due to heavy to intense rainfall, PAGASA said Monday.
Metro Manila, Calabarzon and several other areas may experience scattered rain and thunderstorms due to the habagat, with possible flash floods or landslides from moderate to at times heavy rain.
PAGASA also warned that the habagat may bring strong to gale-force gusts over most of the country Monday, particularly in exposed coastal and upland areas.

articles.title: Victorian prisoners to be sent out to repair roads under Labor’s pothole plan
articles.summary: Inmates would take over ‘basic’ road maintenance duties, allowing skilled crews to focus on fixing 500,000 potholes

blocks.text: Victorian prisoners will be put to work on road maintenance as part of Labor’s plan to fix the state’s potholes if re-elected.

The state’s premier, Ben Carroll, outlined the plan on Monday off the back of an announcement on Sunday that the government would be increasing the road maintenance budget by $352m to fix 500,000 potholes by the end of January.

The funding is on top of the more than $1bn budgeted for road maintenance in May, and is partially offset by delaying planned level-crossing removals in Melbourne’s south-east – two in Highett and one in Mentone.

Carroll said that if Labor wins the November election, it would work with Corrections Victoria to develop a pilot program to put supervised, minimum-security prisoners to work performing roadside maintenance.

The plan would include having prisoners take over “basic” duties such as mowing lawns, controlling weeds, removing graffiti and picking up rubbish, allowing more skilled crews to focus on fixing potholes.
The government said the work of prisoners “will not replace paid jobs” but instead “supplement the workforce where there are skill and capacity shortages”.
“Low-level prisoners want to be doing something that will benefit the whole of the state,” Carroll told reporters on Monday.

“We’ve seen the work that they do on graffiti removal. We’ve seen the work that they do on weeding and supporting our road network more broadly. But working with our crews and really increasing the labour capacity does mean we can fix up more potholes sooner, faster and better.”
However, Australian Lawyers Alliance criminal justice spokesperson and barrister Greg Barns SC described the plan as a “cynical short-term solution to a political problem for the government”.

“Whilst it’s always pleasing to see prisoners given the opportunity to work, unless they are paid the appropriate wage for this work, then it simply amounts to cheap labour and, in this case, for a political purpose,” he said.
According to Corrections Victoria, people in prison are paid between $7.15 to $9.80 per day depending on the complexity of their work. This is significantly below the minimum wage.

The government also compulsorily sets aside 20% of the money earned by individuals in prison as savings, which is only available to them upon their release. When this is factored in, people in prison make less than $40 per week to spend while incarcerated.
after newsletter promotion
Barns said prisoners involved in this work should be paid the award rate, with some funds set aside for their release.
“It is important for prisoners’ stability and to lower recidivism rates that when they return to the community, they have some financial buffer,” he said.
“There also should be a link between this work and future employment placement.”

Carroll on Monday also committed to bringing responsibility for road maintenance “back in-house”, meaning less reliance on private contractors, and setting up a website that will allow Victorians to take a photo of a pothole, request it be repaired and monitor progress.
“What we are doing today, [is] making sure the buck stops with the government,” he said.
It comes as the condition of the state’s roads emerges as a significant issue in the lead-up to the election, particularly for regional Victorians.
Last month, the state opposition pledged to invest $5bn to repair and rebuild the state’s roads and patch 1m potholes if it wins in November.

articles.title: PCG, DENR seize P55,000 suspected illegal timber in Sibuyan
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) seized 11 units of suspected illegally cut timber during a joint…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) seized 11 units of suspected illegally cut timber during a joint operation on Romblon’s Sibuyan Island Sunday.
Authorities launched the operation after receiving a report at 7:50 a.m. about illegally sourced round logs located approximately 150 meters from the national road at Sitio Bato.

Personnel from the Coast Guard Sub-Station in Cajidiocan and the DENR Sibuyan Sub-Station proceeded to Sitio Kaguyangan in Barangay Taclobo, San Fernando town, where they found 11 pieces of Tiga, also known as Mangkono or Philippine Ironwood.Each log measured approximately 25 inches in diameter and 107 centimeters in length.
The confiscated timber was estimated to be worth around P55,000.
Authorities said the timber had been abandoned.

The seizure was made under Section 77 of Presidential Decree No. 705, or the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines, as amended by Republic Act No. 7161, which penalizes the unlawful cutting, gathering, collecting and possession of forest products without the necessary licenses or permits.
The confiscated logs were subsequently transported to the DENR impounding area in Barangay Tampayan, Magdiwang, Romblon, for safekeeping and proper disposition.
The joint operation underscores the continuing efforts of government agencies to curb illegal logging and protect Sibuyan Island’s forest resources. /dp

articles.title: Parts of Central Luzon under yellow rainfall warning – Pagasa
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The heavy rainfall warning amid the effects of the southwest monsoon in parts of Central Luzon on Monday morning has been downgraded into yellow alert. But light to moderate…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The heavy rainfall warning amid the effects of the southwest monsoon in parts of Central Luzon on Monday morning has been downgraded into yellow level.
But light to moderate rains and occasionally heavy rains are still forecast in nearby areas including Metro Manila, the state weather bureau said.

According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) in an 8 a.m. advisory, yellow warning level is raised in Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac (San Clemente, Camiling, Mayantoc, Santa Ignacia, Moncada, Paniqui, San Manuel, Anao, Bamban, San Jose, Capas, Gerona, Tarlac City), Nueva Ecija (Cuyapo, Nampicuan, Carranglan, Lupao, Talugtug) and Pampanga (Porac, Floridablanca, Mabalacat, Angeles).
Areas under yellow warning tend to experience rainfall between 7.5 mm and 15 mm within one hour and could continue in the next two hours.
Flooding is also possible in flood-prone areas during the yellow rainfall warning.
Pagasa then told residents of Metro Manila (Caloocan, Valenzuela, Malabon, Navotas, Quezon City) and Rizal (Rodriguez, San Mateo) to expect light to moderate rains over the next 3 hours.
Meanwhile, similar weather is already affecting other parts of Pampanga, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija and Tarlac, which may also persist within 3 hours and may further affect nearby areas. /apl

articles.title: Over 305,000 families in Calabarzon affected by habagat
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — The number of families affected by heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat in Calabarzon since the first week of August has risen to 305,959, the Department of Social…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — The number of families affected by heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat in Calabarzon since the first week of August has risen to 305,959, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) reported on Sunday (Aug. 30).
The affected families are from 965 barangays across the provinces of Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon.
The agency said the number of families who evacuated from their homes began increasing again on Aug. 29 due to heavy rains, particularly in Cavite, Laguna, and Rizal.
Based on the latest reports from local governments, 7,074 families were still staying in 161 evacuation centers across the region as of noon Sunday.
Rizal had the highest number of operating evacuation centers with 72, followed by Cavite with 58, Laguna with 24 and Batangas with seven.
As of Aug. 30, the DSWD office in Calabarzon had distributed 260,072 family food packs to affected families.

A standard DSWD family food pack contains six kilograms of rice, canned goods such as corned beef, tuna, and sardines, as well as sachets of coffee or chocolate malt drink. It is intended to provide a family of five with food for two days.
The assistance was provided not only to families who evacuated but also to those who remained in their homes but were affected by heavy rains and flooding. /dp

articles.title: La Mesa Dam’s water level slightly decreases but still above ‘critical’ mark
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City has slightly eased but remains above its critical mark, the state weather bureau reported on Monday morning. Based on its…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The water level of La Mesa Dam in Quezon City has slightly eased but remains above its critical mark, the state weather bureau reported on Monday morning.
Based on its hydrological situationer, Pagasa said that as of 5 a.m., La Mesa Dam’s water level stood at 79.92 meters—lower compared to the 80.1 meters recorded at 5 p.m. on Sunday.
The new recorded water level in the dam is also below the overflow elevation of 80.15 meters but still above its critical level of 79.5 meters.
Pagasa said excess floodwaters from La Mesa Dam will flow directly into the Tullahan River, which affects low-lying areas in the following Metro Manila cities:

items: Quezon City (Fairview, Forest Hills Subdivision, Quirino Highway, Sta. Quiteria, and San Bartolome)
Caloocan City
Valenzuela City (North Expressway and La Huerta Subdivision)
Malabon City
Navotas City

blocks.text: “All residents living in the aforementioned areas, especially those residing near the riverbanks, are still advised to take necessary precautionary measures,” Pagasa noted.
According to the weather bureau, light to moderate rainfall remains expected over the watershed area for the next 12 hours.

Pagasa earlier reported that several Luzon provinces are forecast to experience heavy rainfall this Monday due to the southwest monsoon, locally known as “habagat,” being enhanced by Tropical Depression Pilandok.
The weather bureau said Pilandok had slightly intensified while moving almost stationary over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon.

Pilandok is currently carrying a maximum sustained wind speed of 55 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center (up from 45 kph from the Sunday evening bulletin) and gustiness of up to 70 kph (up from 55 kph).
The tropical depression is expected to exit the Philippine area of responsibility by Wednesday evening or early Thursday morning. /apl

articles.title: Del Pilar’s 176th birthday marked quietly amid Bulacan floods
articles.summary: BULAKAN, Bulacan – Few words were spoken when wreaths were offered at the shrine of Gat. Marcelo H. Del Pilar here on Sunday, Aug. 30, to mark the hero’s 176th birth anniversary amid stormy weather.…

blocks.text: BULAKAN, Bulacan – Few words were spoken when wreaths were offered at the shrine of Gat. Marcelo H. Del Pilar here on Sunday, Aug. 30, to mark the hero’s 176th birth anniversary amid stormy weather.
The annual commemorative program was cancelled because of the strong monsoon rains on Saturday (August 29) that flooded many streets in this town and other partst of Bulacan province.

Flowers were laid down on behalf of the intended guest of honor Commission on Elections chairman George Erwin Garcia, Bulakan Mayor Vergel Meneses, the National Press Club of the Philippines, the Central Luzon Media Association (CLMA) and the Philippine Masonry.
Marcelo Day is an annual non-working holiday in Bulacan. In 2023, Marcelo Day was also declared as National Press Freedom Day.
Del Pilar, who is historically known for his numerous pseudonyms like the textbook familiar Plaridel. But to Bulacan he is simply remembered as “Tata Celo, ” the Father of Philippine Journalism.
He was born in San Nicolas on Aug. 30, 1850. He died on July 4, 1896 in Barcelona, Spain while pursuing Filipino enlightenment through the publication of La Solidaridad. /dp

articles.title: 8 escape harm as motorboat capsizes off Romblon amid bad weather
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Eight crew members, including the captain, of landing craft tank (LCT) “PMI 3,” escaped unhurt after the motorized banca they were riding capsized off Looc, Romblon.…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Eight crew members, including the captain, of landing craft tank (LCT) “PMI 3,” escaped unhurt after the motorized banca they were riding capsized off Looc, Romblon.
This happened amid strong waves generated by the southwest monsoon, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said on Sunday (August 30).

They were returning to the LCT, which had taken shelter at Looc Bay because of the rough weather, when the banca was flipped by the waves, according to the Coast Guard Sub-Station Looc and the Looc Municipal Police Station.
The crew had gone ashore to purchase provisions despite the prevailing bad weather.
On their way back to the LCT aboard the MBCA “John Michael,” seawater entered the motorboat, eventually causing it to capsize.
The eight managed to swim back to shore in Barangay Punta, Looc, where authorities coordinated with Barangay Captain Edificio Gabat to temporarily accommodate them at the Punta Evacuation Center.

Retrieval of the capsized boat was postponed because of darkness and continued rough conditions. The following day, authorities located and towed the “John Michael” to the shoreline of Barangay Agojo.
The boat sustained minor damage to its engine, canopy and other structural components, according to the PCG.
The Coast Guard said the incident underscored the need for vessel operators and crew members to prepare adequate provisions before adverse weather set in.

It observed that despite early warnings about the effects of the Habagat and the prevailing weather disturbance, the LCT crew had not stored sufficient provisions, prompting them to travel by sea and expose themselves to danger.
The Coast Guard Sub-Station Looc, in coordination with the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, was tasked with assisting the crew in their safe return to the LCT.

The PCG also found that the MBCA “John Michael” had no registration or documents under the Department of Transportation’s Memorandum Circular No. 2017-001, or the Safety, Security and Environmental Numbering (SSEN) System.

The boat owner was issued a warning and directed to secure the vessel’s registration. The PCG also reiterated its prohibition against the operation of colorum or unauthorized vessels in its area of responsibility. /apl

articles.title: Apayao volunteers haul 1.1 tons of waste from Tumog River
articles.summary: TUGUEGARAO CITY – More than 1.1 tons of plastics and other debris were removed from the banks of Tumog River in Apayao in a cleanup drive aimed at reducing the risk of flooding during future…

blocks.text: TUGUEGARAO CITY – More than 1.1 tons of plastics and other debris were removed from the banks of Tumog River in Apayao in a cleanup drive aimed at reducing the risk of flooding during future typhoons.

The one-day cleanup operation on Aug. 29 involved 608 volunteers who cleared about 40.17 kilometers of riverbanks along Tumog River, which traverses 11 barangays in Luna town, according to the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) in Calanasan.
CENRO Calanasan officer-in-charge Dorothy Joy Cayaba said a total of 1,103.56 kilograms of waste were collected from the river system.

She aid the river waste was sorted on site into 538.78 kilos of recyclables, 59.15 kilos of potential recyclables, 134.07 kilos of special waste, and 371.56 kilos of residuals which are bound for final disposal.
“Clearing Tumog River’s physical blockages helps restore natural water flow, directly reducing the risk of river overflow and flooding in surrounding communities during severe weather,” she said.

The volume of waste collected during the one-day operation also puts attention on the continuing problem of garbage entering the river system and the need to sustain cleanup and proper waste disposal efforts, the CENRO Calanasan office said. /dp

articles.title: Grand Canyon flash flood: About 15 people missing
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — About 15 people may be missing after a flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park, the National Park Service said in a statement Sunday. The floods hit the Bright Angel Canyon and…

blocks.text: LOS ANGELES — About 15 people may be missing after a flash flood in Grand Canyon National Park, the National Park Service said in a statement Sunday.

The floods hit the Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area on Saturday, the service said, adding that it was working with Arizona authorities to evacuate people and account for missing individuals.
Earlier, the park service said that more than 20 people were believed missing.
There were no confirmed deaths or injuries, the park service said in an email.
The flash flood, which began about 2:30 pm on Saturday, was caused by rainfall on the Kaibab Plateau, it said.
As of Sunday morning, 62 people have been evacuated, and others were scheduled to be evacuated, it said.

More thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were possible through Monday, possibly leading to “additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions,” the park service warned. /dl

articles.title: 14 drug suspects arrested in Rizal, Cavite buy-busts
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY — Agents of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and the police have arrested 14 suspected drug offenders in separate drug busts in the provinces of Rizal and Cavite over the…

blocks.text: LUCENA CITY — Agents of the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and the police have arrested 14 suspected drug offenders in separate drug busts in the provinces of Rizal and Cavite over the weekend.

The PDEA office in CALABARZON said in a Sunday report (August 30) that its agents, together with police officers, arrested four alleged large-scale drug traffickers in a buy-bust operation in Barangay Bagumbayan in the Rizal town of Teresa on Saturday (August 29).
The operation resulted in the seizure of 100 grams of suspected shabu (crystal methamphetamine) worth P680,000, along with various drug paraphernalia.
On Sunday morning at 10 a.m., PDEA agents and members of the Cavite Maritime Police arrested 10 more suspects during an anti-illegal drug operation in Barangay Palico I at Imus town.

Authorities recovered 106 capsules of suspected ecstasy worth P180,200, suspected high-grade marijuana or “kush” valued at P7,500, suspected ketamine worth P5,000, suspected liquid ecstasy valued at P4,200, and assorted drug paraphernalia.
Three mobile phones were also confiscated and will be examined for possible evidence of drug-related transactions.
PDEA offices in Rizal and Cavite are conducting further investigations to determine the source of the confiscated illegal drugs and identify other individuals who may be involved.
The 14 suspects, whose identities were not disclosed, are facing charges for alleged violations of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. /apl

articles.title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario ‘Lake America’ in US — but not Canada
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — Google redesignated Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on maps seen by US users Sunday after President Donald Trump announced he was renaming the body of water, with a…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — Google redesignated Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on maps seen by US users Sunday after President Donald Trump announced he was renaming the body of water, with a Canadian official slamming the cross-border tensions as “absolutely backwards.”
People in Canada will still see the body of water labeled Lake Ontario, the Indigenous-rooted name used since the 17th century, on their devices and computers, the US-based tech giant said.

The nomenclatural spat erupted as the latest element of Trump’s “America First” narrative, with the longtime allies ramping up a trade war that has seen Washington and Ottawa slap tit-for-tat tariffs on each other.

Trump launched a new salvo of criticism Sunday, taking aim at the auto industry — even as the United States and Canada have deeply interconnected auto manufacturing sectors, with a hefty amount of Canadian parts used in US-made vehicles.
“I don’t want Canadian cars, I don’t want Canadian parts, I don’t want Canadian anything,” Trump seethed in a post on his Truth Social platform.
Apple as of Sunday has maintained the name Lake Ontario on its Maps app, which comes installed on iPhones in the United States.
Google said it made its change in line with the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), the official federal database for geographic names.

“Since we update Google Maps to reflect name changes in official government sources, which is GNIS for the US, people using Maps in the US will see ‘Lake America,’ those in Canada will continue to see ‘Lake Ontario,’ and those outside of the US and Canada will see both names,” Google said on its blog.
The change mirrors Trump’s unilateral altering of the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America in January 2025 — a move Mexico has also rejected.
Ontario is the smallest by surface area of the five Great Lakes, which straddle the Canada-US border between Ontario province and the US state of New York.
The province’s premier, Doug Ford, offered fresh criticism Sunday of the trade dispute and Trump’s lake name change.

“It’s absolutely backwards. It was like something out of (US comedy TV show) ‘Saturday Night Live’ when he signed a document saying — changed to ‘Lake America.’ No one’s going to call it Lake of America,” Ford told ABC talk show “This Week.”
“It’s just so disappointing,” he said.

Ford also warned that while a trade war would harm both countries, “it’d be definitely devastating on the US” given that Canada has been by far the largest purchaser of US vehicles. Should those buys dry up, US auto factories would be hit hard.
“A tariff on Canada is nothing more than a tax on American people,” he said. “It’s probably the worst move you could ever do.”
In his comments, Trump highlighted the success of Ford Motor Company’s plant in the Detroit area that is working overtime to assemble F-150 pickup trucks.
“They’ve been ripping us off for decades, and it’s going to stop,” he said of Canada.
Many F-150 engines are built just across the border in Windsor, Ontario. But Trump has threatened to double tariffs on such auto parts to 50 percent, along with other Canadian products.
Canada has slapped its own counter-tariffs on US goods ranging between 15 and 50 percent, intensifying the trade war between the historically close allies. /dl
