articles.title: At least 15 people may be missing after flash flood in Arizona’s Grand Canyon
articles.summary:
Dozens evacuated after flash-flood event near Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch, officials say

At least 15 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a major flash

blocks.text: At least 15 people may be missing or unaccounted for after a major flash flood swept through the Grand Canyon national park in Arizona on Saturday afternoon, according to the National Park Service.

The flash-flood event occurred in the area of Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch, where park staff and the Arizona department of public safety have evacuated more than 60 people as of Sunday morning.
No injuries have been reported as of Sunday, according to a statement from the National Park Service.

“Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the Phantom Ranch Canteen and cabins, and the entire North Kaibab Trail from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch are closed until further notice,” the statement said.

Park officials announced the number of people who remain missing or unaccounted for in a separate statement, requesting the public to notify the government agency of information they may know about “hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor” on Saturday, as well as “anyone who had a campground reservation in the affected corridor”.

Nearly all footbridges spanning Bright Angel Creek were destroyed, officials said, and the Colorado River is closed to river traffic until further notice as metal structures and debris enter the river.

About half an inch to 1in (1-2.5cm) of rain fell within about 30 minutes in the rocky area where there is a steep drop in elevation, Justin Johndrow, a National Weather Service meteorologist in Flagstaff, told the Associated Press.

blocks.caption: Handout image released by the Grand Canyon National Park Service shows remnants of stone bridge pylons along Bright Angel Creek. Photograph: J Thompson, handout/National Park Service/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Most of it ran off instantly,” Johndrow said.
He said the flooding happened on the north side of the Grand Canyon, where Bright Angel Creek comes from the North Rim down to the Colorado River, dropping about 6,000ft (1,800 meters).
More rain and thunderstorms were possible in the area into Monday.

articles.title: TD Pilandok intensifies, may exit PAR Wednesday evening
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok has slightly intensified over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, according to the state weather bureau on Monday morning. In its 5…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Depression Pilandok has slightly intensified over the Philippine Sea east of Extreme Northern Luzon, according to the state weather bureau on Monday morning.

In its 5 a.m. weather bulletin, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Pilandok is now carrying a maximum sustained wind speed of 55 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center (up from 45 kph in the previous bulletin) and gustiness of up to 70 kph (up from 55 kph).
Last located 1,130 kilometers east of Extreme Northern Luzon, the tropical depression’s movement is almost stationary.

According to Pagasa, Pilandok is expected to exit the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) by Wednesday evening or early Thursday morning as it is forecast to move generally north-northwestward over the majority of the forecast period.
Pilandok is “less likely” to make landfall over the country and will remain far from the Philippine landmass.
The tropical depression would maintain its strength over the next 24 hours.

It may briefly intensify into a tropical storm on Tuesday afternoon and then weaken into a tropical depression by Wednesday morning. Afterwards, it will maintain its strength throughout the remainder of the forecast period.
‘2 cyclones, LPA outside PAR’
The two low-pressure areas (LPAs) being monitored outside PAR have developed into tropical depressions.
Pagasa said the LPA, last spotted 480 kilometers west-northwest of Itbayat, Batanes, developed into a tropical depression as of 2 a.m.
It is carrying a maximum sustained wind speed of 45 kph and gusts of 55 kph.
The newly developed tropical depression is moving north-northwest at 15 kph.
Meanwhile, the LPA (formerly Obet) has also redeveloped into tropical depression “Saudel.”
It was last located 1,190 kilometers west of Extreme Northern Luzon, moving southward at 15 kph.
Saudel is now carrying 45 kph maximum sustained winds and 55 kph gustiness.
Aside from this, another LPA located about 3,115 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas outside PAR has a “medium” chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.

articles.title: Marcos on National Heroes’ Day: Embody our heroes’ courage
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday called on Filipinos to not just remember the nation’s heroes but also embody their courage and keep the flame of patriotism alive. In…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday called on Filipinos to not just remember the nation’s heroes but also embody their courage and keep the flame of patriotism alive.
In his message in commemoration of National Heroes’ Day, Marcos said the public must renew their “solemn duty” to carry forward the nation for which the heroes fought and sacrificed.
“Our forebears won our freedom, defended our dignity, and laid the foundations of the Republic we cherish,” he said.
“We honor them best by embodying their courage, keeping the flame of patriotism alive and becoming the citizens our country needs,” the president said.
He noted that the heroes’ spirit lives in those who choose to “serve, care, and contribute to a cause greater than oneself.”
These can be seen in soldiers and first responders who risk their lives to keep everyone safe, Marcos said.
“We recognize it in our teachers, health workers, farmers, fisherfolk and overseas Filipinos who sustain our families and communities,” he said.
“We find it in every citizen who helps a neighbor, protects the vulnerable, and works honestly for the common good,” Marcos added.
The president also hoped for Filipinos to continually prove themselves worthy of the liberty the heroes have fought for and build a country that future generations will proudly inherit. /apl

articles.title: US strikes Iran for first time in a month
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — The United States said Sunday it had carried out strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on a small island in the Strait of Hormuz, its first attacks on Iran since late July.…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — The United States said Sunday it had carried out strikes on Iranian rocket launchers on a small island in the Strait of Hormuz, its first attacks on Iran since late July.

“Earlier today, US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island,” a US Central Command spokesman said, adding that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards “were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz.”
The strikes came shortly after the US-Iran war hit the six-month mark, and at a time when hostilities had been subsiding.
In recent weeks, the Trump administration has prioritized “economic warfare” over military strikes against Iran.

Iran has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic sea lane through which one-fifth of the world’s oil passed before the United States and Israel started hostilities with airstrikes on Iran on February 28.
“Last week, CENTCOM completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes,” said Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesman for US Central Command.
“US forces are monitoring the area closely and remain prepared to protect the free flow of commerce through this essential waterway,” he said.
Diplomatic efforts, spearheaded by mediators including Pakistan and Qatar, have tried for months to bring an end to the war to no avail.

While a ceasefire was agreed in April and a memorandum of understanding towards a final peace deal was signed in June, no agreement has been forthcoming and Washington has since declared “economic warfare” against Tehran.
A US naval counterblockade of Iranian ports is squeezing petrol supplies in Iran amid a shortfall of domestic production, as the US ramps up pressure on its foe.
The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement.
In a statement on Friday, US Senator Jack Reed criticized President Donald Trump over the war.
“Six months later, not a single objective has been achieved,” said Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee.
“Indeed, he has weakened our position in the Middle East and the world significantly.” /apl

articles.title: Iloilo City opens first library inside public market
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY — Reading and learning are now within reach of marketgoers after the city government opened its first library inside a public market on Friday. The “Library sa Merkado” is located in the…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY — Reading and learning are now within reach of marketgoers after the city government opened its first library inside a public market on Friday.
The “Library sa Merkado” is located in the dry goods section on the second floor of the Iloilo Central Market.
It initially will be open from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Mondays through Fridays, with the city government considering weekend operations.
Mayor Raisa Treñas, who led the opening, said the library is intended particularly for children who accompany their parents to the market.

“We want to start them young and help them discover that reading can be fun. If they start at an early age, they would enjoy learning and would not have problems with reading comprehension,” she said.
Treñas said the collection of books and stories can help spark children’s imagination and encourage learning.
She also expressed hope that similar reading spaces can be established in other public markets across the city.
Assistant Department Head II Maria Mathilde Treñas said the library is intended to serve not only as a place to read but also as a community learning space for vendors, shoppers and children.
“By bringing books and learning spaces right here in the market, you are saying that education should be accessible wherever our people are,” she said.
The reading space was donated by the Zonta Club of Iloilo City Inc. and built with assistance from the Technical Institute of Iloilo City.
With its opening, Iloilo City now has two operational district libraries, eight barangay reading centers, four outdoor libraries in city plazas and one market-based library.
The opening featured a storytelling activity led by Mayor Treñas, who was joined by her daughter, Thea, and selected daycare children. /apl

articles.title: 15 people may be missing after Grand Canyon flash flood, dozens evacuated
articles.summary: A major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S.…

image.caption: This National Park Service photo shows remnants of a destroyed footbridge along Bright Angel Creek in the Grand Canyon following a flash flood on Saturday. (James Thompson/National Park Service/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A major flash flood at the Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S. National Park Service said. Saturday's flooding has left the park service seeking information about 15 people who may be missing or unaccounted for.
Popular tourist spots including Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch remained closed on Sunday

A major flash flood at Arizona's Grand Canyon forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the U.S. National Park Service said.
The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened Saturday afternoon and has left the park service seeking information about 15 people who may be missing or unaccounted for.
Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and creating what appeared to be a new river rapid.

As the park service tries to account for everyone in the area, it is asking asked anyone with details about people hiking or camping there to get in touch. It said it was working with the Arizona Department of Public Safety to continue evacuations Sunday.
"This is a reminder of what a dynamic and active landscape Grand Canyon is," said Jack Schmidt, director of the Center for Colorado River Studies at Utah State University.

Popular tourist spots including the Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab trail remained closed on Sunday while park officials surveyed the damage, the park said. Rafting trips on the Colorado River also have been halted for now.

More than 60 people were evacuated from Phantom Ranch, which has a historic canteen and dorms, and is a common spot for rafters to get off and on the river. More evacuations were planned Sunday, the park said. No injuries have been reported.

Erica Viola said she was at Bright Angel campground when the rain started Saturday afternoon, and she and about 50 other hikers watched the creek rise and then debris start to flow by, including what looked like a bunkhouse. The group was taken by helicopter to safety, ending her adventure two days early, she said.
About 1.2 to 2.5 centimetres of rain fell within about 30 minutes in the rocky area where there's a steep drop in elevation, said National Weather Service meteorologist Justin Johndrow in Flagstaff.
"Most of it ran off instantly," Johndrow said.
He said the flooding happened on the north side of the Grand Canyon, where Bright Angel Creek comes from the North Rim down to the Colorado River, dropping around 1,830 metres.
More rain and thunderstorms were possible for the area into Monday.

articles.title: Marcos calls on Filipinos to work toward nation-building, do more than remember heroes
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, August 31, National Heroes' Day, urged Filipinos to do more than remember heroes and to work toward nation-building.

blocks.text: NATIONAL HEROES' DAY
Published August 31, 2026 6:34am
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Monday, August 31, National Heroes' Day, urged Filipinos to do more than remember heroes and to work toward nation-building.
"I am in solidarity with the entire Filipino people in the commemoration of our National Heroes' Day," Marcos said in his message.

"Today, I call on every Filipino to do more than remember our brave national heroes. Let us also renew our solemn duty to carry forward the nation for which they fought and sacrificed. Our forebears won our freedom, defended our dignity, and laid the foundations of the Republic we cherish. We honor them best by embodying their courage, keeping the flame of patriotism alive, and becoming the citizens our country needs," he added.
Marcos said the spirit of national heroes lives on in our countrymen who serve selflessly.

"Their spirit endures in every Filipino who chooses to serve, care, and contribute to a cause greater than oneself. We see it in our soldiers and first responders who risk their lives to keep us safe. We recognize it in our teachers, health workers, farmers, fisherfolk, and overseas Filipinos who sustain our families and communities. We find it in every citizen who helps a neighbor, protects the vulnerable, and works honestly for the common good," the president said.

Marcos then encouraged Filipinos to "continually prove ourselves worthy of the liberty entrusted to us and build a country that generations yet to come will proudly inherit. Let the Bagong Pilipinas we are shaping continue to revere the heroes of the past, present, and future."
"Mabuhay ang ating mga Bayani! Mabuhay ang dakilang lahi ng Pilipino!" he added.
Malacañang earlier declared the last Monday of August — August 31 — as a regular holiday to commemorate National Heroes' Day. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Dizon sacks DPWH exec over delayed flood response
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has relieved a maintenance chief following reports of delayed response to calamities, as heavy rains continued to trigger flooding across…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has relieved a maintenance chief following reports of delayed response to calamities, as heavy rains continued to trigger flooding across Metro Manila and several parts of Luzon.
In an Aug. 29 memorandum, Dizon ordered engineer Loreto Balena Jr. relieved as maintenance chief of the Las Piñas-Muntinlupa District Engineering Office.
Dizon cited Balena’s “unsatisfactory performance, lack of urgency, and delayed response to calamities” as grounds for his removal.
Balena was directed to complete an inventory of his office’s properties, finish and sign pending documents and deliverables, and turn over official records and other papers.

Sen. JV Ejercito, meanwhile, urged the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to complete unfinished flood control projects before starting new ones, saying incomplete infrastructure could worsen the country’s vulnerability to flooding.
“For practical reasons, we need to close the gaps so that mitigating or solving flood control would be effective,” Ejercito, chair of the Senate finance committee, told dzBB on Sunday.

“Close the gaps, complete the unfinished flood control projects. No new projects. Finish what needs to be finished,” he added.Ejercito’s call came amid renewed scrutiny of the government’s multibillion-peso flood control program and concerns over unfinished or poorly implemented projects.

He also pushed for the proposed Masterplan for Infrastructure National Development, which he said would provide a long-term framework for infrastructure planning that would survive changes in administrations.

The proposed measure would integrate flood control with transportation, housing, water, energy, utilities and other major infrastructure, rather than allowing projects to be planned and implemented separately.
Ejercito said the government should prioritize the country’s 10 most flood-prone areas and use a 30- to 50-year framework to guide major infrastructure investments.

He said long-term planning could also strengthen accountability by giving projects clear objectives, timelines and costs and help prevent corruption by ensuring that projects form part of a coherent national plan.
Rain volume
The warnings came as Metro Manila was placed under a red rainfall warning by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) at 12:10 p.m. on Sunday.

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) said the metropolis had 186 millimeters of rain in 23 hours from 9 a.m. on Saturday to 8 a.m. on Sunday, based on data from the Pagasa Science Garden Station in Quezon City. A millimeter of rain amounts to a liter of water on a flat area.
Serious flooding remained possible in low-lying and flood-prone areas.
The MMDA said it was deploying mobile pumps, clearing clogged drains and waterways, dredging and removing debris and garbage from drainage inlets as part of its flood mitigation efforts.
Classrooms damaged
The prolonged rains have also taken a toll on schools.
The Department of Education said 9,869 classrooms had been damaged by the combined effects of the “habagat” (southwest monsoon) and tropical cyclones “Luis,” “Maymay,” “Neneng” and “Obet.”
Of the total, 5,731 classrooms sustained minor damage, 2,055 suffered major damage and 2,083 were totally damaged, according to the latest DepEd situation report as of 8 a.m. Sunday.
Central Luzon had the highest number of affected classrooms and schools, with 3,732, followed by Region I with 2,746 and the Cordillera Administrative Region with 1,266.
DepEd estimated that P280 million would be needed for minor repairs, P1 billion for major repairs and P5.2 billion for reconstruction.
At least 59 schools also experienced flooding, including 47 in Central Luzon. —WITH REPORTS FROM SHERIDAN DELFINO, TINA G. SANTOS, AND ANDREA GREGORIO

articles.title: DPWH stops Taguig reclamation projects
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders on allegedly illegal reclamation projects in Taguig City, Secretary Vince Dizon said on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) has issued cease-and-desist orders on allegedly illegal reclamation projects in Taguig City, Secretary Vince Dizon said on Sunday.
Dizon said the orders were served on Aug. 20 following a directive from the Office of the President through the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA), which is under the said office.
“Let’s just discuss and if there is any problem there, then let’s determine the way forward,” Dizon told reporters in an interview after his inspection of the Tumana pumping station in Marikina City.
He added that the orders were “effective immediately,” but he also said his agency did not yet have a list of the projects involved.
Titles questioned
“I think a meeting will be called among different stakeholders, including the City of Taguig plus [Laguna Lake Development Authority] and PRA,” Dizon said.
Earlier this month, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said an investigation by his office has found reclamation activities on Taguig City’s side of Laguna Lake covering at least 85 hectares of land.
He warned that these activities may threaten the Laguna Lake’s ecosystem as garbage meant for the Rizal provincial sanitary landfill may end up there instead.

In a series of posts on X on Saturday, Lacson disclosed that four allegedly “fraudulently” titled parcels of illegally reclaimed land in Taguig City have been identified and will be turned over to the Office of the Ombudsman for investigation.
According to Lacson, the lands cover areas ranging from 5,000 to 193,027 square meters. All four were processed through various patent and land registration procedures.
The senator said further there were four other parcels with no plotted titled lots in the Land Registration Authority’s digital records.
‘Cauldron of worms’
Lacson’s probe into Taguig’s infrastructure projects started last month, triggered by Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano’s allegations on Facebook live that his net worth had increased twofold.
Lacson fired back, saying he had no budget insertions since he was elected senator, and in turn accused Cayetano of making P6.79-billion insertions in the 2025 General Appropriations Act.
Cayetano has denied all these allegations and said Taguig had no “ghost” projects.
Earlier this month, Lacson said his probe into the Taguig projects uncovered a “cauldron of worms” to include illegal reclamation activities in Laguna Lake.

He claimed these activities, which he linked to the Cayetano political family, had been carried out for years under the guise of flood control and mitigation projects. He also alleged that Cayetano threatened the PRA to stop it from investigating the reclamation works.
He had sought the forfeiture of the reclaimed lakeshore areas in favor of the national government.

The Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya) has expressed support for the investigation into the reclamation activities, saying these were threatening Laguna Lake’s ecosystem and affecting fisherfolk and urban poor communities in Muntinlupa and Taguig cities.
Pamalakaya, a national federation of small-scale fisherfolk organizations in the Philippines, also rejected Cayetano’s claim that the projects were intended to control flooding and protect the lake.
Lacson’s office has identified 32 allegedly anomalous flood control projects in Taguig City since he started his probe. —WITH REPORTS FROM INQUIRER RESEARCH, AND PHILIPPINE NEWS AGENCY

articles.title: Hikers feared missing after flash flooding hits Grand Canyon
articles.summary: More than 20 people are thought to be unaccounted for after flash flooding on Saturday.

blocks.text: More than 20 people are thought to be missing or unaccounted for after flash flooding swept through parts of the Grand Canyon.
It hit at around 14:30 local time (22:30 BST) on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).
Sixty-two people have so far been airlifted out of the area, with more expected to follow. No injuries have been reported.
The NPS said flooding had caused significant damage in some areas and that trails in the area have been closed.

It warned that more thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were forecast for Sunday and Monday, which could lead to "additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions".
The NPS asked anyone who knew of hikers or backpackers who were in the inner canyon along the Bright Angel Creek corridor on Saturday to get in touch.
The Grand Canyon is one of the most popular national parks in the US, with about five million people visiting each year. The Bright Angel trail is its most popular hike.
The Phantom Ranch area can only be reached by foot, mule or by rafting the Colorado River, according to Grand Canyon National Park Lodges.

articles.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island in first known attack in weeks
articles.summary: Iran says the attack killed some civilians and is the first known US strike on Iran since late July.

blocks.text: Larak Island is just offshore from the key port of Bandar Abbas and sits right on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global shipping.
Iran is currently making tanker traffic pass by this island for checking and reportedly forcing vessels to pay $2m (£1.5m) to cross.

Hossein Mohebbi, the IRGC's spokesman called the attack a "strategic and fatal mistake by the Trump regime" and said that the "enemy will pay the consequences of this miscalculation in both the economic and military fields".
Iran's Tasnim news agency, which is affiliated with the IRGC, said earlier that the attack was carried out by drones. Reports indicate that two people were killed and two others injured, it said.

Trump ​said last week that all mines‌ placed in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran as part of its efforts to blockade the route had been detonated or removed. He said Iran had been warned that any ship ​or boat deploying new mines would be ​destroyed.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described Trump's claim as a "propaganda" deception.
Iran is facing renewed economic pressure after Washington announced a fresh sanctions campaign on 24 August aimed at further isolating Tehran and expanding secondary sanctions against its allies.

Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures, which they argue followed Washington's military failure in the recent conflict.

The US and Israel launched wide-ranging strikes on Iran on 28 February, with Iran responding by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to marine traffic. The Iran war has now crossed its six-month mark.
Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel through before the war began.

articles.title: USDA reportedly shelves cyclospora research amid relocations and fund cuts
articles.summary:
Trump officials shuttering three projects on foodborne parasite, two defunded by Congress, Politico reports

The Trump…

blocks.text: The Trump administration is shuttering ⁠two of the three US Department of Agriculture research projects studying cyclospora after the foodborne parasite has ⁠sickened tens of thousands of Americans during the summer, Politico reported on Sunday.

The two projects were defunded by Congress earlier in the year, while the third is ⁠due to be moved in coming months from Maryland to Iowa as part of a broader USDA reorganization, according to the ⁠report.

Although the third project remains funded, all scientists working on the ​parasite have declined to relocate ‌to Iowa, Politico reported, citing ‌people familiar with the plans and internal documents.
Reuters could not immediately ‌verify the report.
“None of the research has been disrupted, and research will continue without disruption,” a USDA spokesperson said, while pointing to Congress over the funding cuts.

Congress did not appropriate funding for the two research projects that were being undertaken at the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center ‌outside Washington DC for the 2026 fiscal year in the Agriculture Appropriations Act, the spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The spokesperson ​added that the Agricultural Research Service is working with research leaders to ensure an orderly transition of the programs.
Scientists researching foodborne parasites, including cyclospora, are retiring or leaving the USDA’s ARS rather than relocating or being reassigned to ⁠other projects, the report said.

The Centers for Disease ​Control and Prevention has ​recorded more than 17,000 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases across 48 states ​plus Washington DC, from 1 May to 24 August, making ​it one ​of the largest foodborne illness outbreaks in recent US history.
At least 11,844 additional cases may require further investigation and analysis, the CDC said.

articles.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak island amid strait of Hormuz tensions
articles.summary:
US says attack was response to ⁠Revolutionary Guards preparing rockets to launch sea mines into strait

US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran’s Larak island on Sunday, a US…

blocks.text: US forces have struck two Iranian launchers on Iran’s Larak island on Sunday, a US official said, marking the ⁠first known American strikes since late July.

“I can confirm that earlier today US forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak island. Islamic ⁠Revolutionary Guards Corps forces were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait of Hormuz,” the official said.
Iran’s ⁠Revolutionary Guards said the attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens and ​would be met with a “response ‌and punishment” from ‌Tehran, Iranian state media reported.
A spokesperson said the US would pay for the attack on both economic and military fronts, according to the semi-official news agency Fars.
Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency reported the US had carried out ‌a drone strike on the island.

US president Donald Trump said last week that all mines had been detonated or removed from the international waters of the strait of Hormuz and Iran had been told that any ship or boat placing new mines will be destroyed.
The last known ‌US strikes on Iran were in late July and the war has reached a stalemate in recent weeks, with Washington threatening ​to impose costly sanctions on countries that support Iran.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February and Iran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. The Iran war has now ⁠crossed its six-month mark.
US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on ​Lebanon have killed thousands ​and displaced millions. Eighteen US service ​members have been killed in the conflict.
The war has ​led to the ‌blockade of the ​strait of ​Hormuz, which before the conflict accounted for the transit of about a fifth of the world’s oil barrels consumed.

articles.title: 39 kg of bread dumped in park roadside in Japan
articles.summary: JAPAN — A total of 39 kilograms of bread was recently dumped along a roadside in a national park in western Japan, prompting police to investigate who discarded it and why. The loaves were left near…

blocks.text: JAPAN — A total of 39 kilograms of bread was recently dumped along a roadside in a national park in western Japan, prompting police to investigate who discarded it and why.

The loaves were left near guardrails in Daisen-Oki National Park in Tottori Prefecture between Aug. 14 and 20. The incident has prompted the spread of fake images and videos attempting to link the dumping to a sharp increase in bear encounters in Japan over the past year.
“When I first heard of the reports, my head was full of question marks,” said Koji Iwaihara, director of the Natural Parks Foundation’s Tottori branch.
The bread was initially believed to have been used as bait for cameras livestreaming images of animals, but no such equipment was found.
The foundation later came to believe the bread had been left to feed animals after 1.3 kilograms of chicken was found in the same area.
Bear bait?
Bread was also found scattered around the prefecture’s Hakuto coast, but the brand appears to be different from that found in the national park.
Neither the bread nor the chicken was poisoned.
The prefecture has since installed security cameras in Daisen-Oki National Park, but no further dumping has been reported.

“I don’t understand why it was left on the side of the road” as opposed to inside the mountain, said Tottori Gov. Shinji Hirai, questioning the theory that the food may have been placed there as bear bait.
If that really is the aim, “it may become a dangerous precedent as bears become accustomed to the taste of bread,” he added.
Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated videos and images showing a bear looking at or eating the bread have spread on social media.
The prefectural government plans to ask social media platforms to remove them over concerns the false content could cause reputational damage.
Prefectural police said the perpetrator may have violated a law against illegal dumping or regulations governing national parks. /cb

articles.title: All-time great Aaron Donald comes out of retirement to rejoin stacked LA Rams
articles.summary:
• Los Angeles were already Super Bowl favorites

  • Defensive tackle was 10-time Pro Bowler with Rams

  • 35-year-old aiming to win second Super Bowl in…

blocks.text: Aaron Donald, one of the greatest defensive players in NFL history, is coming out of retirement to rejoin his only professional team, the Los Angeles Rams.

During a 10-season career with the Rams, who drafted him with the 13th overall pick in 2014, Donald was a three-time defensive player of the year and an eight-time first team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl with the Rams at the end of the 2021 season before announcing his retirement in March 2024 at the age of 32.

The 35-year-old returns to a stacked Rams roster who were already betting favorites to win the Super Bowl this season. The team includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford at quarterback and the reigning defensive player of the year, Myles Garrett, who Los Angeles acquired in a trade with the Cleveland Browns in June.
ESPN reports that Donald will earn $20m in his one-year deal, which could rise to $30m with bonuses.

Rumors had circulated that Donald would return after the trade for Garrett. If Donald can replicate anything close to the form he showed during his peak – when he was arguably the greatest defensive tackle of all time – he will form part of a formidable line with Garrett, who set the NFL single-season sack record in 2025.

Donald, who was listed at 6ft 1in and 280 lbs when he retired, is small for a defensive tackle but during his first spell with the Rams he made up for his lack of size with his extraordinary athleticism and work rate. He ended his career with a franchise record 111 sacks.

If the Rams do reach the Super Bowl this season, they will play on home turf at SoFi Stadium, the venue for their championship victory in February 2022. The Rams start their season on 10 September against their NFC West rivals, the San Francisco 49ers.

articles.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard vows retaliation after U.S. bombs targets in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster noted "the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots" after the U.S. bombed targets in…

image.caption: An Iranian flag is shown near Larak Island, Iran, in the Strait of Hormuz on May 16. (Majid Saeedi/Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster noted "the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots" after the U.S. bombed targets in the Strait of Hormuz.
Official says U.S. targeted rocket launchers; IRGC reports several casualties
U.S. forces have struck Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz in the first military action in a month, an American official said Sunday.
Semi-official news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak Island on the strait.

Forces with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military movements.
The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait's international shipping routes.
The IRGC in a statement carried by Iran's state broadcaster noted "the martyrdom and injury of several of our fighters and compatriots."
The statement said the attack will "result in punishment of the aggressor."

articles.title: NASA launches $4B Roman astronomical observatory to explore depths of space
articles.summary: NASA began a new mission to probe some of the biggest mysteries in astrophysics and cosmology with the launch on Sunday of the U.S. space agency's new flagship astronomical observatory, a repurposed…

image.caption: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket lifts off carrying NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., Sunday. (Joe Skipper/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

NASA began a new mission to probe some of the biggest mysteries in astrophysics and cosmology with the launch on Sunday of the U.S. space agency's new flagship astronomical observatory, a repurposed spy satellite that will capture panoramic ‌views of the cosmos.
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a repurposed spy satellite, will capture panoramic views

The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a roughly $4 billion US project, was carried aloft from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket through blue skies just after sunrise. Its mission is planned for five years, though NASA said the telescope may have enough fuel for five additional years.

The telescope, which will park itself in orbit beyond the moon, is designed to investigate cosmic enigmas such as dark energy and dark matter, while also testing gravity at vast scales and searching ​for exoplanets, as planets beyond our solar system are called.

Sunday's launch marked "an endpoint for the engineers, but it's ​a starting point for the scientists," Julie McEnery, Roman telescope senior project scientist, told reporters at a post-launch news conference. "It feels like I'm on the edge of a precipice, and we're just about to set a foot off into the unknown."

The observatory was originally designed for a spy satellite program under the National Reconnaissance ​Office, a part of the U.S. intelligence community that manages the most powerful American spy satellites. That program was over budget and terminated, and the NRO ⁠in 2012 donated it to NASA, which repurposed it ⁠for cosmic exploration.

items: NASA is launching the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Here are just a few of the wonders it will reveal

blocks.text: Roman will travel through space toward an orbital location called Lagrange Point 2, about 1.6 million kilometres from Earth.
The Roman telescope is named after NASA's first chief astronomer, also known as the "mother of the Hubble Space Telescope."

Mission scientists will spend the next 90 days commissioning it and preparing for its science operations. Roman is expected to beam back its first high-resolution images "before the winter holidays," Roman telescope project manager Jackie Townsend said.
Roman will be 'household name': NASA
Roman will build on the capabilities of other orbiting observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, and the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990.
"I have no doubt that Roman will become a household name alongside those great instruments of ⁠discovery," NASA administrator Jared Isaacman told reporters.

McEnery has said that Roman possesses broadly the same sensitivity and sharpness of vision as Hubble, but will survey the cosmos more quickly. Roman can survey our entire Milky Way galaxy in a month while Hubble would need a century, according to McEnery.
During Sunday's news conference, Isaacman took a call from U.S. President Donald Trump and put the phone speaker up to his microphone. Trump said ‌the launch "looked beautiful on television."

items: NASA will no longer attempt to save its aging Swift space telescope
Our Milky Way galaxy gobbled up a smaller galaxy about 11.8 billion years ago, scientists find

blocks.text: "You are doing a fantastic job, and I'm supplying you all that money," Trump said, referring to NASA's approximately $24 billion 2026 budget, which survived an earlier White House proposal to cut the agency's funding by about $6 billion.

Trump's administration tried during both his first and second terms as president to cancel Roman or reduce its funding, but Congress preserved it. Its launch came nine months ahead of schedule, according to NASA.
Dark energy and dark matter

Webb has provided a new understanding of the universe's early history, finding among other things ​that primordial galaxies formed sooner and were bigger than previously known. Webb can look across vast distances and back into deep time, because of the time it takes light to travel.
Roman instead is able to take panoramic views. NASA likens Roman to a camera's wide-angle lens ⁠and Webb to a zoom lens.

"Webb is designed to be able to probe very deeply and with exquisite sensitivity into the universe, so we can find rare things in the early ⁠universe," McEnery told an earlier briefing, while Roman offers "the large vision that complements the deep views that Webb provides."

Roman will help in the understanding of two mysterious cosmic components — dark energy and ⁠dark matter — ⁠by creating the most comprehensive 3D map of the universe to date. Its ​main survey, to take more than a year to complete, will cover more than two billion galaxies.

The Big Bang event roughly 13.8 billion years ago initiated the universe, and it has been expanding ever ​since. This expansion is accelerating, with an invisible force called ⁠dark energy as the hypothesized reason.
Why scientists are racing to study the SpaceX rocket piece believed to have slammed into the moon

The universe's contents include ordinary matter — stars, planets, gas, dust and all the familiar stuff on Earth — as well as dark matter and dark energy. Ordinary matter represents perhaps five per cent of the contents. Dark matter, known through its gravitational influences on galaxies and stars, may represent about 27 per cent. Dark energy may represent about 68 per cent.
Using Roman to gauge dark matter's pull and dark energy's push across the universe will bring scientists closer than ever before to solving both mysteries, according to NASA.

Roman also will conduct one of the most comprehensive searches ever for exoplanets. It is expected to discover thousands of new ones and provide ⁠the first statistical census of planetary systems similar to our ‌own.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: Fact check: Germany's Merz misstates record in ARD interview
articles.summary: Migration, debt and electric vehicles: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made several misleading claims in his ARD summer interview. DW Fact check reviewed them live.

image.caption: Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke with ARD's Markus Preiss in this year's summer interviewImage: dts-Agentur/picture alliance

blocks.text: As part of an annual tradition, Chancellor Friedrich Merz sat down with public broadcaster ARD on Sunday evening for a wide-ranging summer interview. Amid drooping poll numbers, Merz tried to use the interview to tout his government's work on economic, migration and energy policy.
At the same time, Merz made a number of misleading claims, often overstating his administration's work and misrepresenting climate science.
DW Fact check, in collaboration with colleagues across the ARD fact-checking network, reviewed Merz's interview live.

blocks.caption: Asylum applications have dropped sharply, but not by 60% as Merz claimedImage: Joko/IMAGO

blocks.text: Did Merz cut asylum numbers by 60%?

Claim: "One of the main issues in the last federal election campaign was the migration crisis, and together with the federal government, we've been able to reduce the numbers by over 60% in just over a year."
Verdict: Misleading
This is misleading for several reasons — it is both questionable what exactly Merz meant by migration, and also not clear to which period he is referring.

The number of asylum-seekers in Germany has fallen significantly, but not to the extent Merz said. According to the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF), a total of 56,547 asylum applications were filed in the first half of 2026, including 39,646 first-time applications. Compared with the same period last year, the number of first-time applications fell by 35.4%.
In July 2026, the number of first-time asylum applications was 4,311, around 48% below the figure for the same month last year.

To reach 60%, Merz was likely referencing a figure that compares initial applications from August 2025 to the same month a year prior. That decline, is indeed, 58%, close to what Merz stated. But a more complete comparison of January through August 2025 to the prior year shows just a 51% decline.

In addition, the downward trend began even before the Merz government took office in May 2025. After the fall of Syrian ruler Bashar Assad in December 2024, the number of asylum-seekers in Germany declined. At the European level, the number of asylum applications also fell in the first half of 2025.

Official statistics also show a decline in general migration. According to the Federal Statistical Office, around 235,000 more people immigrated to Germany in 2025 than emigrated. This means that net immigration was 45% below the previous year's figure of 430,000 people. But that's mostly due to the number of arrivals falling, while the number of departures remained almost stable.

blocks.caption: Merz cast his vote for a historic amendment to Germany's debt brake in March 2025, ahead of taking officeImage: MICHAEL KAPPELER/AFP

blocks.text: Germany's debt, in context

Claim: "We are still one of the least indebted countries in Europe. We are still a country that has by far the best credit rating of any European nation. No one doubts the debt sustainability of our country or our economy; we are operating within reasonable limits here."
There are three important ways to measure how much debt EU countries hold: debt-to-GDP ratio, deficit spending and credit rating.

On the first — debt-to-GDP ratio, or how a country's total debt compares to its annual economic output — Germany receives a failing grade. The eurozone requires countries to keep this ratio below 60%. Germany and 11 other countries are above that limit, versus 15 countries which are in compliance, putting Germany smack in the middle of the eurozone.

On the second — government deficits, or a country's net borrowing — Germany is just scraping by. The eurozone asks its members to keep this figure below 3%. Germany's net borrowing is at 2.7%, joining 16 other countries that are also below the limit. Of the 17 countries that meet that requirement, Germany comes the second closest to hitting the 3% limit.

As for credit rating — a grade from investors on how likely a country is to repay its debts — Germany does indeed earn the highest marks possible. But it shares that grade with several other countries. There are only 11 countries in the world with an AAA rating from S&P: Germany joins Denmark, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and Switzerland in earning the grade.

In 2009, Germany amended its constitution by adding a so-called "debt brake," mandating the government to keep deficits to 0.35% of GDP. In 2020, that restriction was suspended to deal with the COVID pandemic and then again in 2022 and 2025 to allow for an increase in defense spending.

blocks.caption: Merz claimed the CO2 balance of electric vehicles is often overstated — but the data tells a different storyImage: MiS/IMAGO

blocks.text: Real CO2 balance of electric cars

Claim: "At the European level, the issue with internal combustion engines has nothing to do with CO2 emissions. We want climate-friendly and climate-neutral cars, but we don't want to dictate the technology — it's not up to politicians to decide that. What matters is how much CO2 such a car emits, and the CO2 balance of electric mobility isn't as rosy as it's often portrayed."

Battery electric vehicles produce, on average, 73% less CO2 emissions than internal combustion engine vehicles, according to the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT), a US-based nonprofit think tank.

Battery electric vehicles do generate about 40% higher production emissions, mostly because of the processes involved in manufacturing the battery, though these are usually offset after about one or two years of driving.

Merz was likely referring to a new paper from researchers at the Technical University of Munich, which right-wing media seized on this week. The paper, which took an average of 19 studies, claimed that battery electric vehicles only reduce CO2 emissions by 41%, compared to traditional cars.

But there's a key issue with the TUM paper: including all those studies means older analyses with outdated electricity mixes are given equal weight. The ICCT analysis, on the other hand, uses a more current estimate.
Either way, there's an overwhelming scientific consensus that electric vehicles are better for the environment than traditional cars.
Is Germany's weak economy boosting the right-wing AfD?

articles.title: Trump ‘border czar’ denies that Milo Yiannopoulos was deported for political reasons
articles.summary:
Tom Homan says rightwing influencer overstayed visitor visa after receiving final order of removal

The White House “border czar,” Tom Homan, denied on Sunday that the British far-right…

blocks.text: The White House “border czar,” Tom Homan, denied on Sunday that the British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos was deported just a day after being arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for political reasons.

Homan said it was his understanding that Yiannopoulos, 41, had overstayed what he believed to be a visitor visa, had not appeared at an immigration hearing and was issued a final order of removal on 22 July.

“He didn’t show up,” Homan told CNN’s State of the Union. “The judge ordered him deported. So, once ICE gets an order of deportation from a federal judge, their job is to execute that order, and that’s what they did.”
He added: “He had his due process, ordered removed by a federal judge, and ICE removed him. It’s that simple.”

Yiannopoulos’s removal one day after his arrest, when many others who have been deported had first endured lengthy detention center incarcerations, has prompted questions about whether he received preferential treatment in that respect. Homan said the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, was trying to speed up the deportation process.

“Once a judge orders them out, rather than being in detention, waiting for travel documents and flight arrangements, we – ICE, along with the [border patrol] and [DHS] – [are] working really good on the efficiencies of the removal process,” Homan remarked.
He continued: “As soon as we get an order removal, our goal is remove them as quick as possible, regardless of who they are. Get them out quick. Open those beds up for more detainees.”

DHS had quickly publicized Yiannopoulos’s arrest on Thursday at an airport in New Orleans – where he may have travelled to attend a concert by rapper Ye, formerly Kanye West, on Friday at the city’s Caesars Superdome.

Officials with DHS touted Yiannopoulos’s arrest on Friday. By Saturday morning, Yiannopoulos’s name was removed from a list of people in ICE detention, and DHS confirmed that he had been deported to the UK on Friday – one day after his arrest.

“He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws,” a DHS release said, adding “The administration is working diligently to ensure that aliens in our country illegally can no longer fly unless it is out of our country to self-deport”.
CNN host Dana Bash asked Homan if the rightwing influencer Laura Loomer had, as she claimed, tipped off ICE that Yiannopoulos’s permission to be in the US had expired.
“A lot of people tipped ICE off,” Homan replied. “There are a lot of people who’s calling ICE, and she says she’s one of them. She probably was.
“But bottom line is, it doesn’t matter. He was ordered removed by an immigration judge, and ICE’s job it to execute that order.”
Loomer and Yiannopoulos – who had sanguinely cheered the Trump administration’s deportation efforts before his expulsion from the US – had publicly fallen out.
Homan, meanwhile, denied that the Trump administration had made an example of Yiannopoulos to send a message. “We don’t deport people based on political affiliation,” he said.

articles.title: Nasa launches new space telescope able to see 100 times more than Hubble
articles.summary: The US space agency's telescope is starting a multi-year mission to create a new map of the universe and learn more about dark energy and dark matter.

blocks.text: The successful launch of the telescope took place on Sunday morning local time from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

"What a glorious dawn launch," Jackie Townsend, a project manager on Nasa's Roman telescope, said at the news conference after liftoff. "The ride was magnificent. It put us right where we wanted to be."
About 30 minutes after launch, Roman separated from its SpaceX rocket and is now heading towards its orbiting point around a million miles away.

Astronomer Jenifer Millard said the telescope will be four times further from Earth than the Moon is, where a lot of infrared space cameras - made to pick up what she describes as "heat light"- operate.
She told the BBC this is to make sure infrared light from the Moon and Earth don't interfere with the cameras.

Nasa's James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, also orbits the Sun around one million miles from Earth, but its field of vision is not as expansive. Nasa's Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, orbits at about 300 miles above Earth's surface.
While Roman will look outward into the Universe, Millard said scientists are also anticipating it will find thousands of new worlds in our own galaxy.

Nasa says its "crisp, sweeping surveys will help scientists investigate dark energy and dark matter, discover and characterise exoplanets, map billions of galaxies, study black holes, and explore objects from our own solar system to the edge of the observable Universe."

Dark matter, which is invisible, acts as a kind of gravitational glue, while dark energy is believed to be a repulsive force driving the Universe's expansion. Together, they are thought to make up about 95% of the Universe.
"One of our main goals at Nasa is answering the question: are we alone in the Universe?" Fox said at a Sunday morning news conference.

"With Roman, we are going to make this giant leap forward... that is going to allow us to look at these distant, distant worlds and start to really resolve the atmosphere around them to let us know: could they be habitable?"
Millard said, through the work of telescopes like Roman, scientists are hoping to create "enormous cosmic maps" of the Universe at various stages.
"They'll be almost like an onion, so you can peel back layer upon layer... and see how the distribution of galaxies changes through cosmic time," she said.
"What we want to do is use this distribution to try and figure out dark matter and dark energy because we know they exist, we see their effects, but what they are is a real mystery."

articles.title: Prisons ‘one major event from disaster’ after U-turn on early release scheme
articles.summary:
Critics say the move, which will keep PC Harper’s killers in jail, leaves number of prison spaces ‘too close to the bone’

PC Andrew Harper’s killers will remain behind bars after a critical…

blocks.text: PC Andrew Harper’s killers will remain behind bars after a critical intervention by Andy Burnham, but the move has led to warnings that overcrowded prisons will be left “one major event away from disaster”.
Announcing a U-turn on the early release scheme after weeks of intense pressure, Burnham said he understood “how strongly people feel about this issue”.
The prime minister’s intervention will prevent the early release of offenders guilty of all forms of manslaughter, as well as rapists, child sexual abusers and groomers.
The decision, which affects about 1,400 prisoners, was welcomed by police, victims’ groups and families, including qualified support from Harper’s mother, Debbie Adlam.

But critics said the change could undermine progressive prison reforms in England and Wales. They said the steps Burnham outlined to free up space would take longer to bring into force, putting the orderly management of prisons at risk.

Harper was 28 when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire in August 2019. Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the vehicle and both 17 at the time, were sentenced to 13 years in custody for manslaughter.

blocks.caption: Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were each jailed for 13 years over the killing of PC Harper, had been eligible for early release under the Sentencing Act until Burnham’s intervention.  Photograph: Thames Valley police/PA

blocks.text: Speaking to the BBC, which first reported the government U-turn on Sunday, Burnham said he had “heard” Harper’s family.

“I heard, obviously, what Andrew Harper’s family were saying,” he said. “I mean, who couldn’t? Nobody would want a position to arise where those guilty of killing a police officer are let out early from prison.”
Adlam said she was glad and grateful for the change in the new law but felt “a mixed bag of emotions” and campaigning for the change had been traumatic.

“On the one hand we are glad, but we’ve been [put] through the mill and we are only back at where we were to start with,” she told BBC Breakfast. “We’re not making any headway or anything, we are just literally fighting to get back to where we were.”
Harper’s force, Thames Valley police, said the news would be “welcomed by many across policing and our communities”.

Jason Hogg, the chief constable of the force, said: “Today is not about politics. It is about remembering Andrew, recognising the profound impact his death continues to have on those who knew him, the communities he protected and those who serve in policing today.”
Burnham’s 11th-hour intervention will limit the number of places that can be freed up in the prison estate, which ministers have repeatedly warned is on the brink of collapse.

Before the early prison release scheme that had been due to start this week, the prime minister said spaces would be made available by deporting foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.
But critics warned neither measure would free up sufficient space in a system that is operating at 98% capacity in England and Wales.

Up to 6,000 prisoners were due to have their sentences cut short under the new law, but government figures suggest the number will now be about 4,600. With the first batch of prisoners due to be released early in October, prison governor representatives said staff would be put under intense pressure.

“The truth is I wanted to go even further,” said Burnham. “But I’ve pushed the system to the very limits of what’s possible without risking the prison system collapsing within months, putting the public at enormous risk.”
Nicole Jacobs, the domestic abuse commissioner for England and Wales, said Sunday’s announcement would not bring reassurance to domestic abuse victims.
“Victims and survivors will still be forced to take measures to protect themselves from dangerous abusers because the government and our criminal justice system cannot,” she said.

Sources accused the prime minister of making a “politically easy decision” and warned that multiple governments had failed to deport foreign convicts. Burnham admitted the number that could be returned was in the “hundreds”.
The prime minister’s pledge to “end the injustice” of indefinite jail terms (IPPs) in this parliament was hailed as “a day that thousands of families have spent years fighting for”.

But prison experts said it would be complicated, take time and would be unlikely to free up many places in the short term. IPPs were abolished more than a decade ago but still keep more than 2,000 people in England and Wales behind bars.
“The decision to release people on IPPs is extremely welcome, but the government must now deliver it,” said Andrea Coomber, the chief executive of the Howard League, a penal reform charity.
She said Sunday’s announcement left the prison estate “one major incident away from a disaster”.

“All it will take is something like a serious riot or public disturbance and any capacity will be gone,” she added. “It is just too close to the bone and the government will be left with very little room to manoeuvre.”

She said the move threatened to undermine changes to the Sentencing Act, which were brought forward after a review led by David Gauke, a former justice secretary, and were designed to improve rehabilitation rates as well as freeing up spaces for people coming into the system.

“The Sentencing Act changes were based on deep work over a year from the independent sentencing review, the government and civil servants, with parliamentary scrutiny of the legislation,” said Coomber. “Today’s announcement has undone some of that work.”
Pia Sinha, the chief executive of the Prison Reform Trust, said the government should address the number of people on remand awaiting trial, which account for 18% of those in prison.
“If prisons are full they become warehouses – you can’t deliver interventions, self-harm goes up and rehabilitation goes down,” she said.
“The Gauke reforms were not a magic bullet, but they were brave and they were an investment in the future. That progress must not be lost.”

Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary, accused Labour of avoiding parliamentary scrutiny of the changes. “The government must delay the scheme, bring forward emergency primary legislation and exclude the worst offenders properly,” he said.

articles.title: Man killed by falling sign at Christian festival named as church pays tribute
articles.summary:
Robert Guanco, 41, a pastor at Jesus Living Water church in Eastbourne, described as having ‘touched many lives’

A 41-year-old man

blocks.text: A 41-year-old man who died after a large wooden sign fell at a Christian festival on Friday has been named as Robert Guanco, a pastor at a church in Eastbourne, East Sussex.
A tribute from his church on Sunday described him as a respected pastor who was a “loving husband” and “a devoted and caring father”.
Six other people were injured when the overhead sign fell at the Big Church festival (BCF) near Steyning in West Sussex, including four who were taken to hospital.
Festivalgoers said they rushed to lift the heavy sign, which read “Everything’s Unmissable”, after it was blown over in the wind.

Jesus Living Water church in Eastbourne named Guanco, describing him as “our beloved brother, friend and pastor”, in a GoFundMe to help his family, who it said faced “unimaginable loss” following his death.

It said: “Pastor Robert was a faithful servant of God, a loving husband to Isay, a devoted and caring father to Ellie, and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched. His life, his faith, his love and his service to God will never be forgotten.”

It added: “He was also a good friend, mentor and a blessing to so many people whose lives he touched. His life reflected humility, faith, love, compassion and service. Through his ministry, kindness, prayers and encouragement, he touched many lives.
“His passing is deeply felt by everyone who had the privilege of knowing him.”

blocks.caption: Organisers of the Big Church festival said they were ‘heartbroken’ by Guanco’s death. Photograph: Bigchurchfestival

blocks.text: Organisers of the BCF, billed as the UK’s biggest Christian festival, said they were “heartbroken” by Guanco’s death and cancelled the rest of the event.
“We are devastated by the serious incident that took place at Big Church festival 2026, in which Pastor Robert Guanco tragically lost his life and others were injured,” they said in a statement.

“First and foremost, all of our thoughts are with those who have been affected, their families and friends, and everyone who witnessed what happened. Particularly with the family, friends and church of Pastor Guanco as they process the immense grief of his loss.”
They added: “We are working with the police, the Health and Safety Executive and others as they establish the circumstances surrounding the incident,” they added.
The festival opened on Friday and had been due to run until Sunday. The event, which includes worship, music and various performances, first took place in 2009.

The archbishop of Canterbury, Dame Sarah Mullally, said she was “sad and shocked” by the incident. “I pray for his family, friends and loved ones as they grieve,” she said. “I pray for those receiving treatment and the healthcare workers looking after them.
“And I pray too for the other festivalgoers, staff and event organisers as they come to terms with these tragic events.”
Many people at the festival were first alerted to the tragedy when God TV announced that “due to unforeseen circumstances” the festival live stream had been paused.
Sussex police’s Det Ch Supt Richard McDonagh said: “Our thoughts remain with the family and friends of the man who died and all others who have been affected by this tragic incident.”
He urged anyone among the “thousands of people” at the festival on Friday who had information or video footage to come forward.

articles.title: ‘GB News wouldn’t touch him’: Milo Yiannopoulos will struggle to fit in with UK right wing
articles.summary:
‘Alt-right’ agitator and former Trump backer deported from US is said also to be too extreme for Reform

As he arrives back in the UK after being deported from the US by the Trump…

blocks.text: As he arrives back in the UK after being deported from the US by the Trump administration, the far-right provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos may be wondering what lies ahead for him in his native country.
The “alt-right” agitator, 41, made his name in the US by promoting Donald Trump and associating with his allies before the 2016 election.

But now the Trump administration has unceremoniously dumped the former Breitbart News editor back in the UK after he allegedly overstayed his visa. He has also made plenty of disparaging comments about the president, including that he is “firmly off the Trump train”.
Those in the rightwing ecosystem in the UK say Yiannopoulos is now too extreme to find a prominent berth back home.

The commentator started his career at the Daily Telegraph, where he wrote a controversial blog until 2011, when he started his own website, the Kernel. In 2014 he started working for the former Trump adviser Steve Bannon at Breitbart News, before moving to the US and promoting far-right causes.

He left Breitbart after a controversy over a video in which he appeared to condone sexual relations with boys as young as 13. He later said “sloppy editing” and his “British sarcasm, provocation and gallows humour” had created the wrong impression and denied endorsing paedophilia.

Since he left the UK, GB News has become the ascendant broadcast outlet of the right, but he is unlikely to find a place there. A source at the channel said: “We wouldn’t touch him with a barge pole, not in a million years. GBN had a few odd people to start with and we’ve got rid of them.”

blocks.caption: Yiannopoulos after his arrest by federal immigration agents in New Orleans. Photograph: Department of Homeland Security/Reuters

blocks.text: Of the provocative positions that brought him notoriety in the US, the GB News source said: “He won’t make much money out of it here, he appeals entirely to an American audience. It’s a bigger country and you have a bigger pool of fruit loops.”

There is a growing subsection of rightwing provocateurs in the UK who have been deemed too controversial for the main channels but have established niche brands of their own. The journalist Dan Wootton was suspended from GB News after a guest on his show made sexually inappropriate comments about a female journalist, and after leaving he now has his own channel.

The former TalkTV host Mike Graham has also set up his own independent show. He was sacked after the company said he had failed to cooperate with an investigation into a racist post that appeared on one of his social media accounts. Graham said the racist comment had been the result of his account being hacked.

It is understood that Reform UK will not accept him into its ranks. His former colleague at Breitbart, Raheem Kassam, is close to the party’s leader, Nigel Farage, and is in the UK for Reform’s national conference.
Kassam, who is British but now lives in the US, claimed he was kept updated on the deportation of Yiannopoulos, who he accused of making “lurid and false accusations” against him.
He added: “I got word last month that he was about to be deported. On Thursday night, I got a call. As overly dramatic as it may seem. ‘We got him. In Louisiana.’”
The Maga influencer Laura Loomer has claimed to have reported Yiannopoulos to immigration enforcement over his expired visa.

blocks.caption: Laura Loomer (front, centre) celebrates with Yiannopoulos at a congressional primary election night event in West Palm Beach, Florida, in August 2020.  Photograph: Allen Eyestone/AP

blocks.text: One political party that may accept Yiannopoulos is Restore Britain, which is led by Rupert Lowe, a former Reform MP who had a falling-out with Farage.
Restore has accepted a number of characters viewed as too extreme for Reform, including the convicted criminal Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson.

Yiannopoulos has praised Lowe, calling him “fantastic” and urging those on the UK hard-right to join Restore. He said “the rising generation of young British activists” all “support Restore” and has taunted Reform’s home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, online, telling him “you’re gonna lose all your votes to Rupert”. The Guardian contacted Lowe to ask whether he would accept Yiannopoulos as a party member or adviser but did not receive a response.
Kassam said: “He’s certain to resurface in Britain shortly. Perhaps as an adviser to Rupert Lowe, or perhaps as a contestant on some third-tier reality TV show.”

Yiannopoulos used to have more political influence; he was offered a speaking slot at the Conservative Political Action Conference, or CPAC, in 2017 after he had been supportive of Donald Trump during his run for his first presidency.

He was deported to the UK on Friday, according to US authorities. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said Yiannopoulos “legally entered the country” in May 2019 through New York City but then “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.
In 2022, Yiannopoulos worked on Kanye West’s short-lived 2024 White House campaign, and his social media account suggests he was working one of the rapper’s companies.
Last year, Yiannopoulos said he was “never going back home” because the UK needed a “mass deportation programme”.
Yiannopoulos was approached for comment.

articles.title: Trump says NBC’s Kristen ‌Welker should face ‘punishment’ from FCC
articles.summary:
Trump’s threat comes after host described success record of candidates whom president had endorsed as ‘mixed’

Donald Trump ⁠on…

blocks.text: Donald Trump ⁠on Sunday said NBC’s Kristen ‌Welker – host of Meet the Press – should face “rebuke or punishment” from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

Preceding Trump’s comments was a live shot by Welker in which she described the success record of political candidates whom president had endorsed as “mixed” on Washington DC’s NBC affiliate prior to the airing of Sunday’s edition of Meet the Press, according to CNN media reporter and commentator Brian Stelter.

The president then took verbal aim at Welker with a social media post deriding her as the “Unpopular ‘Hostess’ of … Meet the Fake Press,” accused her of “purposeful inaccuracy” and warned that she would “be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment”.
The post also said that Trump hoped his appointed FCC chair Brendan Carr – and Carr’s colleagues on the commission – “take this Threat to our Country very seriously”.

Once Meet the Press actually started on Sunday, a guest analyst on the show said “the single most important factor in who the Republican nominee will be in [the presidential election of] 2028 will be who Donald Trump endorses”.

Trump is estimated to have made more than 300 endorsements that resulted in the recipient winning. In the election cycle leading up to November’s midterms, 214 of the 218 House candidates he endorsed winning their primaries, including all 24 Republican senate primaries.

Meanwhile, in gubernatorial primaries, five of the 21 candidates he endorsed lost their primaries, among them Mike Lindell – who finished a distant second in Minnesota to state house speaker Lisa Demuth.
The state’s supreme court on Saturday effectively confirmed Lindell’s 11-percentage-point defeat by rejecting his bid for a recount.
“My Endorsements are stronger than ever,” Trump nonetheless maintained in a 23 August social media post. “There has never been anything close!”

When taking aim on Welker on Sunday, he touted recent primary victories by South Carolina US Senate candidate Darline Graham – sister of the late senator Lindsey Graham – and Oklahoma gubernatorial hopeful Mike Mazzei.
He had said days earlier that any of his endorsed candidates who lost were already faced with “impossible” races – but they had earned his support “out of loyalty”.

How much power Trump’s endorsement carries has been a touchy issue for the president. On Friday, HBO Max talkshow host Bill Maher apologized to Trump for claiming that the president is winning “almost none of” his endorsements. Trump had sent Maher statistics making the president’s case that the talkshow host was wrong.

Welker and Trump have a contentious relationship. In June, he walked out of an hour-long interview with the host after being asked, among other unpleasant topics for him, about having pledged “no new wars” during his successful run for a second presidency.
He started war in Iran in late February alongside Israel, and Trump denied guaranteeing there would no wars if he were returned to the Oval Office.
“You’re a one-sided crooked network,” Trump said at the time. “Let’s call it quits because I’ve had enough. Thank you, darling. Have a good time.”
He added: “You ought to straighten out your press. A country can never be great with a dishonest press.”
Trump’s comments on Sunday about Welker were only the latest instance of him or his administration seeking to bring the weight of the FCC down on media outlets with whom he has become cross.

In September 2025, Carr – appointed by Trump – reportedly put pressure on television station groups to pre-empt Jimmy Kimmel’s show as punishment for a comment that the ABC host, a frequent critic of the president, made in the wake of the assassination of conservative influencer Charlie Kirk. Two conservative-friendly broadcast groups, Sinclair and Nexstar, did so. And ABC opted to “indefinitely” pull Kimmel’s show before he ultimately returned to the air a week later.
Trump has also won private settlements from ABC and CBS totaling more than $30m during his second presidency.

Earlier in August, ABC sued the FCC, arguing that it was being illegally targeted by the regulator after being forced to apply early to renew its eight local broadcast licenses. Among Republicans’ complaints about ABC are that its candidates are not given equal airtime on the daytime talkshow The View.

“Acting through the Federal Communications Commission, the Administration has waged a retaliatory campaign against ABC for a single reason: it disapproves of what ABC broadcasts,” the network said in its lawsuit.
NBC is licensed by the FCC to directly operate 11 local stations. The network did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Involving itself in broadcast outlets’ editorial decisions and constitutionally protected speech is beyond the mandate of the FCC, which was established in 1934.

Stelter on Sunday wrote that the FCC “can’t punish Welker” because it has “limited power … by design”. But Stelter noted that Carr has been “responsive” to Trump in the past – and “it’s reasonable to think NBC will be targeted next”.
