articles.title: Headteacher saves 900 children from deadly flash flood in Nepal
articles.summary:
Rajendra Dawadi ordered students to higher ground with moments to spare after receiving warnings from upstream

A headteacher in Nepal evacuated 900 children from a school moments before a…

blocks.text: A headteacher in Nepal evacuated 900 children from a school moments before a deadly wall of water struck their town amid the devastating flash floods that have killed almost 800 people and left thousands missing.
Rajendra Dawadi decided to halt classes and order children to higher ground after receiving warnings about the scale of the flooding heading their way.

Dawadi, the headteacher at Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school in Nuwakot, which has 1,600 pupils, said he had received four warnings from different people within minutes, including one from Betrawati, a town directly upstream.

blocks.caption: Rajendra Dawadi, the headteacher of Tribhuvan Trishuli secondary school in Nuwakot

blocks.text: This prompted him to take immediate action. “I decided I shouldn’t delay any more,” he told the BBC. “Even if the flood was not coming, it was just a matter of a single day’s classes.”
Dawadi said during the evacuation of the school he saw a hostel building about 100 metres from the river being engulfed by the torrent of flood water.
“If we had made the decision 10 minutes later, all of us, including the students and me, would not be able to speak to you today,” he said.
One student said Dawadi’s decision had saved their lives with moments to spare. Yunisha, 16, told reporters: “I, along with my friends, survived by just 10 seconds.”

She described the children running up a muddy path to escape as water and debris inundated the town. “Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes,” she said. She was reunited with her family three days later.
At least 69 schools have been destroyed or damaged by the floods, affecting nearly 19,000 children, according to the charity Save the Children.
In Dhading, one of the areas worst hit by the floods, a group of schoolchildren survived the disaster when they left their classroom for their lunch break.
Others in the area escaped when teachers told them to quickly evacuate classrooms just before the waters came crashing in.
The mother of one child told the Associated Press that teachers had warned students: “There is a flood and you should leave bags and tiffins. That’s how they managed to survive.”
More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far. The country said on Sunday 2,502 people, including 592 foreigners, were out of contact. It reported an updated death toll of 781 people.

The disaster, which struck the Nepal-Tibet border region of the Himalayas on Wednesday morning, was caused by a glacial collapse that sent a wall of water and debris cascading downstream, the US Geological Survey said.

Nepal’s foreign minister has called for a global response to the climate crisis, saying the Nepali people had disproportionately become “major victims of climate change” despite having contributed a fraction of the planet’s fossil fuel emissions.

articles.title: Fifteen Britons among 261 foreigners missing in China after floods
articles.summary: Total number of missing Britons between Tibet and Nepal at 48 as Beijing mobilises more than 2,100 rescue workers

blocks.text: Fifteen British nationals are reported to be missing in China as the search continues for survivors of the devastating flooding in Nepal and Tibet.

Nepali and Chinese authorities confirmed an updated death toll of at least 810 on Sunday. More than 3,000 people are believed missing after flash floods brought upon by a massive glacier collapse in the Himalayas on Wednesday engulfed Gyirong port on the Nepal-China border.

The 15 missing British people are among 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries missing in China, according to figures released by Chinese authorities, bringing the total of missing Britons between Tibet and Nepal to 48. The Tibet autonomous region’s government said the total missing there also included 104 Nepalis, 49 people from India, 33 from Latvia and 18 from the US.

Thirty-three British people had already been declared missing on the Nepal side of the border. Some were on a pilgrimage at the time of the flood, including Hemangini Jitendra Patel and Hema Sunil Amin, two sisters who were last seen on the Friendship Bridge on the border.

The figure for missing Americans has been disputed by the US state department, which declared on Sunday that at least 85 US citizens were missing. The department’s spokesperson, Tommy Pigott, said getting accurate information from the region had been difficult, “made even more so by the devastation and the remoteness that we see”.

Chinese authorities have said at least 16 people have died on their side of the border. But there are concerns over a possible lack of transparency from the Chinese government, which has prevented footage of the floods from being shared in the countryand may have downplayed the casualties.

Police in Nepal said 794 people had been confirmed to have died there and at least 2,742 injured. Numerous areas remain at risk of fresh flooding and people who have returned to their homes have been told to remain alert and be prepared to evacuate again at short notice.
Rescue efforts have been affected by the threat of landslides and dangerous weather as well as confusion over which side of the border victims had been on when the waters struck.

Chinese state television reported that officials in Beijing, far better resourced than their Nepalese counterparts, had mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated more than 220m yuan (£24m) to support relief efforts.

Equipment and supplies have been airdropped to frontline workers, while Chinese soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing, CCTV said. The Chinese premier, Li Qiang, had already travelled to the region.

Numerous countries have pledged to help Nepal, including the US which has offered $3.6m in humanitarian aid, “including up to three months of emergency food assistance to up to 10,000 flood-affected households”, on top of $500,000 previously pledged, and Australia, which will donate more than $3m in assistance.
Britain has committed £5m to Nepal and sent a rapid deployment team, which arrived in Kathmandu on Saturday.

A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: “We are working around the clock to support British nationals and their families affected by the devastating floods on the Nepal-China border. We are coordinating closely with the Nepali and Chinese authorities and have deployed consular support staff to the region to ensure British nationals can access support.”

articles.title: Gilas in good hands with healthy Kai Sotto, says June Mar Fajardo
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–As June Mar Fajardo walks away from Gilas Pilipinas, he knows he’s leaving the national team in good hands. “I told you guys that Kuya Kai will save us this window,”…

blocks.text: Kai Sotto is hugged by teammate June Mar Fajardo after Gilas Pilipinas’ win over Iran in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines–As June Mar Fajardo walks away from Gilas Pilipinas, he knows he’s leaving the national team in good hands.
“I told you guys that Kuya Kai will save us this window,” Fajardo said after the Philippines scraped past Iran, 68-56, in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers on Sunday night.

Kai Sotto (13 PTS, 16 REB, 3 AST) and the Philippines 🇵🇭 shrug off a slow start against Iran to sweep Window 4 and improve to 4-4 in the Asian Qualifiers 📺#FIBAWC x #StepItUp pic.twitter.com/jmNYXS82vu — FIBA Basketball World Cup 🏆 (@FIBAWC) August 30, 2026
“Let’s just pray that he’s always healthy because he will bring us to glory.”
Fajardo was, of course, referring to Kai Sotto, who spearheaded Gilas’ undefeated campaign in the fourth window of the qualifiers despite the absence of naturalized player Justin Brownlee.

The 24-year-old Sotto recorded 18 points, 14 rebounds and one game-saving block in an 82-81 overtime win over Jordan on Friday before following that up with 13 points, 16 rebounds and three assists against the Iranians. The pair of crucial games marked Sotto’s national team return since November 2024, less than two months before he suffered a torn left ACL during a B.League game.
Behind a fully healthy Sotto, the Philippines rose to 4-4 in Group E and strengthened its bid for a spot in next year’s World Cup in Doha, Qatar.
Sotto said giving his retiring hero a winning exit after a decorated 13-year national team career was a big motivation.

“I’m so lucky and blessed. When I was a kid, I looked up to him—he’s my idol,” said Sotto. “I’m so blessed to be part of his journey in the national team. I just really wanted to win these two games for Kuya June.”

articles.title: Pumping stations fail as flood infrastructure pilfered
articles.summary: Stolen cables, valves and manhole covers are impairing flood control infrastructure in Metro Manila, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon lamented yesterday.

blocks.text: Workers conduct repair works inside the Estero de Sunog Apog Pumping Station in Tondo, Manila on August 18, 2025.
The Philippine STAR / Edd Gumban
MANILA, Philippines — Stolen cables, valves and manhole covers are impairing flood control infrastructure in Metro Manila, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon lamented yesterday.
“Citizens must not steal or vandalize public assets. Stripping one small wire causes catastrophic flooding for thousands of families,” Dizon said.
Personnel of the Philippine Coast Guard have been stationed at the Sunog Apog Pumping Station and other vulnerable drainage facilities across the capital to prevent further sabotage.
At yesterday’s inspection of the Sunog Apog facility in Tondo, Manila, Dizon found that stolen high-voltage cables rendered the pumping station inoperative since Saturday.
Replacement cables were installed, restoring the pumping station’s operation yesterday before dawn.
“We worked tirelessly and spent massive public funds to restore this facility and for several weeks, residents enjoyed zero flooding despite heavy downpours,” Dizon told reporters.
Heavy-duty check valves, crucial for preventing backflow from the swollen Marikina River, were also stolen from the Tumana Pumping Station.
Stolen iron manhole covers along Roxas Boulevard have triggered car accidents.
Perpetrators will be arrested and scrap yards will be inspected, Dizon said.

“Before throwing them in jail, I want to dunk them into floodwaters first so they can feel the suffering our citizens go through just because they chose to strip specialized wiring for copper scrap,” Dizon said.
“I speak with raw frustration because we spent huge public funds and exerted massive effort to restore these facilities, only for thieves to ruin them for a few pesos at a junk shop,” he lamented.

articles.title: Head teacher evacuated 900 children minutes before Nepal floods hit school
articles.summary: Rajendra Dawadi leapt into action after receiving warnings over waters heading towards his school.
articles.byline: Ashok Dahal and Kamal Pariyar, BBC Nepali

blocks.text: At first, many students did not realise how serious the situation was.
Pupil Yunisha Amatya, 16, said she scrambled to safety with her friends just before the flood hit.
"I along with my friends survived by just 10 seconds only," she told the BBC.

"Just before the flood came, we were in the class studying. Teachers had gathered in one place and initially had no idea what had happened. After five minutes teachers came and informed us about the flood and asked us to go home."
She said one student fainted after hearing about the disaster, but many initially underestimated the danger and waited for classmates who were in a maths lesson.
Yunisha and her friends scrambled uphill through an escape route behind the school.

"I could not walk fast, and my friends helped me to climb uphill. We tried our best to be in the safer zones then. We escaped through a narrow ladder from backside of the school. Within no time, the bazaar was swept away in front of my eyes," she says, referring to the local market around the school.

"If there was no grip in my shoes I would have fallen and students and other people were jostling each other to reach the safer area while escaping. The people who choose to escape from another route are apparently swept away."
Students and teachers initially moved a few hundred metres uphill to safety before making their way to a neighbouring village.
With roads cut off and transport disrupted, many remained stranded for two nights before rescue efforts reached them.
The principal and Yunisha, who both live across the river from the school, were eventually airlifted back to their home village.
Meanwhile parents were desperately trying to contact their children and relatives.
Yunisha's mother, Sabina Kumari Shrestha, says she repeatedly tried to call both her daughter and husband, but neither could be reached.
Her husband, Yubaraj Amatya, immediately headed towards the school.
"Soon after the flood news spread, I tried my daughter's number, but she was not reachable, then I was afraid," he said.

"Within a few minutes I rushed toward my daughter's school and Trishuli Bazar was all swept by the flood, then I thought my daughter was no more. I was so horrified, stopped my scooter, there was flooding but I could not think of returning without my daughter."
For nearly an hour, he had no idea whether she was alive and kept calling her without success. Then the phone finally connected and Yunisha answered.
"Finally, my daughter received my call and I couldn't stop myself, broke out... two relatives that were with me also cried and hugged me," he said.
Yunisha appears tearful as she recalls that moment.
"After I had reached the top of the hill, I received a call from my father. He was tearful and I could not speak a word then," she said.
Back home, her family waited anxiously for her return.
"Even my younger daughter couldn't sleep. But I felt so good to see her after three days (Friday), I am so happy and relieved," her mother said.
Yunisha says she is now thinking about what comes next.
"Now I am worried about my further studies," she said.
"If I had to change my school, I would have to miss my old friends and will face difficulties to make new friends. I am sad about my further studies."
Head teacher Dawadi says better warning systems, including sirens and evacuation alerts, could have helped residents respond sooner.
But he believes his decision to act immediately prevented a catastrophe.
"Had I decided to close the school after the period, nothing might be left, only the bell would be ringing at 9:30."

articles.title: Seven killed and 23 missing in boat capsizing off northern Cyprus
articles.summary: A search and rescue operation is under way after a ferry carrying nearly 270 people turns over after leaving port.

blocks.text: Passengers stand on capsized Cyprus ferry ahead of rescue
ByGeorge Wright and Ruth Comerford
At least seven people have died and 23 others are still missing after a passenger boat capsized off northern Cyprus, the head of the Turkish administration there has said.

Ünal Üstel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish republic there, said the ferry had been carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members when it began taking on water after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia.
The ship's captain and seven crew members have been detained as part of an investigation into "how this tragedy occurred", Üstel wrote on social media.
A search and rescue operation to find the passengers still unaccounted for is under way, which Turkish authorities have joined. Turkish media is reporting the death toll has risen to eight.
The privately owned ferry left the left the popular holiday resort of Kyrenia at 12:30 local time (09:30 GMT), local media reported.
Üstel said the boat had been scheduled to travel to Turkey on Saturday, but had been delayed due to poor weather conditions.
He told Turkish media outlet TRT that the boat was hit by two waves before it capsized.
While the captain of the vessel was trying to recover from the first wave, a second wave hit and it began taking on water, he told the outlet.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Rescue boats and helicopter around the sinking catamaran close to the port of Kyrenia

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Rescue boats and helicopter around the sinking catamaran close to the port of Kyrenia
Helicopters and coastguard boats have been dispatched to the scene, while ambulances have been stationed on the beach ready to receive rescued passengers.
Üstel wrote on social media that the "priority right now is human life", adding that security forces, rescue teams and health officials were all on the scene.
He added the disaster will be thoroughly investigated and "even the slightest negligence will be uncovered".
"No one will be spared, regardless of who they are, who is found to be at fault or responsible," Üstel said.
Erhan Arikli, the transport minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), which is only recognised by Turkey, told local media that 100 passengers had been taken to shore.
Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan sent his condolences to Turkish Cypriots and said efforts to reach those who were still missing "continue uninterrupted".

"Immediately after the accident, we launched extensive search-and-rescue operations in co-operation with the authorities of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus," he said at a military ceremony on Sunday.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Several rescue boats have been deployed by the coastguard to rescue passengers

blocks.text: Several rescue boats have been deployed by the coastguard to rescue passengers
The ferry - a high-speed 40m long, 10m wide Filo Jet vessel - sails under the flag of Turkey, according to Marine Traffic.
On Sunday evening, Arikli told TRT the ship had completely sunk.
Filo Denizcilik, the company which operates the capsized passenger boat, said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident".
A hotline has been set up to provide passengers' relatives with information. The nationalities of those who were aboard and the status of the injured are unclear.
Local television has broadcast images of the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its hull.
The TRNC, which is recognised only by Turkey, controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.

blocks.caption: Map of the eastern Mediterranean showing the route of a vessel between northern Cyprus and southern Turkey. A label near Kyrenia on Cyprus's north coast states that the vessel departed at 11:58 on Sunday. Another label near Tasucu on Turkey's southern coast states it was due to arrive at 17:52 lo…

articles.title: ‘The river has taken everything’: people return to remains of their homes in Nepal
articles.summary: Precariousness of living in Devighat by the Trishuli River underlined as waters swell again and residents flee to higher ground

blocks.text: The bodies continue to wash up. But the morgues have already run out of room.

Since the deadly floods coursed through the Himalayan valleys of Nepal and Tibet, the numbers of people killed have continued to rise. The bodies have surfaced in their hundreds and continue to be pulled from the thick, tar-like mud that engulfed everything after the flood waters had receded. By Sunday, the death toll stood at 797 in Nepal and Tibet.

Morgues across Nepal are already overflowing. Authorities say they are overwhelmed with the task of trying to identify the dead, many mangled beyond recognition and turning up miles from home. As places to safely store the victims run out, mass burials have begun in the district of Bharatpur.

DNA samples were taken from each body before it was given a tag and a location number, wrapped in a plastic bag and then placed in a shallow grave. The hope, said the police, was that these bodies will eventually be identified by loved ones through DNA and retrieved for proper funeral rites.

In Chitwan, about 100 miles downstream from the region worst hit by the flash floods and mudslides, more than 250 bodies have washed up along the riverbanks. But they are in such a disfigured state that only nine have been successfully identified. Many will now be buried, at least temporarily, in the forest on the edge of the city.

blocks.caption: Residents try to salvage belongings from their damaged homes

blocks.text: In a bid to speed up the identification exercise, local officials have adopted a macabre approach of simply asking people to go through pictures of the bodies and look for identifying features: a necklace, a wedding ring, a tattoo, a scar. Photos of those recovered have been placed on to PowerPoint slideshows, for relatives to sit patiently through, and have been uploaded to the Nepal police website. Outside the morgue in the capital, Kathmandu, photographs of the dead inside have been posted on the walls.

Yet with more than 3,000 still reported missing in Nepal and Tibet, there are fears that the numbers of dead may still rise exponentially. Many of the worst-hit areas, where entire villages were wiped clean away by the apocalyptic tidal wave of mud, water and debris, are still inaccessible except by army helicopter. Speaking on Sunday, the foreign secretary, Amrit Bahadur Rai, said the government had requested “more than 1,000 freezer units” for safe storage of the dead.

blocks.caption: People searching for their belongings in their mud-damaged home in Devighat.  Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: Even in areas lower down the river valley that were decimated by the floods but have remained accessible by road, search and rescue teams have struggled to retrieve all those killed and buried in the mud. On Sunday afternoon in Devighat, a sacred town on the Trishuli River that was left in ruins by the floods, police search and rescue teams prepared to pull another victim from the muddy ruins of a house. All that was visible through the thick mud was their feet.

“It is very tough work. We have retrieved 10 bodies from here so far, maybe there will be more,” said Amabadutta Bhatta, a police superintendent working as part of search and rescue in the city. “The floods destroyed the first and second storey of most homes here. When we finally clear all the mud, which may be many months, who knows what we might find.”

Those who survived the floods in Devighat have slowly come back to see the remains of their houses, many which were wiped away altogether. Standing next to the carcass of her house, reduced to a few concrete blocks and twisted metal, Usha Nepali, 49, wept for the home where she had raised her four children and then her three grandchildren.

blocks.caption: People in Devighat salvage what possessions they can from their damaged homes.  Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: “I invested everything to build this house, so now I don’t know where to go and what to do,” said Nepali. “Nothing is left except this cloth on my back. I haven’t even been able to change clothes since the floods. How can we rebuild this house? This land is no longer safe but it’s the only land we have. The river has taken everything.”

The precariousness of living next to the Trishuli River was underlined on Sunday as the fast-moving waters again swelled dangerously high and rescuers urged people to get to higher ground quickly. Many in Devighat were packing up the few items they could find in their homes, never to return.
Jamuna Magar, 36, said her husband’s family had been living in Devighat for generations. She had come here when she got married and described it as “such a beautiful place”.

blocks.caption: Many returned to Devighat to pack up their belongings before leaving, never to return.  Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

blocks.text: In the minutes after they got warning of the flood, she had time to grab her gold but nothing else. As she stood by the ruins of her house, clutching the only thing she had been able to retrieve so far – a plastic vat of vegetable cooking oil – she said she did not see how they could ever live in Devighat again.

“We had experienced flooding before, but we never knew a flood like this could come and take our house,” she said. “Everything we owned was on the ground floor of the house and now it’s all lost. Even our refrigerator washed away. I’m too worried about my life, about my children’s lives to stay here any longer.”
She feared it would take “decades before they can rebuild Devighat again”.

articles.title: NASA launches first telescope named after female scientist
articles.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, named after NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, will observe black holes, exoplanets and exploding stars.

image.caption: The Nancy Grace Roman Space telescope blasted off on a rocket from Cape Canaveral, FloridaImage: Joe Skipper/REUTERS

blocks.text: NASA has launched a powerful new telescope designed to explore distant planets, exploding stars and black holes while surveying the universe on an unprecedented scale.

The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, named after one of the first women to hold a senior leadership position at NASA, was launched aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday.
The telescope is expected to reach its destination, approximately 1.6 million kilometers (about one million miles) from Earth, in approximately one month's time.
The mission has a total budget of more than $4 billion (€3.45 billion). The first images are expected back on Earth in early 2027.
What will the Roman telescope do?
Astronomers will use "Roman" to investigate a wide range of cosmic phenomena, including black holes, exoplanets and exploding stars.

"It's going to find thousands of supernovae, tens of thousands of planets, billions of galaxies and tens of billions of stars," said NASA science mission director Nicky Fox. "It's going to be able to do things that we've never been able to do before with its massive field of view."
Roman operates in a similar way to the Hubble Space Telescope, which was launched in 1990 and is now showing signs of age while operating with reduced capabilities.
However, Roman is designed to survey the sky far more quickly and will be capable of completing in just one month observations which would have taken Hubble a century.
Scientists expect Roman to generate more than 500 terabytes of data every year. By way of comparison, Hubble has collected approximately 400 terabytes of data in over three decades in space.
"Roman's vast reach will allow us to find the weird, the rare and the unusual," senior project scientist Julie McEnery said on Saturday. "We'll redefine what it means to find a needle in a haystack."
How the Webb telescope captures breathtaking images
Who was Nancy Grace Roman?

The James Webb Space Telescope, named after former NASA administrator James Webb, was launched in late 2021 to complement Hubble. Webb observes the universe at different wavelengths, complementing the observations that will be made by Hubble and Roman.

Launching nearly a year ahead of schedule and within budget, Roman is NASA's first space telescope to be named after a woman. Nancy Grace Roman served as NASA's first Chief of Astronomy throughout the 1960s and 1970s, and retired NASA scientist Ed Weiler said the honor was long overdue.
"This is very, very fitting," he said. "I think Nancy would be very proud."

articles.title: Russia says it helped to repel Niger attempted coup
articles.summary: Soldiers tried to attack a key military base early on Saturday morning, authorities say, but were thwarted.

blocks.text: The Alliance of Sahel States - composed of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso - said the attempted coup was "a betrayal by a group of soldiers involved in an attempt at destabilisation".
The authorities have not said how many soldiers were involved in the attempted coup, nor how many casualties there were.
Niger's military ruler, Gen Tiani, who was sworn in as its president last year after he deposed its elected leader, has also not publicly addressed the incident.
The nation's state broadcaster showed footage of several alleged mutineers being arrested by the Presidential Guard.
On Sunday, Niger Press Agency reported that commercial activity was returning to normal, with petrol stations, shops and other businesses reopening.
Supporters of the government gathered at a public square in central Niamey in support of the security forces and Tiani's government.
Air Base 101, the military site attacked on Saturday, is part of the Diori Hamani airport complex.
It hosts Nigerien military aircraft and drones, as well as an Alliance of Sahel States counter-terrorism unit. Russian and Italian forces are also based there, according to news agency Reuters.
Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso are all military-ruled countries that have cut ties with Western partners and strengthened their co-operation with Russia.
But jihadist violence remains widespread in all three countries, despite the shift in alliances.
For Niger's government, Saturday's mutiny highlights that the military is dealing not only with an external insurgency, but also signs of discontent within its own ranks.
The airbase where the mutiny began had itself been targeted twice by jihadists this year – once by an Islamic State affiliate and later by an al-Qaeda affiliate.
Nigerien authorities say security forces have increased patrols around key sites in Niamey following the attempted takeover, including the main airport entrance and the presidential pavilion.

articles.title: Want to live in history? N.S.'s oldest wooden home offers 'unique opportunity'
articles.summary: Nova Scotia's oldest documented wooden structure, a 318-year-old National Historic Site in Annapolis Royal, is for sale for $495,000. The de Gannes-Cosby House reflects centuries of French and…

image.caption: The building has been occupied by more than 20 families. Now, owner Alyn How is looking for new homeowners. (Stéphanie Blanchet)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia

Nova Scotia's oldest documented wooden structure, a 318-year-old National Historic Site in Annapolis Royal, is for sale for $495,000. The de Gannes-Cosby House reflects centuries of French and British rule in the region and has been continuously occupied.
The 318-year-old de Gannes-Cosby House in Annapolis Royal is listed for $495,000
· CBC News
· Posted: Aug 30, 2026 12:25 PM EDT | Last Updated: 2 hours ago
Nova Scotia's oldest documented wooden structure, a 318-year-old National Historic Site in Annapolis Royal, is for sale for $495,000.
Located on St. George Street, the de Gannes-Cosby House reflects centuries of French and British rule in the region and has been continuously occupied.
“It's not an easy house to live in. It's difficult to heat and living in a museum is not for everybody,” said Alyn How, who inherited the home and is acting as the real estate agent.
His parents bought the property in 1983, but How says it’s time for someone new to “put their stamp on it.”

items: How this 315-year-old private home in Annapolis Royal became a national historic site

blocks.text: Selling the one-and-a-half-storey house — located at 477 St. George St. — may take time, How said. The property has been on the market for two weeks, drawing early interest but no offers.

“It's not like a condominium in Halifax, it's not like a bungalow in a subdivision,” he said. “It is a unique opportunity and we're going to take our time to make sure that we find the right buyer for it because it is of national significance.”

Between 1605 and 1710, Port-Royal, now known as Annapolis Royal, served as the capital of the French colony of Acadia. As French and British forces fought over the territory, a final British siege captured the capital in 1710.
Today, the house stands as a reminder of nearly 120 years of Acadian settlement. It was originally built for French officer Louis de Gannes de Falaise and funded by King Louis XIV.
After 1727, it housed British officer Alexander Cosby, lieutenant-governor of the fort and town of Annapolis Royal.
“It’s really important for the patrimonial value of the Acadian people,” said André-Carl Vachon, an author and lecturer on Acadian history.
The building retains many of its original structural features, such as post-and-beam framing and wattle-and-daub infill.
Both Vachon and How hope whoever buys the home next will preserve its historic spirit.

articles.title: British woman killed in stabbing at German railway station
articles.summary: A 27-year-old German man was arrested immediately after the incident in Rosenheim, Bavaria.

blocks.text: A British woman has died after being stabbed at a railway station in southern Germany in the early hours of Sunday morning, police have said.

The 31-year-old woman was attacked at the station in Rosenheim, Bavaria, shortly before 01:00 local time (00:00 BST). She was taken to hospital where she died as a result of "severe" injuries, the Bavarian Police said in a statement.
Officers arrested a 27-year-old German man at the scene immediately after the incident. The background and motive for the attack is under investigation, the statement added.
Police have asked anyone who may have witnessed "an argument or physical altercation" at the station late on Saturday or early on Sunday to contact them.
The suspect, from the Fürstenfeldbruck district, will be brought before magistrates later on Sunday, according to German news agency DPA.
It is unclear whether the two knew each other or what the woman was doing in Bavaria, DPA also reported.
Rosenheim is one of the largest cities in Upper Bavaria and is a busy rail hub for passengers travelling to Austrian cities including Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck.
The Rosenheimer Herbstfest - an event similar to the Oktoberfest beer festival - is currently taking place in the area.
Responding to the attack, Rosenheim Mayor Abuzar Erdogan said "there are no indications of a security threat in our city or of any link to our Herbstfest".

"The criminal investigation department is working closely with the public prosecutor's office to investigate the circumstances and motive behind the crime as a matter of urgency," he wrote in a statement.
A Foreign Office spokesperson told the BBC: "We are supporting the family of a British woman who died in Germany [and] are in touch with the local authorities."

articles.title: On the road with pro-independence Albertans, one small town at a time

image.caption: Chris Scott is with the group Let’s Talk Alberta. Last week, they toured around southern Alberta, handing out lawn signs and talking to residents about independence. (Mantai Chow/CBC)

blocks.text: We hit the road with separatists as they meet supporters in rural Alberta
Chris Scott sat in the driver’s seat of his 2001 Monaco Dynasty motorhome last week, bumping along the network of rural highways in southern Alberta.
The vehicle creaked a bit. Some leather-covered furniture was cracking, and some cabinet drawer latches didn’t work anymore.
It’s like Alberta, Scott said: you can ignore problems and let them get worse, or you can pay attention to them and fix them.
“I see there's a lot of things going on with Alberta that need some care and attention,” said Scott.

The restaurant owner, who gained prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic, has hit the road this summer to talk independence, travelling with a group of people who also support the idea of Alberta becoming its own nation.
CBC News recently spent a day aboard the “Let’s Talk Alberta” bus, speaking with passengers about what motivates them at a time when Albertans are weighing their vote in an Oct. 19 referendum.

Earlier this summer, CBC spent time with volunteers helping the pro-Canada group Forever Canadian, talking to them about their efforts and why they wouldn’t be voting to have a future referendum on whether Alberta should stay in the country.

Federalist and separatist groups have been a common sight this summer, fundraising and shaking hands with voters at events like the Calgary Stampede. Voter mobilization efforts are expected to ramp up considerably with less than two months to go to the referendum.
On the bus
On a recent weekday in August, Scott’s bus hit the road for a 10-stop tour through the southern part of the province.
Scott’s passengers included Jasper Smit, a friend from the Netherlands who runs a social media channel called CommonSense TV.
Leaning on a countertop in the back of the motorhome, Smit studied the packaging of a snack purchased from a highway gas station. He read it aloud: roasted grilled pepperoni cheesesteak.
“Mystery meat!” called out another rider.
The wrapping on the bus’ exterior was less ambiguous.

The vehicle is emblazoned with the “Let’s Talk Alberta” decal, framed by provincial viewscapes: the hoodoos of Drumheller flowing into sweeping mountains and rivers, topped by an expansive prairie sky. It was an Alberta postcard, designed with artificial intelligence and then smoothed out by a designer.

On the back of the vehicle, a Bible verse printed in script: Jeremiah 29:7 — "Seek the peace and prosperity of the city to which I have carried you into exile. Pray to the Lord for it, because if it prospers, you too will prosper."
It was Scott who procured the motorhome to criss-cross the province.
With a full standup shower and decent-sized bed in the back, Scott could spend days on the bus if he needed to.
Increasingly, he has been, as he’s travelled to all corners of the province with the clock running down to voting day.
He carries with him his experiences from the pandemic.
He was charged and later acquitted for breaching public health restrictions during COVID-19 related to his Whistle Stop Cafe in east-central Alberta.

Scott was highly critical of politicians that he viewed as allowing laws that "strip our fundamental rights and freedoms away." His reputation has made him something of a folk hero amongst those who share his views in these small towns.
“I just learned that if there's something that's wrong, you need to stand up for yourself,” Scott said of his experience.
When the bus pulls into a town, it’s often greeted with supporters. Some caught word of the trip on social media.
In Rosemary, Alta., with a population of little more than 350, a lone man who came out to get a lawn sign said he heard news of the trip on a Facebook group entitled, “Bassano Bitching or Bragging.”
“The whole thing is really not about separation, in my opinion,” said Bassano resident Tom Schaffer.
“It's about making the government wake up and go, hey, these guys might want to separate. Maybe we should actually do something and listen to them?”

Tanya Clemens, co-leader of a separate Alberta independence group, Let Alberta Decide, was on the bus too, as was John Bolton, a former Calgary radio host who now provides emcee services at various independence events, and Patti Vold, a mother of nine and a grandmother of 15.

There was also Sandy Duguay, who was born and raised in Montreal, where she lived through two referendums as an English speaker. Duguay also spent 26 years in Victoria, where her husband was a chaplain at a prison on Vancouver Island.

Duguay was never involved in politics before, but was motivated to become political after the COVID-19 pandemic hit, which evolved into helping the Alberta independence signature drive. She’s now travelling full-time on the bus.
“I feel very close to these people,” Duguay said, who turns 72 in a few weeks.

As the bus weaved its way along the route, the conversation snaked through the group’s motivating complaints with the federal government. Some, like frustration with the federal equalization program or Ottawa’s approach to firearms, have been kindling for alienation for years.
The cultural divide at play quickly came into focus, too. Certain federal bills, perhaps less familiar to the broader Canadian public, are viewed by this group as threats to religious freedom.

“Bill C-9 especially,” Duguay said, referring to the Combatting Hate Act, which amends the Criminal Code to strengthen penalties for hate crimes. The Liberals received support from the Bloc Québécois after including a clause to remove a religious exemption from the country's hate speech laws.

items: Contentious anti-hate legislation passes final vote in the House, now moves to Senate

blocks.text: The Conservatives have argued that amounts to an “assault” on religious freedoms, while Justice Minister Sean Fraser has said the new law won’t “criminalize faith.”
“Look what’s happened to Europe,” Duguay said, turning to Smit. “You were founded on Judeo-Christian principles. And you guys were the first to get rid of them."

Wearing a Let’s Talk Alberta shirt and a Whistle Stop hat, Smit, the visitor from the Netherlands, didn’t entirely agree. He said he's “not religious at all" and that embedding Christian principles into governance would set a precedent that would require adopting other religious laws whenever demographics shifted in the future.
“In all fairness, you should bring that [into] politics,” he said.
Vold, the grandmother of 15, feels Christian values have been fading from public life, which is pushing society towards moral decline.

“For many, many years, the idea was you shouldn't mix church and state, right? I disagree,” Vold said. “The state should not be in the church, but people of faith should be in the state. They should be helping to guide the country.”
Soon after this conversation, the bus arrived in Strathmore and pulled near Kinsmen Park. Scott and Smit exited. Talk of faith continued, until suddenly, Smit ran back up the bus stairs.
“The police are here.”
A heated confrontation
Outside the bus, a crowd had formed in the parking lot.

Various supporters of the independence movement who had arrived to greet the bus gathered around Scott as he was engaged in an argument. On the other side was a town official, flanked by a peace officer.
“So anyway, we'll be here for about an hour,” Scott said.
“I’m asking you to leave,” the official responded. The group was free to express its opinions, the man said, but not on the town’s property.
“But I can,” Scott responded. “It’s public property.”
The crowd grew increasingly frustrated. Scott was told that if he did not move the vehicle, the RCMP would be called.
“Well, I mean, it’s not the first time I’ve been arrested,” Scott said.
Minutes passed. Separatist influencers began to livestream from the scene. Eventually, word came that the bus was allowed to stay.

“The town respects individuals' right to peacefully express their views and participate in democratic processes,” a town spokesperson later said in an email to CBC News. “The group was able to continue gathering and expressing its views.”
The bus moved on to an Airdrie pizza place that’s become a gathering spot for the separatist movement.

Behind schedule and with three stops still to go, the Let’s Talk Alberta crew sat down and scarfed down slices, with a Toronto Blue Jays game playing on the screens above and curious onlookers surrounding the crowd of blue shirts.
One man asked what the group was doing there.
“It’s an Alberta independence bus tour,” he was told.
The man grimaced.
Polling suggests that support for independence is stronger in the rural regions, and Let’s Talk Alberta’s tour last week to smaller locales was largely met by receptive crowds.
But to win in October, the group understands it needs to make gains in the cities, where it hasn't received as friendly a welcome as it has in rural Alberta. That’s where they're headed next.
“September, October will be all cities,” Duguay said. “The cities, different cultures, different mindsets … we’ve covered just about every little town. But now, the cities.”

articles.title: Go eyes funding for school counselors
articles.summary: Sen. Bong Go said he will closely scrutinize the government’s education budget to ensure that adequate funding is provided for school counselors and mental health personnel, as new Department…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Bong Go said he will closely scrutinize the government’s education budget to ensure that adequate funding is provided for school counselors and mental health personnel, as new Department of Education (DepEd) data showed that fewer than 1,000 registered guidance counselors are serving more than 45,000 schools nationwide.

The senator, who chairs the Senate committees on youth and sports, said the shortage deserves particular attention during congressional deliberations on the national budget, especially amid recent incidents of school violence, bullying and other concerns affecting the well-being of Filipino learners.
Go said the government must make sure these created positions are actually funded, filled, deployed and sustained so students can access mental health and psychosocial support when they need it.
“Mental health issue is real. This is real,” Go stressed during the Senate hearing on the recent school shooting in Zamboanga City.

DepEd Undersecretary Willie Cabral disclosed that while around 5,000 registered guidance counselors were recorded nationwide as of Jan. 31, fewer than 1,000 were actually serving under the agency. These personnel have to respond to the needs of learners spread across more than 45,000 schools.

The department had created around 5,000 guidance counselor positions in 2020, but only about 1,000 of these were eventually filled, underscoring the difficulty of translating authorized positions into personnel actually working in schools.

articles.title: Palace defends Marcos singing at First Lady's birthday
articles.summary: President Marcos has drawn flak over online videos showing him singing during the birthday celebration of First Lady Liza Marcos while some areas were inundated by floods caused by the southwest…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos meet the Filipino community in Melbourne, Australia on March 4, 2024.
PPA pool photos by Noel Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has drawn flak over online videos showing him singing during the birthday celebration of First Lady Liza Marcos while some areas were inundated by floods caused by the southwest monsoon.
A backdrop of the stage where Marcos delivered song numbers showed that the event took place on Aug. 26 and carried the theme “Liza and the Chocolate Factory.”
The First Lady turned 67 on Aug. 21.
Palace press officer Claire Castro, however, said the government’s operations did not stop even if the President spent some time with his family.

“The President is the President wherever he is. His spending of some time with his family did not mean that the performance of his mandate or the operations of the government stopped,” Castro said in a text message.

In one of the videos, the President was seen belting out “You,” a ballad popularized by Filipino music icon Basil Valdez. In another video, Marcos was shown singing “And I Love Her” by British pop band The Beatles.
The videos were posted online by Vigan City Mayor Jose Singson Jr. on Aug. 28 and have since been reposted by various news organizations and social media users.

Marcos’ critics have accused him of being insensitive, saying he was partying while people in flooded areas were suffering. Some social media users have also questioned the President’s quality of leadership, claiming he was out of touch with the experiences of ordinary Filipinos, especially those in flood-hit areas.
Castro also responded to former presidential spokesman Harry Roque’s statement that the President was having a concert while Pampanga and Bulacan were submerged in floods.

“Let us not forget that the President prioritized the site visits and inspections in Pampanga and Bulacan to improve the plight of our countrymen and to deliver assistance to the affected. Members of the media witnessed this last Monday,” she said.

“The little time and one night the President spent with his wife, his family and other people close to him to thank God for the gift of life given to his spouse does not mean he abandoned his obligation to the nation. It did not happen during the height of the cyclone last Friday or Saturday,” she said.
Castro reiterated that the President remains focused and has asked agencies to act swiftly on the effect of the monsoon rains.
“In conditions like this, he chose to remain in the Philippines to continue his monitoring,” the Palace press officer added.
About eight million people in 10 regions have been affected by the enhanced southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng, according to latest government data.

articles.title: DPWH, PRA halt reclamation in Taguig
articles.summary: The Department of Public Works and Highways and the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) have issued a cease-and-desist order against an unauthorized reclamation project along the Taguig…

blocks.text: Department of Public Works and Highways.
Businessworld / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Public Works and Highways and the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) have issued a cease-and-desist order against an unauthorized reclamation project along the Taguig waterfront, DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said yesterday.

Speaking during a field inspection in Marikina, Dizon confirmed that the formal order was executed following explicit directives from the Office of the President to halt illegal earth-filling and coastal development activities along Laguna de Bay.
Dizon said the order was served on Aug. 20 and took effect immediately.

The PRA, an attached agency under the Office of the President, oversees all reclamation civil works nationwide. Unsanctioned projects have come under intense scrutiny from public works and environmental officials for disrupting natural drainage channels and compounding severe monsoon flooding across Metro Manila and surrounding river basins.
Dizon said that multi-agency coordination meetings have been convened to resolve jurisdiction, environmental impact and legal violations surrounding the project.

“A meeting has been called with key stakeholders, including the city government of Taguig, the Laguna Lake Development Authority and the Pasig River Urban Development Project,” he said. “We will discuss the issues and determine the way forward, but all reclamation activities are ordered stopped effective immediately.”

The DPWH chief emphasized that the government will strictly enforce coastal and riverbank regulations to ensure development projects do not compromise Metro Manila’s overall flood control master plan.

articles.title: Tour for Asean leaders’ spouses set
articles.summary: Filipino traditional arts, fashion, entertainment and food are expected to gain the spotlight during the tour of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) leaders’ spouses at the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Filipino traditional arts, fashion, entertainment and food are expected to gain the spotlight during the tour of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) leaders’ spouses at the Likhang Filipino in Pasay City this November.
First Lady Liza Marcos provided details of the tour after a meeting with the National Organizing Council (NOC) and representatives of ASEAN countries last Aug. 28.

“Productive briefing with the NOC and the other ASEAN country representatives during their walk through for the upcoming Spouses’ Tour at Likhang Filipino,” the First Lady posted on Facebook yesterday.
“Thrilled to hear their positive feedback on our detailed preparations – and even more excited to welcome our ASEAN First Ladies this November!”
The planned activities include the witnessing of a float parade with marching bands, the performance of folk dances from Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao and a fashion show.

articles.title: Germany's Christian Churches take a stand against far right
articles.summary: The AfD in Saxony-Anhalt has embarked on a confrontational course toward the churches. Representatives of the Catholic and Protestant churches are responding with a mix of anxiety and resolve.

image.caption: Saxony-Anhalt's churches have been reminding voters of their Christian values ahead of the state election on September 6Image: Christoph Strack/DW

blocks.text: Flags flutter in the wind outside Magdeburg's Catholic cathedral. "Love thy neighbor, dialogue, human dignity, solidarity. VOTE CONSCIOUSLY!", they proclaim. Just a few minutes' walk away, a sign on the building of the Protestant Cathedral Congregation reads: "DIVERSITY IS DIVINE." Other Protestant churches across the region display banners reading "Heart Instead of Hate."

For many months now, warnings about the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which is particularly strong in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, have been part of everyday church life. During a sermon at a pilgrimage event in September 2025, Magdeburg Bishop Gerhard Feige remarked almost in passing that pilgrims of hope do not cast their votes on a whim, "into the blue." He was interrupted by prolonged applause — blue is the AfD's party color.

The AfD holds a commanding lead in the polls ahead of the state election on September 6. The prospect of a government led by the party alone appears increasingly plausible. At the same time, Germany's domestic intelligence agency has classified the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt branch as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" organization.
What if Germany's far-right AfD party wins in Saxony-Anhalt?
Churches speak out against AfD
In Saxony-Anhalt, 10% of the population is Protestant and 3% is Catholic; only a few thousand people belong to the Muslim or Jewish faiths.

More than 85% of the state's 2.1 million residents have no religious affiliation, compared with a national average of 47%. Nevertheless, the churches play an important role as defenders of democracy — and that, apparently, is precisely what troubles the AfD.

With its so-called government program, adopted at a state party conference in April, the party launched a broadside against both the Protestant and Catholic churches. The program calls for an end to all state payments to the two churches and for the abolition of church tax collection by public authorities, a service for which the churches themselves pay.

blocks.caption: Bishop Gerhard Feige has said he could never have imagined that so many people could once again be so easily led astray by the far rightImage: Peter Gercke/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: In cases of so-called church asylum, where refugees seek shelter on church premises for fear of renewed persecution in their countries of origin, the AfD is calling for churches to be held financially accountable on a "permanent" basis.

The Protestant Academy of Saxony-Anhalt should also no longer receive any state funding whatsoever. The reason, according to the AfD, is its "political agitation in line with the established parties: climate dogma, gender ideology, and the rainbow cult." The academy is said to advocate "unchecked mass immigration." Yet in scarcely any German federal state is the proportion of foreign nationals as low as it is in Saxony-Anhalt.
From estrangement to open confrontation

The sharpness of the criticism goes far beyond anything typically heard from other regional branches of the Alternative for Germany or from the party's national leadership. Long gone are the days when representatives of the then-emerging party complained about not being invited to church congresses or Catholic conventions.

In February 2024, the plenary assembly of the German Catholic Bishops' Conference unanimously adopted a declaration entitled "Ethnic Nationalism and Christianity are Incompatible." In it, the bishops identified an ethnonationalist mindset within the AfD and spoke of a "genuine right-wing extremism." The document was prompted by the state elections scheduled to take place later that year in the eastern German states of Thuringia, Saxony, and Brandenburg. Now, in September 2026, elections are due to follow in Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin.
At present, the confrontation between the AfD and the churches is nowhere more intense than in Saxony-Anhalt.
Germany's churches get creative about new ways to worship

For Bishop Feige, the AfD's current direction is "without question" an expression of ethnonationalism. "Until now, Saxony-Anhalt's motto has been 'Thinking Modern'. The AfD wants to replace it with 'Thinking German'," he told DW. "The AfD's election posters speak a very clear language: 'Save your country', 'Take your country back', 'Deport from day one!' What else could that be but ethnonationalism?"

The 74-year-old said he "could never have imagined that so many people today could once again be so easily led astray, or that arsonists, pied pipers and respectable-looking agitators could emerge, and that so many would fall for them."

As an example, Feige cited the so-called flag assembly that the AfD wants to reintroduce in the state's schools: the raising of the flag and the singing of the national anthem. "This existed during the Nazi era and was later adopted by the GDR," he said, referring to the former East Germany. "And now it is supposed to return? I find that inconceivable."

blocks.caption: Bishop Friedrich Kramer said Christian messages should not be interpreted as an endorsement of any particular political partyImage: Martin Schutt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Both major Christian churches emphasize they are speaking out not against a particular party, but in defense of a Christian view of humanity. Whether the issue is climate protection and the safeguarding of creation or the treatment of strangers, the churches' interventions are "primarily not political messages, but Christian ones, and should not be interpreted as an endorsement of any particular political party," Friedrich Kramer, bishop of the Protestant Church in central Germany, recently told the online magazine Die Eule.
Religious freedom, according to the AfD

Jews and Jewish life, incidentally, are never mentioned in the government program. By contrast, Islam appears repeatedly. According to the AfD, it will "restore religious freedom to appropriate limits." Islam is described as a "religion alien to our culture." Freedom of religion, the party argues, does not oblige Germans to "fulfill every demand of the Islamic lobby."

Representatives of the state's Jewish association, which includes the synagogue of the Jewish community of Halle targeted in a 2019 right-wing extremist attack, as well as representatives of the largest mosque congregation in the state, declined to comment when asked.

Notably, the AfD's platform speaks of a "Christian mission" that, in its view, the churches supported by church tax, which it labels the "church-tax churches," no longer fulfill. This evokes the support that US President Donald Trump receives from influential evangelical and conservative Christian groups in the United States. In Saxony-Anhalt, however, there is only a limited presence of comparable religious milieus.
Threat from the far right: Never quite German enough?
Why bishops are sounding the alarm

"A government involving the AfD would have devastating consequences," Kramer said. That is why, he added, cultural institutions and civil society organizations are joining forces to warn against the AfD.

His Catholic counterpart, Feige, likewise cautioned against "downplaying" the prospect of an AfD-led government. During the election campaign, he said, the party is presenting itself "with messianic ideas" and promoting slogans such as "Everything will be fine" or "Anything is possible."

Because the AfD's lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, "comes across as highly polished and enthusiastic," some people ask what could possibly be "right-wing extremist or dangerous" about him. "But behind him stand forces that give cause for concern," said Feige. "If an AfD single-party government comes to power here, it will be a pilot project. Then Saxony-Anhalt will become a gateway to national politics."
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Cone savors 'sweet' Gilas win over Iran, home sweep
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–Coach Tim Cone considers himself the “happiest guy in the world” after Gilas Pilipinas completed a fourth window sweep of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers with Sunday’s 68-56…

blocks.text: Gilas Pilipinas coach Tim Cone during a game against Iran in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers at Mall of Asia Arena.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net

MANILA, Philippines–Coach Tim Cone considers himself the “happiest guy in the world” after Gilas Pilipinas completed a fourth window sweep of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers with Sunday’s 68-56 win over Iran.
Gilas improved to an even 4-4 win-loss slate before a home crowd at Mall of Asia Arena, trimming the gap with Iran, and also Jordan after the two teams fell to 5-3 to close out the window winless.
The Philippines defeated Jordan, 82-81, in overtime last Friday.

Cone also took notice of the circumstances behind Gilas’ win, as it beat Iran for the first time in a Fiba competition since the 2015 Asian Championship in Changsha, China, while also playing with an all-Filipino lineup following the absence of naturalized player Justin Brownlee.
“It makes it really sweet to come out and win this game,” said Cone.
But Gilas had to go the wringer for the second straight game after missing 11 of 13 shots in the first quarter to trail 18-7.
Big contributions from Kai Sotto, Juan Gomez de Liano, plus a morale-boosting appearance from the retiring June Mar Fajardo enabled Gilas to fight back and turn the contest into a seesaw affair.
It wasn’t until the fourth quarter that Ramos made crucial shots, even as the rest of Gilas was able to tighten things up to see off the Iranian side.

“It was one of those slow starts that we have, but the guys kept fighting and fighting and getting back into the game,” Cone said. “At halftime, we felt good about ourselves, and we felt we could pull this one out.
“But it’s just a great character performance by these guys, in both games,” he added.

articles.title: Jason Arday accuser given three-month teaching ban but can continue research
articles.summary:
Nathan Cofnas allowed to resume Ghent University work, as US ambassador claims credit for lifting of suspension

Prof Jason Arday’s accuser Nathan Cofnas has been barred from teaching on…

blocks.text: Prof Jason Arday’s accuser Nathan Cofnas has been barred from teaching on Ghent University campus for three months but has been allowed to continue his research position.
Earlier this month Cofnas, an American academic, was suspended from his postdoctoral research position at the Belgian institution pending a “preliminary investigation” launched after Arday’s death.

Ghent did not name Cofnas but has since confirmed it has “imposed a disciplinary measure” on a staff member for three months, under which they were “required to work remotely and may not carry out any teaching”. Cofnas’s research activities in the role have been “strictly limited to the research topics for which the appointment was made”.
In a post on X, Cofnas said he was grateful to Ghent’s rector, Petra De Sutter, “for allowing me to stay”.

The US ambassador to Belgium, Bill White, who had criticised Cofnas’s suspension, claimed on his official X account that the university and Cofnas had “amicably reached an agreement” to lift the suspension, enabling the academic to complete his one-year appointment.

In a statement, Ghent said an inquiry was under way “to determine if further disciplinary action is warranted”. The university later confirmed it had been in contact with the US ambassador, who “provided further context regarding his statements on X”.

Cofnas’s role at Ghent has been mired in controversy. In May, Ghent’s philosophy department alleged to university leaders that Cofnas had “very limited expertise” for his role researching “the future of liberalism”, alleging he had a “far-right agenda”.

In July Cofnas accused Arday, a Cambridge sociologist, of plagiarism, alleging there were “serious questions” about his biographical claims. Arday was found dead on 14 August. His family paid tribute to him as an “amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son”.

blocks.caption: Jason Arday was found dead on 14 August. He was accused of plagiarism by Cofnas.  Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian

blocks.text: White, a Donald Trump supporter, donor and fundraiser, had called Cofnas’s suspension “truly unacceptable”, calling for De Sutter to immediately rescind it earlier this month.

On Friday, White wrote on his personal X account: “I just saved Belgium from a complete global media meltdown and well deserved spanking by @elonmusk and everyone by resolving the UGHENT Cofnas matter – quite quickly.”

The night before, Cofnas thanked White and the US state department for “defending American values” on X, adding: “It was beyond my imagination that such a person would take an interest in the fate of a postdoc. The Ambassador responded with great support which helped to bring about a just outcome.”

“Anti-woke” Cofnas has been accused of promoting pseudoscientific ideas of racial difference in his online writings, and was reportedly among bloggers recommended to the Palantir founder, Peter Thiel, by a “race science” researcher.
Cofnas has also hit out at Trump and Maga in his writing, while claiming the US president’s executive orders against diversity, equity and inclusion in the US were a “cause for celebration”.
In a piece in April last year he said the Republican party had “degenerated into a low-IQ cult of personality”.

Hitting out at Trump’s tariffs, he said the effect “will be to halt the American economic juggernaut, discredit the anti-woke movement, pave the way for a leftwing populist … (and) stop the right’s momentum in other countries”.

In October, he wrote: “The right simply does not have the human capital to retake the institutions and run them effectively. The vast majority of intelligent, psychologically stable, and public-spirited Americans remain left and woke. The Trump administration’s war on universities, science, and data has only reinforced smart people’s identity as leftists.”

Asked by the Guardian if he stood by previous criticisms of Trump and Maga, Cofnas said: “I voted for Trump three times and I am still a registered Republican. I strongly criticised some Maga policies, particularly tariffs. There are other Maga policies that I support, such as interventions on behalf of free speech.”

Ghent University said it did “not wish to comment further on the controversy surrounding this matter … ongoing preliminary disciplinary inquiries must be allowed to proceed calmly, independently and with full respect for the rights of all those involved”.

articles.title: June Mar Fajardo sparks Gilas Pilipinas win in his 'last game'
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines–June Mar Fajardo officially confirmed his retirement from Gilas Pilipinas duties following Sunday’s 68-56 win over Iran in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers…

blocks.text: June Mar Fajardo holds up the game ball as he says goodbye to the crowd after playing his final game for Gilas Pilipinas–a 68-56 win over Iran in the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers–on Sunday at Mall of Asia Arena.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net

MANILA, Philippines–June Mar Fajardo officially confirmed his retirement from Gilas Pilipinas duties following Sunday’s 68-56 win over Iran in the fourth window of the Fiba World Cup Asian Qualifiers at Mall of Asia Arena.
And Fajardo made sure that he won’t go off into the sunset without having a hand in the victory that enabled Gilas to close in on the race for spots in next year’s World Cup in Doha, Qatar.
Fajardo had six points and two rebounds in seven minutes, but it was during the second quarter when he helped spark Gilas’ fightback from a lethargic first quarter.

THANK YOU, JMF 🥹 June Mar Fajardo receives “MVP” chants in what might be his last game for Gilas Pilipinas. @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/i3vouiDwFX — Rommel Fuertes Jr. (@MeloFuertesINQ) August 30, 2026

“Siyempre kung ano yung pwede kung maitulong, ibibigay ko kasi gusto ko i-cherish yung last game ko (Of course, I wanted to give whatever I can to help because I want to cherish my last game),” Fajardo said.
A jump hook over Arman Zangeneh with 2:39 left that cut the deficit to 29-25 brought big cheers from the crowd, and the basket seemed to have galvanized Gilas.
Coach Tim Cone later said that the play was a morale-booster for the home side, which would go into the half up 36-34 after trailing 18-5 in the opening period.

Gilas would eventually get the job done behind Kai Sotto, Juan Gomez de Liano, Dwight Ramos and AJ Edu, allowing Fajardo to get a fitting curtain call with chants of “MVP” and receive the game ball from his teammates.

‘LAST GAME NA. LAST GAME NA TALAGA’ 👏 After 13 years of representing the Philippines with Gilas, June Mar Fajardo officially calls it a career. @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/tCPss9VjKy — Rommel Fuertes Jr. (@MeloFuertesINQ) August 30, 2026
The swan song was actually his 70th game in all Fiba competitions across 13 years that started at the same venue in the 2013 Fiba Asia Championship.
And with that, Fajardo’s national team career has come full circle.
“Last game, last game na talaga (it’s really my last game),” said the 36-year-old Fajardo.
